description.source: What will you say to the American people as you accept your party's nomination for President?
Which of these themes will you emphasize the most as you campaign for President this year?
Your closest rival for the nomination, Bernie Sanders, will be meeting with you to discuss your policy objectives. What tone are you looking to strike with him?
An outbreak of COVID-19 has led to a wave of stay-at-home orders and business closures. How will you campaign over  the next few months?
Do you plan to make Trump's 2019 impeachment a focus of your campaign? And if so, how much?

Trump's 2019 impeachment trial was closely tied the role your son, Hunter, took with a Ukranian energy company called Burisma. Was his appointment appropriate, given your son's background and skill set?
What do you have to say about the selection of Elizabeth Warren as your running mate? What makes her the best choice?
What are your thoughts on the death of George Floyd and the wave of protests in the wake of his death? Will you make an appearance at a Black Lives Matter event?
After the tumuluous events of this summer, many in your party are upset that you did not choose an African-American running mate. What can you say to address thiis?
To what extent do you support emergency economic legislation to address the effects of COVID-19 on society?
What is your opinion on the expansion of mail-in voting and early voting in this election? Do you have any concerns?
As President, would you consider implementing policies such as a national lockdown or a mask mandate to control COVID-19?
What is your position on the need for a federal infrasctructure bill? How large should any package be?
Do you support the plans of some in your party to expand the size of the Supreme Court, in order to counteract the Republicans' actions in regard to Merrick Garland and Amy Coney Barret?
With the tragic passing of Ruth Bader-Ginsburg, it appears that Republicans are poised to place another conservative judge on the Supreme Court. What are your thoughts on their tactics?
Are you open to attending the customary three debates with your opponent, Mr. Trump?
What is your reaction to the news that President Trump has contracted COVID-19 and been hospitalized?
There has been an increase in Asian-American hate crimes in 2020, along with the rise of COVID and the inflammatory statements of Trump. What do you think about this?
Recent articles have discussed Donald Trump paying no federal income taxes in some previous years, or having a secret Chinese bank account. Is this something you want to emphasize?
To what extent will you undo the draconian immigration and asylum policies that have been enacted under Trump?
What are your views about the relationship wih China? Has Trump been too antagonistic on the trade issue?
Which gun control measures do you favor? Which ones do you oppose?
President Trump has repeatedly dodged the question when asked whether he will accept the results of this year's election. Do you have any statements to make?
Right-wing websites have been circulating a story about a laptop that your son, Hunter, purportedly lost. Do you have any comment?
Where do you want to concentrate your attention on during the final day of the campaign?
We should put our focus into Georgia and North Carolina.
This election is a battle for the soul of America. If Donald Trump is President for four more years, the damage to this nation may be irreversible.
We're going to build back better than ever before. I'm going to work for every American, repairing our critical infrastructure at home and our standing in the world.
I will be a President for all Americans. Black, brown, Latino, gay, straight, Christian, Jewish, Muslim, rich, poor, or middle-class. I'm a uniter, not a divider.
We have a President who turns his back on science, decency, and truth itself. A President who spends more time watching Fox News than he does doing his job. We need an adult in the White House.
We're going to defeat COVID and get America working again. I'm going to push for this day and night from the moment I step into the White House.
We need to build a country where all citizens are equal before the law and before their fellow man. We need to make sure people from all walks of life get the help they need to succeed.
I'm the trusted, steady leader that we need in a time of national crisis. I worked in the White House, actually worked, for eight years next to my great friend Barack Obama.

Donald Trump has assaulted our most vulnerable citizens, given away billions in tax breaks to the top 1 percent, alienated our allies, and utterly failed to address the COVID and policing crises. He must go.
I'm going to listen to our medical experts and stay at home to stop the spread. There are plenty of ways to get the message out on TV and in social media now. We're all in this together.
For the most part, I'm going to campaign from home until things settle down. But I do want to make a couple of public speeches (to limited crowds) on our most important issues.
I should be out there talking to the American people. That doesn't mean we do rallies with 10 thousand people, but we can't afford to just sit around in our basement for the next five months.
I'm prepared to give Senator Sanders some significant input into our platform and our campaign. He ran a very good race and said a lot that resonated with the American people.

It's very important for our party to remain united and to put up a unified front against Donald Trump. And that's a two-way street, I'm sure we can both find some common ground and make a good show of unity.
We appreciate Senator Sanders and his support. But it's important to note that I won the nomination by a lot. I will be cordial but make few promises.
Who authorized this meeting? Did I authorize this meeting? We're telling Bernie Sanders that he'd better fall in line. We have an election to win.
The real crime here is what Donald Trump was doing, and we saw that with the impeachment proceedings. He shouldn't even be the President right now.
There's absolutely no evidence that Hunter Biden did anything inappropriate in this case, the other side is putting forward debunked conspiracy theories to the contrary.

I'm proud of my son. He's overcome a lot to find success in life. This campaign is about the American people and their struggles and opportunities. I'm not going to spend my time talking about Trump and Ukrainie.
Hunter Biden is my son, but in this case his judgment was a little off. I'm prepared to fully apologize for any mixed signals this created.
Donald Trump flagrantly broke the law and he shouldn't be the President right now. Of course I'm going to bring that up.
I'm not going to spend the 2020 campaign focusing on 2019 issues. We need to talk about our plans to fight this COVID-19 epidemic and rebuild the economy.
We might have our political differences, but I can't say whether I think this impeachment trial was justified or not. It's really a pretty gray area when you get down to it.
I'm proud to stand with Black Lives Matter in the wake of this incident. We need to fight the root causes of black poverty, defund the police, and fight for equity in our society and government.

This looks like an appalling misuse of police force, and incidents like this are the reason Black Lives Matter exists. I'm proud to do my small part to support the peaceful protests happening right now.

Being a police officer is one of the hardest jobs there is, but they got it very wrong here. I have every confidence that Hennepin County will take the appropriate action against the officers involved in this case.
This case is no excuse for the rioting and disorder that we're seeing in many large cities, which in no way honors George Floyd. I condemn this situation unequivocally.
We need to put $2000 in the hands of every American, and we need to put forward a truly substantial relief package for our struggling small businesses and job creators.
We need to extend and expand unemployment insurance. We need a second round of stimulus payments like we had the first time. The economists are clear on this.

If you look at what's happening right now with Trump and Mitch McConnell, they're holding up important legislation here. Hopefully everyone will come to their senses and it won't be an issue by next year.
I'm going to be taking a hard look at the economic conditions from my first day in office, and recommending the appropriate action from there.
One hundred percent. If we don't see the level of deaths and cases go down in this country, then we need to do whatever it takes to bring those into line.
If everyone would just wear a mask, the rate of transmission would drop by a lot, and we could all together beat this pandemic.

This shouldn't be a political decision that the President makes, it should be based on the science. The CDC is not recommending anything like a national lockdown right now, and I'm going to respect their expertise.

We're not going to have a national lockdown. That's just fear-mongering from the Republicans to distract from how they've mishandled the pandemic. This is something each locality can decide for themselves, based on local conditions.

I'm proposing a pretty big bill, you might have noticed, around $2 trillion to rebuild our roads, develop mass transit and green energy, and repair critical human infrastructure needs as well. We must move forward as a country.

We're going to propose an infrastructure bill pretty soon after my inauguration, and it's going to be $500 billion or more. We're going to put people to work rebuilding our roads, bridges, ports, and power grid for the 21st century.

One of the first things we're going to do when I'm President is to make a full assessment of the nation's infrastructure and where we need to improve. And once we have that, then I can help us pass an informed and targeted infrastructure bill that addresses real priorities.
We need to worry about beating the COVID-19 pandemic and protecting the right of every American to have their voice heard at the ballot box. Those will be my first priorities.

Trump's destructive trade war has set our relationship with China back 15 or 20 years, and that's ignoring the racist potshots he's taken at them over COVID. Our global economy depends on healthy trade and good relations between China and the outside world.

We have to be very realistic about how much cooperation is possible between the U.S. and China, but Trump's actions the past four years haven't helped. The last thing we need to be doing right now is inflaming the situation.

Our relationship with China, depends on China. If they show a greater willingness to cooperate, then we can rebuild our relationship from the damage that Trump inflicted. If they continue to act in a hostile manner, we'll have to react accordingly.

With what we've seen recently in Hong Kong and Xinjiang, we can no longer afford to be naïve about where China is heading. I will aggressively continue our policy of pivoting to Asia to contain the rising influence of China.

One of the greatest human tragedies of the Trump Administration is the situation on the southern border. We will stop separating families, and we will do whatever it takes to reform our immigration processing in a sensible, humane manner.

We're going to undo some of these policies from day one, and I plan to make a strong push for an immigration reform bill that can help us deal with the backlog of asylum applications, and bring some of the undocumented out of the shadows.
Nobody can deny that the situation on the southern border is a problem right now, and one that we take very seriously. I'm going to do everything I can to resolve this issue when I'm President.
We're going to be fair, but we're going to be tough. I've always supported the rule of law in my career, for decades now, regardless of what some right-wing websites try to say about me.

We need to look at whatever we can do right now to take guns off of the streets and reduce the level of shootings and murders in this country. I am going to push for any kind of assault weapons ban, background check, or other legislation that we can get.

If you look at these mass shootings we keep seeing, assault weapons are responsible for 90 percent of the problem. Everyone wants them banned except a small group of extremists and NRA lobbyists who have bought the Republican Party wholesale.
If we win Florida, this election is over. I want us doing events all over the state.
The right-wing media wants to present me as some kind of a gun-grabber, when that couldn't be further from the truth. My only crime is not parroting the NRA's every last word on this issue.
Come on, man! If there was ever a real investigation of Trump's tax practices by the IRS or the FBI, he'd probably be in prison right now. Am I wrong?

As part of a balanced campaign strategy, of course we're going to attack Donald Trump on his tax shenanigans. But we just need to make sure our main focus is on the substantive issues affecting working Americans.
People know all about Donald Trump and the dozens of scandals that have unfolded around him. I think we're better off talking about solutions to the COVID-19 crisis and the economy.

It's a shame that it takes a global pandemic for us to get serious about the right to vote. The future of democracy demands that we protect the vote in this country, and I intend to push for federal legislation to do just that.

These are perfectly reasonable measures to take that will save lives in the midst of a global pandemic. It's a shame that Republicans, including Trump's Postal Service head, are willing to undermine this process so brazenly.
Anyone can see that we have special circumstances this year. If I'm elected, I plan to appoint a commission to research which of these measures were effective, and what we can do differently in 2024.

Two of my old friends, Jimmy Carter and James Baker, came out with a great study on election integrity a few years ago, and it's time we put their recommendations into action. I think this would represent a reasonable compromise between making it easy to vote, while ensuring our elections are secure from fraud.

Trump's willingness to inflame racial tensions and spread disinformation about China and coronavirus is appalling. There is a direct relationship between his actions and the increase in attacks that we've seen.
Asian-American hate needs to stop, right now. As a candidate I am pleading with all Americans to look into their hearts and ask what they can do to help on this important issue.

Reasonable, intelligent people should be able to distinguish between criticism of China, and criticism of Asian-Americans in the United States. It's very sad and unfortunate that some can't understand this, and we need to do everything possible to prevent these kinds of attacks.

These attacks are wrong and they should prosecuted to the full extent of the law. At the same time, we need more answers from China. Millions of lives and trillions of dollars have been lost, yet they continue to block any serious investigation into the origins of this virus.

I'm warning Mitch McConnell right now. Either he can back off and wait until this election is over with to nominate a justice, or I will do everything in my power to expand the size of the Court as President.

This is a naked power grab by the Republicans, Trump, and Mitch McConnell that puts the integrity of the Court in serious jeopardy. It was just four years ago that McConnell took the exact opposite position on this same issue.

We can sit around all day worrying about tactics, but the fact of the matter is, we need to win elections. If Democrats did a better job of appealing to all Americans, we wouldn't be in this predicament right now.
Absolutely. We can't sit here and play by the niceties of a bygone era while Republicans steamroll us. I'm prepared to appoint four new justices to the Supreme Court.
Fair is fair, right? The Republicans have stolen two seats on the Court with McConnell's chicanery. I think we should create two new justices and appoint them in return.

This is a very serious issue and the integrity of the Court is at risk. We're going to create a commission when I'm elected to recommend ways in which we can reform the federal court system and restore the faith of the American people.
The Court has had nine justices since 1869, and any attempt to change that is sure to destroy the Court's legitimacy even further. We must look at other kinds of reform.

We are praying for a full recovery, but we've seen time after time how Trump has disregarded the medical advice on masking and social distancing.
Jill and I are praying for a full and speedy recovery for President Trump. As someone who has dealt with tragedy, you never want to see this kind of thing happen to anyone.

With minority voter suppression, Russian interference, social media misinformation, and the Postal Service's sabotage of mail-in voting, I don't know why Trump should be the one to doubt the integrity of this year's election. It's Democrats who should be worried!

I've walked the walk on this issue. As Vice President, I was the one who personally certified Donald Trump's election in January of 2017. Trump's rhetoric is extremely irresponsible and dangerous to the future of democracy in this country.

If Trump thought he was going to win this election, he wouldn't be saying these kinds of things. I'm confident that we're going to win, and that the American people will have full faith in the outcome this year.
Let's just wait and see how this all plays out before we go throwing wild accusations at each other. I have every confidence that this will be a fair election.
This is a fake laptop. End of story. I don't know how it got passed around, but you have to strongly suspect Russian intelligence or other nefarious actors here.
This story is disinformation, nothing is proven about the laptop, and no reputable news agency will run with this story. Why should I insert myself into the middle of this controversy?
I want us to focus on Pennsylvania, with maybe a quick stop over the border in Ohio.
We're going to campaign hard in Michigan, Wisconsin, and Iowa on this final day of the campaign.

Elizabeth Warren ran an incredible campaign and I'm proud to have us join forces on this year's Democratic ticket. She is someone who can really help pull our party together and maximize turnout this fall.
We need a Vice President who can help us create a fair deal for the average American. Elizabeth Warren has fought against injustice throughout her career, and we're proud to have her in our campaign.

My goal from the start has been to create an Administration that looks like the rest of America. I'm proud to have a woman as my running-mate, and you'll see with some of my other picks for Attorney General, Secretary of Defense, and so on, that I'm very serious about giving everyone a shot.

I talked to a lot of terrific women, including several African-Americans, and ultimately I went with the person who was most ready to be President from day one. That doesn't mean it wasn't a tough decision.

I chose the best person for the job, period. Equality is about giving everybody an equal chance to prove themselves... it doesn't mean you have litmus tests or only consider candidates of a certain race.

description.source: Let's step back a couple years. In the run-up to the 2016 election, you have the luxury of being your party's presumptive nominee, along with a significant amount of time to prepare for the campaign. How will you take advantage of this time?
There was a mass shooting at a gay nightclub in Orlando overnight, perpetrated by a Muslim, resulting in 50 people killed. What is your reaction?
The FBI director, James Comey, has handed down a severe criticism of your email practices while Secretary of State, though he declined to recommend any indictments. Do you have any comment?
What message will you emphasize as you accept your party's nomination for President of the United States?
What was your rationale behind selecting Tim Kaine as your running mate?
Will you give Bernie Sanders a prime speaking slot at the Democratic Convention?

To what extent will you attack Donald Trump for the rhetoric he has used about Mexicans, Muslims, women, and other groups?
What message will you emphasize about the political views of Donald Trump on economic and budget issues?
What are the next steps that the United States should take to combat global warming?
Do you have plans to take in more than the current level of 10,000 refugees per annum from the conflict in Syria?

During a fundraiser, you made a comment that around half of Trump's supporters form a "basket of deplorables", with a renewed emphasis on racism, bigotry, and Islamophobia. Do you care to clarify?

Do you plan to participate in the customary series of three televised debates with Donald Trump in this election cycle?

A video surfaced of Trump describing how he tried to seduce a married woman, and how he can generally kiss women or "grab them by the pussy". 14 women have also stepped forward to accuse him of assault. What is your response?

I will write a book about the challenges facing America, and on my fight for healthcare access, fair pay, the environment, and the economy. From the time that I was First Lady of Arkansas until now, I have always fought to give every American a fair shake.

It's hard to visit certain places in the heat of a campaign. I will do a tour of the U.S. where I visit all 50 states and highlight the people we're fighting for with Obama's policies, and whom we'll keep fighting for when I'm President.

You could also go the other way and abandon running for politics, maybe taking up a job offer at a TV station. The world is your oyster.

description.source: Let's step back a couple years. In the run-up to the 2016 election, you have the luxury of being your party's presumptive nominee, along with a significant amount of time to prepare for the campaign. How will you take advantage of this time?
The FBI director, James Comey, has handed down a severe criticism of your email practices while Secretary of State, though he declined to recommend any indictments. Do you have any comment?

What message will you emphasize as you accept your party's nomination for President of the United States?
What was your rationale behind selecting Cory Booker as your running mate?
Will you give Bernie Sanders a prime speaking slot at the Democratic Convention?

description.source: Let's step back a couple years. In the run-up to the 2016 election, you have the luxury of being your party's presumptive nominee, along with a significant amount of time to prepare for the campaign. How will you take advantage of this time?

“Perfect”

Those were the words of Barack Obama, as he watches a large flatscreen television across the room from him. The audio output from it relays the projection of the state of Utah in favour of him, completing his 538 vote nationwide sweep of the presidential election. He chuckles to himself. His master plan of tricking the US public into thinking he was an earnest man, that hoped everyone would succeed. He'd played them like fiddles. With his new house and senate supermajorities, he could instate his master plan. First, he would pass a bill that knocks down every Christian church in America and use the rubble to build monuments to Allah. Next, he was going to raise taxes to 101% percent on billionaires, and use the money to buy every school and start teaching communist history. Finally, he would amend the constitution, and remove every odd-numbered amendment, making the American population bend to his every whim (probably, he hadn't thought that far yet). He wonders how anyone could have possibly missed such an obvious plan. It seems only a few people on the internet realized it, but thankfully nobody took them seriously...

From coast to coast and town to town in nearly every public meeting space and private residence, millions of Americans have been captivated, inspired, and in some cases even moved to tears by Republican presidential candidate Mitt Romney, all signs that the nation has undeniably been swept up in full-scale Romneymania. The raw energy and enthusiasm of Romney coupled with his uplifting story of rising from moderate wealth to overwhelming riches are just some of the reasons reverent portraits of the former Massachusetts governor have started appearing in windows across the country, often accompanied by one of Romney's signature inspirational phrases, such as 'let Detroit go bankrupt’, or 'Corporations are people.'

Barack Obama's signature achievement from his first term was a landmark health care reform act. The law will establish insurance exchanges which must meet minimum coverage standards, and also cannot deny people based on pre-existing conditions. To help support these policies, every American will be mandated to purchase health insurance.

stance_desc_1.source: Believes that government regulations have put an unaffordable burden on doctors and insurance companies. Supports drastic cuts to Medicare and Medicaid. May support an end to the FDA and other regulatory agencies to restore competitiveness to the American health care system.

stance_desc_2.source: Supports a greater role for the free market in the halth care sector. Opposed to Obamacare. Probably would not support an end to the FDA or other, more radical measures.

stance_desc_3.source: Probably opposed to Obamacare. Would probably support malpractice reform and other incremental measures to cut overall health care costs, without challenging the larger regulatory system.

stance_desc_4.source: Supports some effort to collectively insure the poor and the chronically ill. May disagree with certain aspects of Obamacare or may not support a mandate, but agrees that the current system needs more intervention.

stance_desc_5.source: Supports Obamacare more or less as is. Rejects calls for a public option but supports an insurance mandate and also strongly supports the existing Medicare system.

stance_desc_6.source: Supports Obamacare but also would support a public insurance agency to ensure minimum coverage standards are met at an affordable cost. Believes that malpractice suits are conducive to good care by providing oversight of the medical system.

stance_desc_7.source: Admires the attempt of Obamacare to reform the system, but sees the change as too incremental. Favors a socialized medical system on the model of most European countries.

description.source: With the death of Osama Bin Laden in 2011 at the hands of the Navy SEALs, a dark chapter from America's history appears to be closed. No significant terrorist attacks have occurred during the Obama Administration, and the war in Iraq appears to have been successfully ended. However, potential trouble looms with Iran's nuclear program.

stance_desc_1.source: Would support an invasion of Iran and advocates for air strikes against their nuclear program. Believes in American Exceptionalism and unilateral action without restraints. Opposes membership in the United Nations. Supports increased military spending and American force projection.

stance_desc_2.source: Supports firm action against Iran and would consider an invasion if necessary. Also supports a strong military. Pays some respect to international alliances and institutions, and does not support radical measures like withdrawing from the U.N.

stance_desc_3.source: Would support any measure to prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapons, but would need to see some evidence that other measures have failed before supporting an invasion. Willing to cooperate with allies and to work within the U.N. where necessary.

stance_desc_4.source: Favors a mix of diplomatic pressure and sanctions against Iran, would be opposed to bombing until the effects of those policies can be evaluated. Supports other efforts like drone strikes which project force at minimum risk to American troops.

stance_desc_5.source: Willing to consider air strikes against Iran if other measures fail. Wants Russia, China, and other powers in the region to put more pressure on the ruling regime as well. Seeks to work within regional power structures when projecting American influence.

stance_desc_6.source: Skeptical of action against Iran. Also critical of other measures such as drone strikes which can potentially kill innocent civilians. Thinks terrorism is in large part a reaction against American overreach.

stance_desc_7.source: Opposed to nearly all foreign interventions. Does not support intervention in Iran. Argues that American intervention in previous decades caused the situation in Iran in the first place. Generally a vocal critic of Israel.

description.source: The United States enters 2012 with a struggling economy. After a severe recession from 2007-2009, unemployment remains over 8%, and many voters are frustrated with the slow pace of job creation. At the same time, the annual deficit has exploded since Obama took office, with some advocating for immediate cuts in government spending.

stance_desc_1.source: Supports growing the economy through large tax cuts, a sweeping reduction in the public sector, and overhaul of Social Security & Medicare, and possibly by reducing the power of the Federal Reserve to inflate the currency.

stance_desc_2.source: Generally supports tax cuts and a reduction in government, including entitlement reform. May favor incremental change over sweeping reductions.

stance_desc_3.source: Supports smaller government in principle. May be willing to compromise and to consider temporary stimulus programs, in exchange for other concessions.

stance_desc_4.source: Favors temporary stimulus measures combined with long-term budget cuts. Generally comfortable with the free market and mainstream economics.

stance_desc_5.source: Favors stimulus measures and not opposed to government programs in principle. Uncomfortable with rapid increases in spending or with entirely new programs and departments.

stance_desc_6.source: Favors both short-term stimulus and long-term growth in the scope of government. Supports a wide range of regulation to mitigate the excesses of the free market.

stance_desc_7.source: Questions the underlying assumptions of capitalism. Supports massive increases in government programs, and would support government ownership of key industries, where appropriate.

description.source: Even as the pace of immigration has declined in recent years, there is fierce disagreement on how to handle the issue of illegal immigrants within the country, and also on how many legal immigrants to allow. Some on the right demand mass deportations, while employers who benefit from cheap labor are more circumspect. At the same time, many liberals and Hispanics urge for some form of recognition and a path to citizenship for illegals.

stance_desc_1.source: Supports the immediate deportation of all illegal immigrants living in the United States. Supports the construction of a border wall. Takes a hard line on legal immigration and visa approvals. Sees Hispanics and other immigrants as a threat to American culture and as a strain on social programs.

stance_desc_2.source: Supports deportation of illegal immigrants living in the United States, with no exceptions based on time spent in the country. Supports construction of a wall and increased border security. May favor incremental measures to avoid the disruption would follow from deporting up to 20 million people in a short period of time.

stance_desc_3.source: Supports deportation of illegal immigrants, but may be willing to offer select, long-term residents a path to citizenship. May or may not advocate for a reduction in legal immigration. Supports increased border security as the best way to solve the issue in the long-term.

stance_desc_4.source: Supports deportation of newly arrived illegal immigrants, a path to citizenship for some long-term residents, and increased border security. Generally sees legal, skilled immigrants as an economic asset.

stance_desc_5.source: Favors some kind of citizenship program for long-term and young illegal immigrants. Friendly with the Hispanic community and not fundamentally opposed to immigration, but may be opposed to policies such as bilingual education. Supports increases in legal immigration and in visa programs.

stance_desc_6.source: Supports a path to citizenship for most illegal immigrants. Would relax immigration restrictions from all sources. Sees current border security as adequate, and does not believe it is the main issue in the current immigration debate.

stance_desc_7.source: Supports huge increases in legal immigration. Would not attempt to deport individuals currently living in the United States. Supports the basic premises of multiculturalism and programs like bilingual education.

description.source: The culture wars have been a feature of American politics for decades, and 2012 is no exception. An increasingly empowered LGBT community demands acceptance for gay marriage while most conservatives still find the idea to be anathema to their sensibilities. The ever-present debates on abortion, religious issues, and gun control are still running strong as well.

stance_desc_1.source: An evangelical Christian or otherwise deeply traditional on social issues. Believes that abortion is murder, and that gay marriage threatens thousands of years of religious and civil precedents. Also favors a traditional role for women and traces many current problems to the women's liberation movement.

stance_desc_2.source: Deeply religious and traditional in their outlook. May support some exceptions but is generally pro-life. Views homosexuality as a sin and opposes gay marriage. Supports traditional family structures and is also a supporter of gun rights.

stance_desc_3.source: Agrees in principle with the idea of the nuclear family as the bulwark of society. Does not take a hard line on gay marriage, but is probably opposed to it. May be willing to compromise on abortion and gun rights in some cases.

stance_desc_4.source: Does not favor extreme measures on the social issues of the day. May support civil unions. Sees the feminist movement as a net positive, while criticizing its perceived excesses. Favors sensible regulation of gun ownership.

stance_desc_5.source: Favors civil unions and may support gay marriage. May support reduced penalties for some drug offenses. In general a supporter of gun control, while acknowledging the rights conferred by the Second Amendment.

stance_desc_6.source: Favors gay marriage, decriminalization of marijuana, legal access to abortion through at least the first trimester, and wide restrictions on gun ownership. Follows women's issues closely and supports increased funding for women's shelters, child care, birth control, and similar programs.

stance_desc_7.source: Favors gay marriage. Advocates for an immediate end to the drug war and the legalization of marijuana and perhaps other drugs. Thinks abortion should be legal in all circumstances. Supports a total or near-total ban on gun ownership. Supports early education on contraceptives to reduce teen pregnancy.

text.source:
“Perfect”

Those were the words of Barack Obama, as he watches a large flatscreen television across the room from him. The audio output from it relays the projection of the state of Utah in favour of him, completing his 538 vote nationwide sweep of the presidential election. He chuckles to himself. His master plan of tricking the US public into thinking he was an earnest man, that hoped everyone would succeed. He'd played them like fiddles. With his new house and senate supermajorities, he could instate his master plan. First, he would pass a bill that knocks down every Christian church in America and use the rubble to build monuments to Allah. Next, he was going to raise taxes to 101% percent on billionaires, and use the money to buy every school and start teaching communist history. Finally, he would amend the constitution, and remove every odd-numbered amendment, making the American population bend to his every whim (probably, he hadn't thought that far yet). He wonders how anyone could have possibly missed such an obvious plan. It seems only a few people on the internet realized it, but thankfully nobody took them seriously...

“Breaking New: RomneyMania sweeps America”

From coast to coast and town to town in nearly every public meeting space and private residence, millions of Americans have been captivated, inspired, and in some cases even moved to tears by Republican presidential candidate Mitt Romney, all signs that the nation has undeniably been swept up in full-scale Romneymania. The raw energy and enthusiasm of Romney coupled with his uplifting story of rising from moderate wealth to overwhelming riches are just some of the reasons reverent portraits of the former Massachusetts governor have started appearing in windows across the country, often accompanied by one of Romney's signature inspirational phrases, such as 'let Detroit go bankrupt’, or 'Corporations are people.'

Human Rights -- It's past time that we cut allegiances with dictators like the House of Saud and truly lived up to our ideals. I will only support or give aid to democratically elected leaders.

Pragmatism -- Our foreign policy right now is effective. We need to guide foreign nations towards democracy and open markets. Doing so will increase the world's prosperity and decrease the chance of future wars.
Non-Intervention -- Most of our foreign troop deployments are relics of the Cold War. We need to stop occupying other nations and focus on fixing our problems here at home.

We will attack Mitt Romney relentlessly. He has flip-flopped on key issues and he destroyed thousands of jobs at Bain Capital. He is out of touch with the American people, and he's attacking us for a health care plan that is nearly identical to his own plan in Massachusetts.
Behind the scenes my surrogates have plenty of dirt to spread about Romney and the Republicans. As President, I will stick to a message of optimism and hope in my own campaign speeches.

I will promise a fresh start in overcoming the gridlock in Washington. In my second term I will reach out to moderates and sensible Republicans to find common, pragmatic solutions to our most pressing issues.

I will pledge a new commitment to liberalism and economic revival. Our social programs and unions need to be protected. In those areas where Republicans continue to stand in the way of progress, we will look for other ways to get things done.

Barack Obama's signature achievement from his first term was a landmark health care reform act. The law will establish insurance exchanges which must meet minimum coverage standards, and also cannot deny people based on pre-existing conditions. To help support these policies, every American will be mandated to purchase health insurance.

stance_desc_1.source: Believes that government regulations have put an unaffordable burden on doctors and insurance companies. Supports drastic cuts to Medicare and Medicaid. May support an end to the FDA and other regulatory agencies to restore competitiveness to the American health care system.

stance_desc_2.source: Supports a greater role for the free market in the halth care sector. Opposed to Obamacare. Probably would not support an end to the FDA or other, more radical measures.

stance_desc_3.source: Probably opposed to Obamacare. Would probably support malpractice reform and other incremental measures to cut overall health care costs, without challenging the larger regulatory system.

stance_desc_4.source: Supports some effort to collectively insure the poor and the chronically ill. May disagree with certain aspects of Obamacare or may not support a mandate, but agrees that the current system needs more intervention.

stance_desc_5.source: Supports Obamacare more or less as is. Rejects calls for a public option but supports an insurance mandate and also strongly supports the existing Medicare system.

stance_desc_6.source: Supports Obamacare but also would support a public insurance agency to ensure minimum coverage standards are met at an affordable cost. Believes that malpractice suits are conducive to good care by providing oversight of the medical system.

stance_desc_7.source: Admires the attempt of Obamacare to reform the system, but sees the change as too incremental. Favors a socialized medical system on the model of most European countries.

description.source: With the death of Osama Bin Laden in 2011 at the hands of the Navy SEALs, a dark chapter from America's history appears to be closed. No significant terrorist attacks have occurred during the Obama Administration, and the war in Iraq appears to have been successfully ended. However, potential trouble looms with Iran's nuclear program.

stance_desc_1.source: Would support an invasion of Iran and advocates for air strikes against their nuclear program. Believes in American Exceptionalism and unilateral action without restraints. Opposes membership in the United Nations. Supports increased military spending and American force projection.

stance_desc_2.source: Supports firm action against Iran and would consider an invasion if necessary. Also supports a strong military. Pays some respect to international alliances and institutions, and does not support radical measures like withdrawing from the U.N.

stance_desc_3.source: Would support any measure to prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapons, but would need to see some evidence that other measures have failed before supporting an invasion. Willing to cooperate with allies and to work within the U.N. where necessary.

stance_desc_4.source: Favors a mix of diplomatic pressure and sanctions against Iran, would be opposed to bombing until the effects of those policies can be evaluated. Supports other efforts like drone strikes which project force at minimum risk to American troops.

stance_desc_5.source: Willing to consider air strikes against Iran if other measures fail. Wants Russia, China, and other powers in the region to put more pressure on the ruling regime as well. Seeks to work within regional power structures when projecting American influence.

stance_desc_6.source: Skeptical of action against Iran. Also critical of other measures such as drone strikes which can potentially kill innocent civilians. Thinks terrorism is in large part a reaction against American overreach.

stance_desc_7.source: Opposed to nearly all foreign interventions. Does not support intervention in Iran. Argues that American intervention in previous decades caused the situation in Iran in the first place. Generally a vocal critic of Israel.

description.source: The United States enters 2012 with a struggling economy. After a severe recession from 2007-2009, unemployment remains over 8%, and many voters are frustrated with the slow pace of job creation. At the same time, the annual deficit has exploded since Obama took office, with some advocating for immediate cuts in government spending.

stance_desc_1.source: Supports growing the economy through large tax cuts, a sweeping reduction in the public sector, and overhaul of Social Security & Medicare, and possibly by reducing the power of the Federal Reserve to inflate the currency.

stance_desc_2.source: Generally supports tax cuts and a reduction in government, including entitlement reform. May favor incremental change over sweeping reductions.

stance_desc_3.source: Supports smaller government in principle. May be willing to compromise and to consider temporary stimulus programs, in exchange for other concessions.

stance_desc_4.source: Favors temporary stimulus measures combined with long-term budget cuts. Generally comfortable with the free market and mainstream economics.

stance_desc_5.source: Favors stimulus measures and not opposed to government programs in principle. Uncomfortable with rapid increases in spending or with entirely new programs and departments.

stance_desc_6.source: Favors both short-term stimulus and long-term growth in the scope of government. Supports a wide range of regulation to mitigate the excesses of the free market.

stance_desc_7.source: Questions the underlying assumptions of capitalism. Supports massive increases in government programs, and would support government ownership of key industries, where appropriate.

description.source: Even as the pace of immigration has declined in recent years, there is fierce disagreement on how to handle the issue of illegal immigrants within the country, and also on how many legal immigrants to allow. Some on the right demand mass deportations, while employers who benefit from cheap labor are more circumspect. At the same time, many liberals and Hispanics urge for some form of recognition and a path to citizenship for illegals.

stance_desc_1.source: Supports the immediate deportation of all illegal immigrants living in the United States. Supports the construction of a border wall. Takes a hard line on legal immigration and visa approvals. Sees Hispanics and other immigrants as a threat to American culture and as a strain on social programs.

stance_desc_2.source: Supports deportation of illegal immigrants living in the United States, with no exceptions based on time spent in the country. Supports construction of a wall and increased border security. May favor incremental measures to avoid the disruption would follow from deporting up to 20 million people in a short period of time.

stance_desc_3.source: Supports deportation of illegal immigrants, but may be willing to offer select, long-term residents a path to citizenship. May or may not advocate for a reduction in legal immigration. Supports increased border security as the best way to solve the issue in the long-term.

stance_desc_4.source: Supports deportation of newly arrived illegal immigrants, a path to citizenship for some long-term residents, and increased border security. Generally sees legal, skilled immigrants as an economic asset.

stance_desc_5.source: Favors some kind of citizenship program for long-term and young illegal immigrants. Friendly with the Hispanic community and not fundamentally opposed to immigration, but may be opposed to policies such as bilingual education. Supports increases in legal immigration and in visa programs.

stance_desc_6.source: Supports a path to citizenship for most illegal immigrants. Would relax immigration restrictions from all sources. Sees current border security as adequate, and does not believe it is the main issue in the current immigration debate.

stance_desc_7.source: Supports huge increases in legal immigration. Would not attempt to deport individuals currently living in the United States. Supports the basic premises of multiculturalism and programs like bilingual education.

description.source: The culture wars have been a feature of American politics for decades, and 2012 is no exception. An increasingly empowered LGBT community demands acceptance for gay marriage while most conservatives still find the idea to be anathema to their sensibilities. The ever-present debates on abortion, religious issues, and gun control are still running strong as well.

stance_desc_1.source: An evangelical Christian or otherwise deeply traditional on social issues. Believes that abortion is murder, and that gay marriage threatens thousands of years of religious and civil precedents. Also favors a traditional role for women and traces many current problems to the women's liberation movement.

stance_desc_2.source: Deeply religious and traditional in their outlook. May support some exceptions but is generally pro-life. Views homosexuality as a sin and opposes gay marriage. Supports traditional family structures and is also a supporter of gun rights.

stance_desc_3.source: Agrees in principle with the idea of the nuclear family as the bulwark of society. Does not take a hard line on gay marriage, but is probably opposed to it. May be willing to compromise on abortion and gun rights in some cases.

stance_desc_4.source: Does not favor extreme measures on the social issues of the day. May support civil unions. Sees the feminist movement as a net positive, while criticizing its perceived excesses. Favors sensible regulation of gun ownership.

stance_desc_5.source: Favors civil unions and may support gay marriage. May support reduced penalties for some drug offenses. In general a supporter of gun control, while acknowledging the rights conferred by the Second Amendment.

stance_desc_6.source: Favors gay marriage, decriminalization of marijuana, legal access to abortion through at least the first trimester, and wide restrictions on gun ownership. Follows women's issues closely and supports increased funding for women's shelters, child care, birth control, and similar programs.

stance_desc_7.source: Favors gay marriage. Advocates for an immediate end to the drug war and the legalization of marijuana and perhaps other drugs. Thinks abortion should be legal in all circumstances. Supports a total or near-total ban on gun ownership. Supports early education on contraceptives to reduce teen pregnancy.

text.source:
“Perfect”

Those were the words of Barack Obama, as he watches a large flatscreen television across the room from him. The audio output from it relays the projection of the state of Utah in favour of him, completing his 538 vote nationwide sweep of the presidential election. He chuckles to himself. His master plan of tricking the US public into thinking he was an earnest man, that hoped everyone would succeed. He'd played them like fiddles. With his new house and senate supermajorities, he could instate his master plan. First, he would pass a bill that knocks down every Christian church in America and use the rubble to build monuments to Allah. Next, he was going to raise taxes to 101% percent on billionaires, and use the money to buy every school and start teaching communist history. Finally, he would amend the constitution, and remove every odd-numbered amendment, making the American population bend to his every whim (probably, he hadn't thought that far yet). He wonders how anyone could have possibly missed such an obvious plan. It seems only a few people on the internet realized it, but thankfully nobody took them seriously...

“Breaking New: RomneyMania sweeps America”

From coast to coast and town to town in nearly every public meeting space and private residence, millions of Americans have been captivated, inspired, and in some cases even moved to tears by Republican presidential candidate Mitt Romney, all signs that the nation has undeniably been swept up in full-scale Romneymania. The raw energy and enthusiasm of Romney coupled with his uplifting story of rising from moderate wealth to overwhelming riches are just some of the reasons reverent portraits of the former Massachusetts governor have started appearing in windows across the country, often accompanied by one of Romney's signature inspirational phrases, such as 'let Detroit go bankrupt’, or 'Corporations are people.'

Let’s hope Romney's business experience can guide America to a prosperous economy.

These banks would have never grown so large in the first place without colluding with the federal government. They only exist now because of a corrupt and possibly unconstitutional bailout.
That's not the best solution for us to take. The last thing we need right now in the financial sector is some kind of arbitrary, destabilizing government action.
We have passed the Dodd-Frank Act to analyze systemic risks to the financial system.
Too big to fail is too big to exist. It's pathetic just how much our representatives have allowed themselves to be bought by financial institutions.
Climate change is a hoax purveyed by a collection of scientists and liberal politicians to provide them a pretext for further intervention in the economy.

Even if climate change is real, it's impossible to determine how much of it results from human action. It's just as possible that the earth is warming of its own accord, and it makes no sense to disrupt our economy and potentially cause a depression until we have more information.

We should have more laws and regulations to reduce our total carbon emissions. Sensible next steps include some combination of a cap-and-trade program domestically, as well as international agreements with other nations.
This is a terrible idea. Can't you just picture twenty million employees performing make-work jobs at miniscule wages?
There are better ways to help the poor among us.
This sounds like a political non-starter. It's an interesting idea but let's steer the conversation towards something more productive.
If we created jobs like this at a set minimum wage, it would benefit everyone. Private sector wages would increase and economic insecurity would be greatly mitigated for millions of people.
Absolutely there is. There are more trees in the United States now than there were at the time of the American Revolution.
We need some rational management of our nation's resources, but I think too often we err on the side of caution when it comes to utilizing our nation's timber.
No, I don't think so. The last thing we need is a return to the abuses of the past.
Current practices are much too permissive. Priceless old-growth forest has been almost completely destroyed, and we are headed into the future on an unsustainable trajectory.
Joseph Schumpeter coined the term of "creative destruction". Society will never evolve if some people aren't relocated into more productive pursuits from time to time.
We created numerous companies like Staples, which are American success stories employing thousands of people.
We all made mistakes when we were younger. I'm no exception.
I will hammer on the theme that Obama has completely failed the United States as President. He has presided over the largest deficit increases and highest unemployment rate in almost a hundred years.

My message will be a message of hope. After four years of economic blight the American people need to feel good about themselves, and they need to know that their efforts will be rewarded with material prosperity.
I will emphasize the point that the Republican Party has a big tent. We are the party for anyone who tries to work hard and get ahead in America.

I will address the long-term danger that liberalism has to create an ossified, uncreative society. I will also emphasize the danger to our individual and collective rights that is inherent Obama's philosophy.
American Exceptionalism -- Providence has given America to the world as an inspiration, and we must vigorously defend the ideals of peace and freedom wherever they may be threatened.
Human Rights -- It's past time that we cut allegiances with dictators like the House of Saud and truly lived up to our ideals. I will only support or give aid to democratically elected leaders.

Pragmatism -- Our foreign policy right now is effective. We need to guide foreign nations towards democracy and open markets. Doing so will increase the world's prosperity and decrease the chance of future wars.
Non-Intervention -- Most of our foreign troop deployments are relics of the Cold War. We need to stop occupying other nations and focus on fixing our problems here at home.
Barack Obama is a smart, engaging man. I like him and wish him all the best after we defeat him in November.
I'm not sure how much I have in common with someone like Obama. I don't really have an opinion one way or the other.
Barack is a decent guy. Our personal feelings for each other are not the issue. What's important are our differences of opinion on how to get the American economy moving.
I don't particularly like Barack. It's hard to feel good about someone who promotes policies as misguided as his.

We will attack Barack Obama relentlessly. He has gone back on his pledge to clean up our political system, he has destroyed hundreds of thousands of jobs in his first term, his values are out of touch with those of most Americans, and his health care reform is disastrous.
My surrogates have plenty of points to make about the failure of the Obama Administration. As the nominee, I will take the high road and stick to a message of optimism and American renewal.
I will reach out to moderates and conservative Democrats and attempt to build an all-encompassing coalition. It's time that America had a true leader in charge.

I will emphasize the conservatism of my views and my governing philosophy. I will remind the American people that I am strong on defense and that I'm pro-life, pro-free market, pro-business, and deeply religious.

Barack Obama's signature achievement from his first term was a landmark health care reform act. The law will establish insurance exchanges which must meet minimum coverage standards, and also cannot deny people based on pre-existing conditions. To help support these policies, every American will be mandated to purchase health insurance.

stance_desc_1.source: Believes that government regulations have put an unaffordable burden on doctors and insurance companies. Supports drastic cuts to Medicare and Medicaid. May support an end to the FDA and other regulatory agencies to restore competitiveness to the American health care system.

stance_desc_2.source: Supports a greater role for the free market in the halth care sector. Opposed to Obamacare. Probably would not support an end to the FDA or other, more radical measures.

stance_desc_3.source: Probably opposed to Obamacare. Would probably support malpractice reform and other incremental measures to cut overall health care costs, without challenging the larger regulatory system.

stance_desc_4.source: Supports some effort to collectively insure the poor and the chronically ill. May disagree with certain aspects of Obamacare or may not support a mandate, but agrees that the current system needs more intervention.

stance_desc_5.source: Supports Obamacare more or less as is. Rejects calls for a public option but supports an insurance mandate and also strongly supports the existing Medicare system.

stance_desc_6.source: Supports Obamacare but also would support a public insurance agency to ensure minimum coverage standards are met at an affordable cost. Believes that malpractice suits are conducive to good care by providing oversight of the medical system.

stance_desc_7.source: Admires the attempt of Obamacare to reform the system, but sees the change as too incremental. Favors a socialized medical system on the model of most European countries.

description.source: With the death of Osama Bin Laden in 2011 at the hands of the Navy SEALs, a dark chapter from America's history appears to be closed. No significant terrorist attacks have occurred during the Obama Administration, and the war in Iraq appears to have been successfully ended. However, potential trouble looms with Iran's nuclear program.

stance_desc_1.source: Would support an invasion of Iran and advocates for air strikes against their nuclear program. Believes in American Exceptionalism and unilateral action without restraints. Opposes membership in the United Nations. Supports increased military spending and American force projection.

stance_desc_2.source: Supports firm action against Iran and would consider an invasion if necessary. Also supports a strong military. Pays some respect to international alliances and institutions, and does not support radical measures like withdrawing from the U.N.

stance_desc_3.source: Would support any measure to prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapons, but would need to see some evidence that other measures have failed before supporting an invasion. Willing to cooperate with allies and to work within the U.N. where necessary.

stance_desc_4.source: Favors a mix of diplomatic pressure and sanctions against Iran, would be opposed to bombing until the effects of those policies can be evaluated. Supports other efforts like drone strikes which project force at minimum risk to American troops.

stance_desc_5.source: Willing to consider air strikes against Iran if other measures fail. Wants Russia, China, and other powers in the region to put more pressure on the ruling regime as well. Seeks to work within regional power structures when projecting American influence.

stance_desc_6.source: Skeptical of action against Iran. Also critical of other measures such as drone strikes which can potentially kill innocent civilians. Thinks terrorism is in large part a reaction against American overreach.

stance_desc_7.source: Opposed to nearly all foreign interventions. Does not support intervention in Iran. Argues that American intervention in previous decades caused the situation in Iran in the first place. Generally a vocal critic of Israel.

description.source: The United States enters 2012 with a struggling economy. After a severe recession from 2007-2009, unemployment remains over 8%, and many voters are frustrated with the slow pace of job creation. At the same time, the annual deficit has exploded since Obama took office, with some advocating for immediate cuts in government spending.

stance_desc_1.source: Supports growing the economy through large tax cuts, a sweeping reduction in the public sector, and overhaul of Social Security & Medicare, and possibly by reducing the power of the Federal Reserve to inflate the currency.

stance_desc_2.source: Generally supports tax cuts and a reduction in government, including entitlement reform. May favor incremental change over sweeping reductions.

stance_desc_3.source: Supports smaller government in principle. May be willing to compromise and to consider temporary stimulus programs, in exchange for other concessions.

stance_desc_4.source: Favors temporary stimulus measures combined with long-term budget cuts. Generally comfortable with the free market and mainstream economics.

stance_desc_5.source: Favors stimulus measures and not opposed to government programs in principle. Uncomfortable with rapid increases in spending or with entirely new programs and departments.

stance_desc_6.source: Favors both short-term stimulus and long-term growth in the scope of government. Supports a wide range of regulation to mitigate the excesses of the free market.

stance_desc_7.source: Questions the underlying assumptions of capitalism. Supports massive increases in government programs, and would support government ownership of key industries, where appropriate.

description.source: Even as the pace of immigration has declined in recent years, there is fierce disagreement on how to handle the issue of illegal immigrants within the country, and also on how many legal immigrants to allow. Some on the right demand mass deportations, while employers who benefit from cheap labor are more circumspect. At the same time, many liberals and Hispanics urge for some form of recognition and a path to citizenship for illegals.

stance_desc_1.source: Supports the immediate deportation of all illegal immigrants living in the United States. Supports the construction of a border wall. Takes a hard line on legal immigration and visa approvals. Sees Hispanics and other immigrants as a threat to American culture and as a strain on social programs.

stance_desc_2.source: Supports deportation of illegal immigrants living in the United States, with no exceptions based on time spent in the country. Supports construction of a wall and increased border security. May favor incremental measures to avoid the disruption would follow from deporting up to 20 million people in a short period of time.

stance_desc_3.source: Supports deportation of illegal immigrants, but may be willing to offer select, long-term residents a path to citizenship. May or may not advocate for a reduction in legal immigration. Supports increased border security as the best way to solve the issue in the long-term.

stance_desc_4.source: Supports deportation of newly arrived illegal immigrants, a path to citizenship for some long-term residents, and increased border security. Generally sees legal, skilled immigrants as an economic asset.

stance_desc_5.source: Favors some kind of citizenship program for long-term and young illegal immigrants. Friendly with the Hispanic community and not fundamentally opposed to immigration, but may be opposed to policies such as bilingual education. Supports increases in legal immigration and in visa programs.

stance_desc_6.source: Supports a path to citizenship for most illegal immigrants. Would relax immigration restrictions from all sources. Sees current border security as adequate, and does not believe it is the main issue in the current immigration debate.

stance_desc_7.source: Supports huge increases in legal immigration. Would not attempt to deport individuals currently living in the United States. Supports the basic premises of multiculturalism and programs like bilingual education.

description.source: The culture wars have been a feature of American politics for decades, and 2012 is no exception. An increasingly empowered GLBT community demands acceptance for gay marriage while most conservatives still find the idea to be anathema to their sensibilities. The ever-present debates on abortion, religious issues, and gun control are still running strong as well.

stance_desc_1.source: An evangelical Christian or otherwise deeply traditional on social issues. Believes that abortion is murder, and that gay marriage threatens thousands of years of religious and civil precedents. Also favors a traditional role for women and traces many current problems to the women's liberation movement.

stance_desc_2.source: Deeply religious and traditional in their outlook. May support some exceptions but is generally pro-life. Views homosexuality as a sin and opposes gay marriage. Supports traditional family structures and is also a supporter of gun rights.

stance_desc_3.source: Agrees in principle with the idea of the nuclear family as the bulwark of society. Does not take a hard line on gay marriage, but is probably opposed to it. May be willing to compromise on abortion and gun rights in some cases.

stance_desc_4.source: Does not favor extreme measures on the social issues of the day. May support civil unions. Sees the feminist movement as a net positive, while criticizing its perceived excesses. Favors sensible regulation of gun ownership.

stance_desc_5.source: Favors civil unions and may support gay marriage. May support reduced penalties for some drug offenses. In general a supporter of gun control, while acknowledging the rights conferred by the Second Amendment.

stance_desc_6.source: Favors gay marriage, decriminalization of marijuana, legal access to abortion through at least the first trimester, and wide restrictions on gun ownership. Follows women's issues closely and supports increased funding for women's shelters, child care, birth control, and similar programs.

stance_desc_7.source: Favors gay marriage. Advocates for an immediate end to the drug war and the legalization of marijuana and perhaps other drugs. Thinks abortion should be legal in all circumstances. Supports a total or near-total ban on gun ownership. Supports early education on contraceptives to reduce teen pregnancy.

text.source:
“Perfect”

Those were the words of Barack Obama, as he watches a large flatscreen television across the room from him. The audio output from it relays the projection of the state of Utah in favour of him, completing his 538 vote nationwide sweep of the presidential election. He chuckles to himself. His master plan of tricking the US public into thinking he was an earnest man, that hoped everyone would succeed. He'd played them like fiddles. With his new house and senate supermajorities, he could instate his master plan. First, he would pass a bill that knocks down every Christian church in America and use the rubble to build monuments to Allah. Next, he was going to raise taxes to 101% percent on billionaires, and use the money to buy every school and start teaching communist history. Finally, he would amend the constitution, and remove every odd-numbered amendment, making the American population bend to his every whim (probably, he hadn't thought that far yet). He wonders how anyone could have possibly missed such an obvious plan. It seems only a few people on the internet realized it, but thankfully nobody took them seriously...

“Breaking New: RomneyMania sweeps America”

From coast to coast and town to town in nearly every public meeting space and private residence, millions of Americans have been captivated, inspired, and in some cases even moved to tears by Republican presidential candidate Mitt Romney, all signs that the nation has undeniably been swept up in full-scale Romneymania. The raw energy and enthusiasm of Romney coupled with his uplifting story of rising from moderate wealth to overwhelming riches are just some of the reasons reverent portraits of the former Massachusetts governor have started appearing in windows across the country, often accompanied by one of Romney's signature inspirational phrases, such as 'let Detroit go bankrupt’, or 'Corporations are people.'
Sorry, you’ve lost the 2012 election

Your political career very well might be still alive. Your popular vote victory in this election signals that the people still like you, so perhaps another run in 4 years is in the cards? Maybe you'll be Grover Cleveland 2.0 ...

Your political career is most likely over, despite your relative youth, due to the harsh reality of what happens to one-term presidents in this day. Speaking tours and book deals await your future. Perhaps you can be the next Jimmy Carter?

It just seems that America didn't think your first term was impactful enough. The sluggish economy, as well as your promises not meeting your ambitious 2008 rhetoric likely led to this. You still did do a lot, and it's clear that many Americans thought you deserved a second chance with the margin of victory. Let’s hope Romney's business experience can guide America to a prosperous economy.

It just seems that America didn't think your first term was impactful enough. The sluggish economy, as well as your promises not meeting your ambitious 2008 rhetoric likely led to this. Democrats are despondent that after 8 years of George Bush, you weren't able to revitalize the country in time. The house has also stayed Republican and the senate is eerily close to being in their hands as well.
might be casting a lot of tie-breaking votes. Let’s hope Romney's business experience can guide America to a prosperous economy.

It just seems that America didn't think your first term was impactful enough. The sluggish economy, as well as your promises not meeting your ambitious 2008 rhetoric likely led to this. The swing compare to 2008 is staggering, and just goes to show how unpopular you are. The Senate has gone red as well. Let’s hope Romney's business experience can guide America to a prosperous economy.
Congratulations! you've won the 2012 election

It seems Obamacare will survive, as your veto power will stop any attempts at that. you'll also be given another chance to bring recovery to the economy after the Bush recession. If all goes well, you can leave a stronger country for Hillary Clinton in 2016 to take the reins of.

Congratulations! You've successfully fought off a challenge from Mitt Romney and the Republicans, to become the third president in a row to win re-election. Mitt Romney calls to congratulate you on your victory, and the Democrats made some gains in both chambers as well, with the house being just shy of being controlled by them. Your optimistic rhetoric from 2008 wasn't here this time, but Democrats are still satisfied with your electoral vote margin.

Joe Biden is a bit annoyed you won without him, though.
