text.source:
“Perfect”

Those were the words of Barack Obama, as he watches a large flatscreen television across the room from him. The audio output from it relays the projection of the state of Utah in favour of him, completing his 538 vote nationwide sweep of the presidential election. He chuckles to himself. His master plan of tricking the US public into thinking he was an earnest man, that hoped everyone would succeed. He'd played them like fiddles. With his new house and senate supermajorities, he could instate his master plan. First, he would pass a bill that knocks down every Christian church in America and use the rubble to build monuments to Allah. Next, he was going to raise taxes to 101% percent on billionaires, and use the money to buy every school and start teaching communist history. Finally, he would amend the constitution, and remove every odd-numbered amendment, making the American population bend to his every whim (probably, he hadn't thought that far yet). He wonders how anyone could have possibly missed such an obvious plan. It seems only a few people on the internet realized it, but thankfully nobody took them seriously...

“Breaking New: RomneyMania sweeps America”

From coast to coast and town to town in nearly every public meeting space and private residence, millions of Americans have been captivated, inspired, and in some cases even moved to tears by Republican presidential candidate Mitt Romney, all signs that the nation has undeniably been swept up in full-scale Romneymania. The raw energy and enthusiasm of Romney coupled with his uplifting story of rising from moderate wealth to overwhelming riches are just some of the reasons reverent portraits of the former Massachusetts governor have started appearing in windows across the country, often accompanied by one of Romney's signature inspirational phrases, such as 'let Detroit go bankrupt’, or 'Corporations are people.'
Sorry, you’ve lost the 2012 election

Your political career very well might be still alive. Your popular vote victory in this election signals that the people still like you, so perhaps another run in 4 years is in the cards? Maybe you'll be Grover Cleveland 2.0 ...

Your political career is most likely over, despite your relative youth, due to the harsh reality of what happens to one-term presidents in this day. Speaking tours and book deals await your future. Perhaps you can be the next Jimmy Carter?

It just seems that America didn't think your first term was impactful enough. The sluggish economy, as well as your promises not meeting your ambitious 2008 rhetoric likely led to this. You still did do a lot, and it's clear that many Americans thought you deserved a second chance with the margin of victory. Let’s hope Romney's business experience can guide America to a prosperous economy.

It just seems that America didn't think your first term was impactful enough. The sluggish economy, as well as your promises not meeting your ambitious 2008 rhetoric likely led to this. Democrats are despondent that after 8 years of George Bush, you weren't able to revitalize the country in time. The house has also stayed Republican and the senate is eerily close to being in their hands as well. Ryan might be casting a lot of tie-breaking votes. Let’s hope Romney's business experience can guide America to a prosperous economy.

It just seems that America didn't think your first term was impactful enough. The sluggish economy, as well as your promises not meeting your ambitious 2008 rhetoric likely led to this. The swing compare to 2008 is staggering, and just goes to show how unpopular you are. The Senate has gone red as well. Let’s hope Romney's business experience can guide America to a prosperous economy.
Congratulations! you've won the 2012 election

It seems Obamacare will survive, as your veto power will stop any attempts at that. you'll also be given another chance to bring recovery to the economy after the Bush recession. If all goes well, you can leave a stronger country for Hillary Clinton in 2016 to take the reins of.

Congratulations! You've successfully fought off a challenge from Mitt Romney and the Republicans, to become the third president in a row to win re-election. Mitt Romney calls to congratulate you on your victory, and the Democrats made some gains in both chambers as well, with the house being just shy of being controlled by them. Your optimistic rhetoric from 2008 wasn't here this time, but Democrats are still satisfied with your electoral vote margin.

Congratulations! You've successfully fought off a challenge from Mitt Romney and the Republicans, to become the third president in a row to win re-election. Mitt Romney calls to congratulate you on your victory, and the Democrats made some gains in either chamber as well, but you will ultimately have to bargain a lot with Republicans to pass legislation. You didn't do as well as 2008, being the first person since FDR to be re-elected with fewer electoral votes.

Congratulations! You've successfully fought off a challenge from Mitt Romney and the Republicans, to become the third president in a row to win re-election. Mitt Romney calls to congratulate you on your victory. and the Democrats made some meager gains in either the house as well, but Senate losses will bring you down a notch, and force you to be even more bipartisan than before. Lets hope
is ready to break some Senate ties. You didn't do as well as 2008, being the first person since FDR to be re-elected with fewer electoral votes.

To the surprise of many, you became the first Democrat to lose the popular vote while winning the electoral vote! Republicans are seething, trying to cope with the fact that they were so close to victory.
Sorry, you've lost the 2012 election

Many in the conservative wing of the Republican party weren't too keen on you being the nominee, so it's unlikely you'll get nominated again. You still do have a future in politics, so perhaps you could join the Senate or run for governor again, as New England is showing an increasing willingness to elect moderate Republicans on the gubernatorial scale. You might be able to carve out a strong base of support, based on one of your political or personal aspects, to win in either of these positions.

It seems Obama will have another four years to recover the economy, as well as deal with the middle east. Republicans are despondent that you didn't defeat him, as they felt he was a very exploitable incumbent. Fortunately, you did much better than McCain, and it wasn't another landslide loss.

It seems Obama will have another four years to recover the economy, as well as deal with the middle east. Republicans are despondent that you didn't defeat him, as they felt he was a very exploitable incumbent. Fortunately, you did better than McCain, although that might have just been the stagnant economy that caused that.

It seems Obama will have another four years to recover the economy, as well as deal with the middle east. Republicans are despondent that you didn't defeat him, as they felt he was a very exploitable incumbent. Another crushing defeat was not what the Republicans needed, but at least they are keeping their house majority.

To the shock of many, Obama loses the popular vote while winning the electoral vote. Your Republican colleagues aren't too happy, believing a more geographically oriented pick for the presidency instead of your could have won it for them
Congratulations! you've won the 2012 election

Romneycare will most likely be replacing Obamacare (although they aren't all too different), as well as the Bush tax cuts will be extended to help the economy grow. If you're able to recover it and don't make any major mistakes, you should be able to win re-election in 2016. Get ready to move into the White House!.

Congratulations! Despite a well-fought battle from Barack Obama, you've become the first Mormon president and prevented the 3rd re-election in a row. Your margin of victory is remarkable, a complete flip of 2008. It seems the US population was ready for change again. The Senate flips a few seats in favour of the Republicans, too.

Congratulations! Despite a well-fought battle from Barack Obama, you've become the first Mormon president and prevented the 3rd re-election in a row. With a respectable win, you will net a few Senate seats, but so few coming your way will likely mean
will be breaking a few ties. Let’s hope your bipartisanship and moderate views help decisions be made quickly and effectively.

Congratulations! Despite a well-fought battle from Barack Obama, you've become the first Mormon president and prevented the 3rd re-election in a row. it was close, though. Your slim margins will keep the Senate in Democrat’s hands, so be prepared to make concessions to your propositions
To the chagrin of Democrats, creating flashbacks to 2000, the popular vote is won by the Democrats, despite your electoral vote win. be prepared for a galvanized liberal base during the mid-terms.
Joe Biden is a bit annoyed you won without him, though.
Many are also angered of your dropping of Joe Biden, which they feel cost you some votes and possibly the election. Biden himself has already yelled at you for losing the election.

description.source: In the most general terms, what will be your overall campaign strategy against Obama?
What will be the overriding theme of your nomination speech at the Republican Convention?
The Affordable Care Act (i.e. 'Obamacare') will cap annual premiums, require minimum coverage levels, and outlaw discrimination against people with pre-existing conditions. What do you think?
A recent Supreme Court decision affirmed an Arizona law allowing officers to check suspected illegal immigrants for proof of immigration status. Do you think this law is a good idea?
What is your guiding foreign policy philosophy?
Do you support allowing the Bush Tax Cuts to expire for high-income households at the end of 2012?
What is your position on gay marriage?
To what extent will you speak about your religious faith (Mormonism) on the campaign trail?
Would you consider a default on some U.S. debt obligations if the financial situation of the country continues to deteriorate?
Over half of all sexual harassment complaints filed in 2011 were dismissed -- an increase from previous years. Do you think enough is being done to prevent sexual harassment in the workplace?
Should the United States have been so quick to drop its support for Hosni Mubarak in 2011, given recent events in Egypt?
The United States has historically subsidized corn producers. With recent price increases in the corn market, do you still believe that such a program is necessary?

The budget for the Department of Housing and Urban Development was cut by nearly $4 billion in 2012. Do you think subsidized housing for the poor is a good place to begin reducing the federal deficit?
Will you wear an American flag lapel on your suit as you campaign?
We have now had 10 years to analyze the effects of the No Child Left Behind Act. Do you think it is time for a change?
Is your campaign planning to allow Ron Paul a high-profile speaking slot at the Republican Convention, in light of the number of delegates that he commands?
Should the DEA prosecute medicinal marijuana growers in states where that practice has been legalized?
Would you support posting active U.S. Army troops on the U.S.-Mexico border to prevent illegal immigration and drug smuggling?
The maximum duration of unemployment insurance, with all extensions factored in, has been reduced from 99 weeks. Do you think this is appropriate in the current economic climate?
The water level of Lake Mead (the reservoir near Hoover Dam) has been steadily dropping in recent years. Should the Bureau of Reclamation regulate the use of this water more strictly?

Should the Social Security Trust Fund be purchasing U.S. Treasury bills? Should it be allowed to invest in other bonds and securities to potentially increase its rate of return? Or conversely, should the funds be held in a 'lockbox' to guarantee benefit payments?
Should Angela Merkel be doing more to preserve to Euro as the European Union's common currency?
In November 2011, Ohio voters rejected a law to limit collective bargaining power for public unions. Do public sector unions such as teachers' and police unions have too much bargaining power?
Is the United States too reliant on fossil fuels for its energy needs?
Does it make sense to dispose our nuclear waste at Yucca Mountain in Nevada?
This is an unconscionable violation of civil rights and will certainly lead to racial profiling.
The proper authority for enforcement rests with the federal government. This law goes further than federal laws and even if constitutional, should be repealed.
I don't want to comment on an issue that is best left to the voters of Arizona.
The federal government has forced Arizona's hand by being too lax on enforcement for far too long.
Yes. People will continue to move into the region and place an unsustainable burden on the water supply unless the price accurately reflects current and future scarcity.
I'm very worried about the falling water levels in that area. If this continues, then we would eventually need to consider taking action.
I think the system we have in place is working. There will be ebbs and flows in the water level, but we've already seen it start to rebound the last couple of years.
They already regulate it too strictly in my opinion. Water should be much cheaper in the Southwest.
Nuclear power has proven itself to be a dangerous policy idea. We should be moving away from nuclear and into more environmentally friendly types of energy.
I think that what we're doing now is fine. There is no point in revisiting this issue, since the Yucca Mountain plans have been scrapped in any case.
We have to put this waste somewhere. I understand the objections from some in Nevada, but where else are we supposed to store it?
As a sovereign state, Nevada has every right to reject this proposal. Nobody wants to live next to a toxic nuclear waste site.

Decades of meddling by the U.S. has created these unstable situations in the Middle East. We should have withheld our support for Mubarak when he first took office, instead of giving him billions in military aid.
That's a great question. It's hard to speculate on what might have been, but it at time it seemed clear that Mubarak had to go.
We should have been more active in brokering a compromise solution between Mubarak and the protestors.
We have allowed one of the last moderate regimes in the Middle East to be replaced by Muslim fundamentalists. This is an unconscionable betrayal of our ally Israel and will harm American security.
Unions have been eviscerated by decades of outsourcing. Public unions are a necessary bulwark of the middle class and should have every right to bargain for fair wages and benefits.
I support the hardworking teachers and firefighters of Ohio and elsewhere.
That's an issue for the states to decide. You know, the federal government does not support collective bargaining for its employees, so it's not appropriate for me to comment on a state matter.

Collective bargaining in the public sector is one of the primary contributors to our exploding state deficits, which must eventually be subsidized by the federal government. I agree that the practice should end.
This is probably unconstitutional and would represent another step in the transformation of our country into a police state.
I don't agree with that course of action. The Border Patrol is in place to do just that job.
Those decisions, you know, I think our military is a fine force and that's not necessarily the best use of its resources.
I support a wall and I support the presence of American troops. The purpose of the military is to defend our borders.
Gay marriage should be protected at the federal level. The Defense of Marriage Act should be repealed.
I think civil unions are an acceptable compromise for the majority of mainstream Americans.
I'm opposed this personally. I think that, you know, different states have different opinions on this matter and it's best left to them to decide on the issue.
Under no circumstances should the sacred institution of marriage be undermined. The Defense of Marriage Act was passed specifially to address this issue.
The answer is obvious. By continuing to rely on non-renewable energy sources, we place ourselves at greater risk for future energy shocks and we contribute to global warming.
Yes. We need to combine the use of these sources with further research into solar and wind power.
Fossil fuels and coal are the backbone of our energy supply. If we got rid of those, what would we have left? We have to be realistic and realize that our options are limited.
Just drill baby. We need more development of our fossil fuels to reduce foreign dependence.
I support letting the cuts expire. It's time that wealthy Americans paid their fair share for the opportunities our society gives to them.
Perhaps we can consider letting these expire at some point in the future, but for now we are mired in a stagnant economy and need to avoid tax increases.
We should keep the tax cuts as is for the foreseeable future. I don't think it's sound economics to rise taxes on this group.
Our most productive citizens need further tax cuts to stimulate business confidence, investment, and further job creation.
This policy has contributed to the degradation of the American diet and contributes to our exploding obesity and diabetes epidemics. It should be ended.
There is a need for some level of subsidies, but what we have now is too much.
This policy distorts the free market and favors certain types of food over others. It is an example of crony capitalism.
The Department of Agriculture uses subsidies to rationally manage food production. It would be foolish to reverse that policy.
This idea was a failure from day one. Federal education funds are needed the most in low-income districts which have disproportionately suffered from this legislation.
There is a danger of 'teaching to the test'. We do need some testing in place, but to do so on an annual basis is too frequent and interferes with good educational practice.
This is a good program overall. Perhaps some minor details can be fixed, but without standardized testing there is no way to monitor the quality of our educational system.
I question the premise that the Department of Education should be providing funds in the first place. Education is a local concern.

This program will be a disaster. Not only is it an unconstitutional violation of personal freedom, but it will lead to a decline in American health care and will prove to be financially impossible to maintain without socializing the health care system.
This is the wrong way to reform the American health care system. We should be focusing on malpractice reform and on cutting red tape for private insurers.

I'm convinced that this program will work. This is a good compromise allowing private insurers to conduct business, while securing access to health insurance for more Americans. If anything, the increased transparency will reduce insurance costs.
There should be a public insurance company offering health care to all Americans. Private insurers are simply too greedy and too likely to turn down people with pre-existing health conditions.
Absolutely. Marijuana is a dangerous controlled substance, and the federal government has a responsibility to enforce all laws that are currently on the books.

Is this a real question? Where states refuse to uphold their responsibilities, the federal government should step in. Perhaps we can argue about the severity of the penalty, but never about the crime itself.

We might disagree with these laws, but it is the responsibility of the DEA to uphold them. I do think we can look into reducing the penalties, which should decrease the strain on our prisons and allow people a second chance to lead productive lives.
This entire thing wouldn't even be an issue if marijuana were decriminalized as it should be. The DEA should never be prosecuting non-violent, licensed growers of medicinal marijuana.
Some economists estimate that the unemployment rate would be 1-2% lower if unemployment benefits were not so long in duration.
That is nearly two years. We need unemployment benefits but these extensions were clearly out of control.

This is entirely appropriate for an economy recovering from the worst recession since the 1930s. Additionally, there have been repeated jobs proposals in Congress, all of which have been sabotaged by Republican obstructionism.

There shouldn't be limits on the duration of unemployment insurance. This program is the only thing supporting many displaced workers, and the economic benefits of unemployment insurance are also beyond dispute.
The Euro is destined to fail. I can hardly blame Germany for losing patience with its less fiscally scrupulous neighbors.
If Merkel fails in this mission, we all will be affected negatively. I have the utmost faith that she realizes this and will act accordingly.

What's happening now in Europe is criminal. The working class is being punished to fulfill the avarice of huge, multinational banks. Germany should be doing much more to assist Greece, Italy, and Spain before it is too late.
Under no circumstances would the United States consider that as a course of action.
We need to consider all options. A controlled debt writedown just might be the best way to reignite the world economy, which is suffering from an abundance of bad debt at the current moment.
This is a corrupt, ludicrous practice which Congress uses to hide the true size of our budget and Social Security deficits.

I think anyone who has managed money can tell you there is a place for U.S. Treasuries in any professional portfolio. Allowing the Social Security fund to invest in other securities opens a huge number of potential problems and conflicts of interest.
We'll have to make decisions like these at some point. It's better to do so now when we still have some control over the outcome, rather than waiting for a budget crisis to kick in.
We have to make difficult choices. I don't like this any more than most people, but small cuts are necessary to put us on a fiscally sustainable path.
This is the wrong way to go about balancing the budget. I oppose these cuts.
$4 billion barely puts a dent in the size of the deficit. If we made a serious attempt to cut the size of the military our savings would be vastly greater.
It baffles me how someone could be ashamed to display the American flag. It seems a little unpatriotic to me.
Didn't Nixon invent this tactic as a cheap political ploy in the 1960s? This is far from the best way for someone to display their patriotism.
I don't think this is an issue. It just goes to show how as we become more modern in our views as a society, that sexual harassment will become less of an issue in the workplace.
I'm very concerned about this issue. I would like to see our funding level increase for the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, so that adequate resources are in place to pursue these claims.
I don't think we should jump to any conclusions based on one or two years of data. I'm glad you bring this up though. It's a subject worthy of further study by an official panel.
The last thing we need is someone like Ron Paul taking up precious prime time coverage at our convention. We will seat all duly elected delegates, but Ron Paul will never speak at my convention.

You know, it couldn't hurt to give Mr. Paul a few minutes outside of prime time. Even if his views are a little on the fringe, he does have a very committed following. I'm willing to compromise on a couple of issues if that's what it takes to bring them in.
Give him a good slot. He was one of our most effective primary challengers after all. And I'll even throw a line into my nomination speech praising the zeal and efforts of his supporters.
I will hammer on the theme that Obama has completely failed the United States as President. He has presided over the largest deficit increases and highest unemployment rate in almost a hundred years.

My message will be a message of hope. After four years of economic blight the American people need to feel good about themselves, and they need to know that their efforts will be rewarded with material prosperity.
I will emphasize the point that the Republican Party has a big tent. We are the party for anyone who tries to work hard and get ahead in America.

I will address the long-term danger that liberalism has to create an ossified, uncreative society. I will also emphasize the danger to our individual and collective rights that is inherent Obama's philosophy.
American Exceptionalism -- Providence has given America to the world as an inspiration, and we must vigorously defend the ideals of peace and freedom wherever they may be threatened.
Human Rights -- It's past time that we cut allegiances with dictators like the House of Saud and truly lived up to our ideals. I will only support or give aid to democratically elected leaders.

Pragmatism -- Our foreign policy right now is effective. We need to guide foreign nations towards democracy and open markets. Doing so will increase the world's prosperity and decrease the chance of future wars.
Non-Intervention -- Most of our foreign troop deployments are relics of the Cold War. We need to stop occupying other nations and focus on fixing our problems here at home.
The Mormon Church has been the guiding force of my life. It's only natural for me to discuss this influence in my campaign speeches.

On occasion it makes sense to bring this up. Over the years I have helped out many in need through the Mormon Church, both with my time and through charity. We should make sure the American people know this about me.

I already made one speech that was entirely devoted to this issue back in 2008. Bringing it up more often runs the risk of distracting the American people from the most important issues of this campaign.

We will attack Barack Obama relentlessly. He has gone back on his pledge to clean up our political system, he has destroyed hundreds of thousands of jobs in his first term, his values are out of touch with those of most Americans, and his health care reform is disastrous.
My surrogates have plenty of points to make about the failure of the Obama Administration. As the nominee, I will take the high road and stick to a message of optimism and American renewal.
I will reach out to moderates and conservative Democrats and attempt to build an all-encompassing coalition. It's time that America had a true leader in charge.

I will emphasize the conservatism of my views and my governing philosophy. I will remind the American people that I am strong on defense and that I'm pro-life, pro-free market, pro-business, and deeply religious.

Barack Obama's signature achievement from his first term was a landmark health care reform act. The law will establish insurance exchanges which must meet minimum coverage standards, and also cannot deny people based on pre-existing conditions. To help support these policies, every American will be mandated to purchase health insurance.

stance_desc_1.source: Believes that government regulations have put an unaffordable burden on doctors and insurance companies. Supports drastic cuts to Medicare and Medicaid. May support an end to the FDA and other regulatory agencies to restore competitiveness to the American health care system.

stance_desc_2.source: Supports a greater role for the free market in the halth care sector. Opposed to Obamacare. Probably would not support an end to the FDA or other, more radical measures.

stance_desc_3.source: Probably opposed to Obamacare. Would probably support malpractice reform and other incremental measures to cut overall health care costs, without challenging the larger regulatory system.

stance_desc_4.source: Supports some effort to collectively insure the poor and the chronically ill. May disagree with certain aspects of Obamacare or may not support a mandate, but agrees that the current system needs more intervention.

stance_desc_5.source: Supports Obamacare more or less as is. Rejects calls for a public option but supports an insurance mandate and also strongly supports the existing Medicare system.

stance_desc_6.source: Supports Obamacare but also would support a public insurance agency to ensure minimum coverage standards are met at an affordable cost. Believes that malpractice suits are conducive to good care by providing oversight of the medical system.

stance_desc_7.source: Admires the attempt of Obamacare to reform the system, but sees the change as too incremental. Favors a socialized medical system on the model of most European countries.

description.source: With the death of Osama Bin Laden in 2011 at the hands of the Navy SEALs, a dark chapter from America's history appears to be closed. No significant terrorist attacks have occurred during the Obama Administration, and the war in Iraq appears to have been successfully ended. However, potential trouble looms with Iran's nuclear program.

stance_desc_1.source: Would support an invasion of Iran and advocates for air strikes against their nuclear program. Believes in American Exceptionalism and unilateral action without restraints. Opposes membership in the United Nations. Supports increased military spending and American force projection.

stance_desc_2.source: Supports firm action against Iran and would consider an invasion if necessary. Also supports a strong military. Pays some respect to international alliances and institutions, and does not support radical measures like withdrawing from the U.N.

stance_desc_3.source: Would support any measure to prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapons, but would need to see some evidence that other measures have failed before supporting an invasion. Willing to cooperate with allies and to work within the U.N. where necessary.

stance_desc_4.source: Favors a mix of diplomatic pressure and sanctions against Iran, would be opposed to bombing until the effects of those policies can be evaluated. Supports other efforts like drone strikes which project force at minimum risk to American troops.

stance_desc_5.source: Willing to consider air strikes against Iran if other measures fail. Wants Russia, China, and other powers in the region to put more pressure on the ruling regime as well. Seeks to work within regional power structures when projecting American influence.

stance_desc_6.source: Skeptical of action against Iran. Also critical of other measures such as drone strikes which can potentially kill innocent civilians. Thinks terrorism is in large part a reaction against American overreach.

stance_desc_7.source: Opposed to nearly all foreign interventions. Does not support intervention in Iran. Argues that American intervention in previous decades caused the situation in Iran in the first place. Generally a vocal critic of Israel.

description.source: The United States enters 2012 with a struggling economy. After a severe recession from 2007-2009, unemployment remains over 8%, and many voters are frustrated with the slow pace of job creation. At the same time, the annual deficit has exploded since Obama took office, with some advocating for immediate cuts in government spending.

stance_desc_1.source: Supports growing the economy through large tax cuts, a sweeping reduction in the public sector, and overhaul of Social Security & Medicare, and possibly by reducing the power of the Federal Reserve to inflate the currency.

stance_desc_2.source: Generally supports tax cuts and a reduction in government, including entitlement reform. May favor incremental change over sweeping reductions.

stance_desc_3.source: Supports smaller government in principle. May be willing to compromise and to consider temporary stimulus programs, in exchange for other concessions.

stance_desc_4.source: Favors temporary stimulus measures combined with long-term budget cuts. Generally comfortable with the free market and mainstream economics.

stance_desc_5.source: Favors stimulus measures and not opposed to government programs in principle. Uncomfortable with rapid increases in spending or with entirely new programs and departments.

stance_desc_6.source: Favors both short-term stimulus and long-term growth in the scope of government. Supports a wide range of regulation to mitigate the excesses of the free market.

stance_desc_7.source: Questions the underlying assumptions of capitalism. Supports massive increases in government programs, and would support government ownership of key industries, where appropriate.

description.source: Even as the pace of immigration has declined in recent years, there is fierce disagreement on how to handle the issue of illegal immigrants within the country, and also on how many legal immigrants to allow. Some on the right demand mass deportations, while employers who benefit from cheap labor are more circumspect. At the same time, many liberals and Hispanics urge for some form of recognition and a path to citizenship for illegals.

stance_desc_1.source: Supports the immediate deportation of all illegal immigrants living in the United States. Supports the construction of a border wall. Takes a hard line on legal immigration and visa approvals. Sees Hispanics and other immigrants as a threat to American culture and as a strain on social programs.

stance_desc_2.source: Supports deportation of illegal immigrants living in the United States, with no exceptions based on time spent in the country. Supports construction of a wall and increased border security. May favor incremental measures to avoid the disruption would follow from deporting up to 20 million people in a short period of time.

stance_desc_3.source: Supports deportation of illegal immigrants, but may be willing to offer select, long-term residents a path to citizenship. May or may not advocate for a reduction in legal immigration. Supports increased border security as the best way to solve the issue in the long-term.

stance_desc_4.source: Supports deportation of newly arrived illegal immigrants, a path to citizenship for some long-term residents, and increased border security. Generally sees legal, skilled immigrants as an economic asset.

stance_desc_5.source: Favors some kind of citizenship program for long-term and young illegal immigrants. Friendly with the Hispanic community and not fundamentally opposed to immigration, but may be opposed to policies such as bilingual education. Supports increases in legal immigration and in visa programs.

stance_desc_6.source: Supports a path to citizenship for most illegal immigrants. Would relax immigration restrictions from all sources. Sees current border security as adequate, and does not believe it is the main issue in the current immigration debate.

stance_desc_7.source: Supports huge increases in legal immigration. Would not attempt to deport individuals currently living in the United States. Supports the basic premises of multiculturalism and programs like bilingual education.

description.source: The culture wars have been a feature of American politics for decades, and 2012 is no exception. An increasingly empowered GLBT community demands acceptance for gay marriage while most conservatives still find the idea to be anathema to their sensibilities. The ever-present debates on abortion, religious issues, and gun control are still running strong as well.

stance_desc_1.source: An evangelical Christian or otherwise deeply traditional on social issues. Believes that abortion is murder, and that gay marriage threatens thousands of years of religious and civil precedents. Also favors a traditional role for women and traces many current problems to the women's liberation movement.

stance_desc_2.source: Deeply religious and traditional in their outlook. May support some exceptions but is generally pro-life. Views homosexuality as a sin and opposes gay marriage. Supports traditional family structures and is also a supporter of gun rights.

stance_desc_3.source: Agrees in principle with the idea of the nuclear family as the bulwark of society. Does not take a hard line on gay marriage, but is probably opposed to it. May be willing to compromise on abortion and gun rights in some cases.

stance_desc_4.source: Does not favor extreme measures on the social issues of the day. May support civil unions. Sees the feminist movement as a net positive, while criticizing its perceived excesses. Favors sensible regulation of gun ownership.

stance_desc_5.source: Favors civil unions and may support gay marriage. May support reduced penalties for some drug offenses. In general a supporter of gun control, while acknowledging the rights conferred by the Second Amendment.

stance_desc_6.source: Favors gay marriage, decriminalization of marijuana, legal access to abortion through at least the first trimester, and wide restrictions on gun ownership. Follows women's issues closely and supports increased funding for women's shelters, child care, birth control, and similar programs.

stance_desc_7.source: Favors gay marriage. Advocates for an immediate end to the drug war and the legalization of marijuana and perhaps other drugs. Thinks abortion should be legal in all circumstances. Supports a total or near-total ban on gun ownership. Supports early education on contraceptives to reduce teen pregnancy.

answer_feedback.source: This is just what the liberal wing of your party wants to hear.
Many of your supporters were hoping for a more vigorous stance.
Your supporters are in shock at this response -- while your opponents mock you for changing your position so drastically.
That was a good, honest response. Unfortunately, you'd better be prepared to lose some votes in Arizona and Nevada.
The Democrats have spent years trying to erase the stigma that they are soft on defense. This won't help.
Good response. It's important to stand by your policies.
This isn't what you did in 2011. Have you had a change of heart?
You may be right, but you were one of the people who allowed this to happen. Republicans now have ammunition to brand you as a 'flip-flopper'.
You depend on support from public sector unions. Try not to undermine them like this in the future.
Your answer has fired up the liberal base. This should help bolster turnout in key states this fall.
A safe response, but your core voters wanted more from you.
Your personal views come as a surprise to most people, and a disappointing one to your electoral base.
After all their support, the GLBT community can't believe what you just said. You had better be prepared for a backlash from your liberal base.
This response is a little disappointing to environmentalist Democrats.
This is probably the best response for you, but it may make some moderates feel uneasy.
There's certainly nothing wrong with this answer -- it is a little cautious however.
Unfortunately for you, most Democrats agree that we should use a combination of revenue increases as well as spending cuts to balance the budget.
Your supporters can't believe what you just said. You favor even more tax cuts for the rich? They're not the ones voting for you this November...
Horrible response. Some very large agricultural corporations and many Midwest voters disagree.
There's a certain panache to this answer that farmers find appealing.
You can write any thoughts of winning this election right now. Criticizing your own policy this strongly looks bad to almost everyone.
This is a bad answer for you, considering that it's your own health care plan.
Way to stick up for your principles and your policies.
Pundits are asking whether you've implied that your plan doesn't go far enough.
This is just what the conservative wing of your party doesn't want to hear.
The Republicans had no idea that were nominating an environmentalist.
You have expressed a foreign policy position that is anathema to your electoral base. This will hurt you in November.
Did you watch the protests at all? What kind of compromise are you suggesting?
Conservative pundits are very disappointed in your response. You've just reinforced their concerns that you are secretly a moderate.
The Christian right is livid. Already they are talking about fielding a splinter candidate or staying home this fall.
This is a break from your previous statements, and an unwelcome one in the eyes of most potential supporters.
The conservatives in your party are not looking for someone who wavers on this issue, but this may be a safer response overall.
You have fired up the Christian right. This is a key issue to them and they are glad to see that you are on board.
Bad answer for a Republican candidate -- too environmentalist.
This is a good middle ground for you to stake out. I'm confident the American people will appreciate your sensibilities.
Did you seriously just say on a live mic that you favor raising the income tax? And you're a Republican? Your chances of winning this election may have just gone up in smoke.
Your base is hoping to hear something more forceful on the taxation issue.
This answer strikes a good balance between appealing to your base and winning the undecided voter.
This response is a bit of a gamble for you. You've certainly fired up your conservative base, but what will the rest of the country think.
Horrible response. Some very large agricultural corporations and many Midwest voters disagree.
You've borrowed the language of the Libertarians -- but it does sound a little strange to hear Mitt Romney talking about “crony capitalism” ...
There's a certain panache to this answer that farmers find appealing.
Everyone needs to appeal to their base, but saying you'd end the Department of Education makes you look a bit extreme to most people.
Keep throwing the red meat to your supporters.
This is a decent response for you if you're trying to appeal to a larger base.
You've spent years convincing your Republican base that you had changed your mind on this issue. What gives?
How can you even say something like this? You've placed yourself to the left of Barack Obama on health care...
As bad as things are, you might have a shot with a negative message towards the incumbent. Make sure you offer your own solutions too.
This could work very well for you. Make sure you also offer some policy specifics to keep your base fired up.
You will need to win some swing states this fall. It sounds like you're trying to strike a good balance between electability and the demands of your conservative base.
There are enough concrete problems for you to focus on. It seems like a bit of a detour to attack liberalism as a theory, instead of focusing on your own solutions.
Obama's popularity numbers are lukewarm, and the economy is bad. This could work for you.
Everyone knows that conservative activists are fantastic at negative advertising. Let them do their thing while you give positive, uplifting solutions.
You already have a reputation as a moderate, and plenty of voters are looking for a new start. Make sure you get some conservative support though.

text.source: How the fuck did Florida tie are you fucking kidding me

“Too close to call!”

The state of Florida has a margin of victory under half a percent, and with the election hinging on its result, the recounts in the state are going to decide it. Every court option and legal procedure will be investigated by you and your opponent, so be ready for the long haul. Let’s hope this delay in fundamental democracy doesn't result in the unpreparedness of any critical governmental agencies. That would be truly terrible!

“GOD FUCKING DAMNIT GORE”

Those words rang out from the president's office, despite the door being shut. In the room, were President Bill Clinton and Vice President Al Gore.'I BROUGHT THE ECONOMY BACK FROM A TERRIBLE STATE RUN BY INCOMPETENT REPUBLICANS. I WON DURING THE MID-TERMS AND GAVE YOU A FREE TICKET TO THE PRESIDENCY. AND WHAT DO YOU DO? YOU LET THE SON OF THE GUY WHO I BEAT BECOME PRESIDENT! 538 VOTES TO 0!' Those were the words of a less than happy Bill Clinton. Gore responded 'I-I don't know what happened, I-I thought I ran a good campaign b-but...' Clinton interrupted, saying 'You know exactly what happened Gore. For some reason, you did a tank photo op like Dukakis, which is already bad enough. BUT THEN you accidentally fired the tank, I have no clue how, those things are hard to fire, and you hit a group of spectators. Killing 5. Your court date is in a month so you better start prepping a defence team.' 'co-' 'If you’re asking me for a pardon, you can shove it. Then in your speech to the nation about it, you claimed the ghost of William Mckinley had fired the tank by controlling your body. You then spent 50 thousand dollars of taxpayer money on hiring an exorcist to try and remove him. That’s why you lost, Al.
Sorry, you've lost the 2000 election

You still have many options for your political career as of now. You are still popular in your party and Texas, so there is no doubt you can still influence the next candidate. Perhaps it will be you, or your brother. Maybe the American public will get sick of the Bush family and choose someone else entirely. Whatever the case, let’s hope the Republicans can recover as the Democrats did 8 years ago.

Despite your best efforts, Al Gore will succeed Clinton in the presidency. Many Republicans are disappointed with your loss, seeing the Monica Lewinsky scandal, among others a real opening for them to return to the White House. The closeness of the election will likely inspire Gore to be a bit more moderate and bipartisan in his decision-making. With the close Senate, it will certainly be needed.

Despite your best efforts, Al Gore will succeed Clinton in the presidency. Many Republicans are disappointed with your loss, seeing the Monica Lewinsky scandal, among others a real opening for them to return to the White House. Gore flipping the House and Senate will give him some breathing room, but with the slim margins, he will have his work cut out for him.

Despite your best efforts, Al Gore will succeed Clinton in the presidency. Many Republicans are disappointed with your loss, seeing the Monica Lewinsky scandal, among others a real opening for them to return to the White House. Many are shocked at the margin you lost by, seeing the Lewinsky scandal as giving a lot of socially conservative states the impetus to vote for you. Many it really IS just the economy that matters.

For the first time since 1888, the loser of the popular vote has won the election! This has many Republicans enraged, especially due to the fact this is the 3rd Democrat in a row winning with less than 50% of the popular vote. Maybe a run in 4 years IS in the books for you...
Congratulations! You won the 2000 election

What will happen next is up to you, although most people have some expectations. Tax cuts will certainly be going into effect, and some bills related to gay marriage or homosexual people in the military will as well. Just keep an eye out for 2004, and don't make the same mistakes as your dad.

Well done! You've prevented another term of Democrats and succeeded your father as the next Republican president. Your impressive margin allows the Senate and House to stay in Republican hands, with a Republican president for the first time since Dwight Eisenhower!

Well done! You've prevented another term of Democrats and succeeded your father as the next Republican president. You've managed to flip a few seats in the house and Senate, but it's best you act quickly on your promises or the midterms could take that all away.

Well done! You've prevented another term of Democrats and succeeded your father as the next Republican president. You barely won, however, so let’s hope your bipartisanship and compassionate conservativism resonate with many Americans.
For the first time since 1888, the loser of the popular vote has won the election! This has many Democrats are very angry, especially at Ralph Nader for "spoiling" the election.
Sorry, you've lost the 2000 election

It's up to you what you want to do next. A run in 4 years isn't totally out of the question, but after your decades in politics, you might be burnt out. In any case, let’s hope Bush can continue the economic prosperity and tone down the foreign policy intervention, such as in Somalia. Anything more like that would be a disaster...

It just seems all the little things affecting your campaign were too much to handle. Maybe you should have emphasized your relation to Clinton more. Maybe you should have moved politically left to catch some votes from Nader. Maybe you should have moved politically RIGHT to appeal to the south. Whatever it is, George Bush will be the next president. At least with the close margin, Bush's bipartisanship will have to be on full display.

It just seems all the little things affecting your campaign were too much to handle. Maybe you should have emphasized your relation to Clinton more. Maybe you should have moved politically left to catch some votes from Nader. Maybe you should have moved politically RIGHT to appeal to the south. Whatever it is, George Bush will be the next president. As it has since 94, the House and Senate will be Republican hands firmly, as they made some small gains.

It just seems all the little things affecting your campaign were too much to handle. Maybe you should have emphasized your relation to Clinton more. Maybe you should have moved politically left to catch some votes from Nader. Maybe you should have moved politically RIGHT to appeal to the south. Whatever it is, George Bush will be the next president. Bush won by a larger than expected amount, and as such, the Senate and House will favour him heavily. I guess his bipartisanship won't be needed for the next two years...
For the first time in over a century, the loser of the popular vote has won the election! Your fellow Democrats are already having flashbacks of 1888, and are blaming Ralph Nader for it.
Congratulations! You won the 2000 election

You'll no doubt be continuing the economic policies of Clinton, but with your own, Al Gore twist. The environment, healthcare for all, and technology will be your 3 goals of the next term, and if you are successful as Clinton in your achievements, 2004 will be a cakewalk.

Despite another challenge being thrown at you, you've cast aside George Bush and flipped the script on the Republicans, allowing Democrats to win their own 3 presidential elections in a row. Another commanding win for the Democrats as well, and with this, you have flipped both chambers back. Who cares about 1994, anyways?

Despite another challenge being thrown at you, you've cast aside George Bush and flipped the script on the Republicans, allowing Democrats to win their own 3 presidential elections in a row. The house and Senate have tightened up in your favour, but you will still have to appeal to moderate Democrats to pass legislation.

Despite another challenge being thrown at you, you've cast aside George Bush and flipped the script on the Republicans, allowing Democrats to win their own 3 presidential elections in a row. Unfortunately, your win was nowhere near as big as Clinton's, so the chambers are in the Republicans favour for now.

Interestingly enough, you've lost the popular vote despite winning overall, for the first time since 1888. Republicans aren't too happy about losing 3 elections in a row to someone who won less than 50% of the popular vote.

”As expected, you've lost the 2000 election.”

Congratulations! You received 5% of the popular vote! You will enable the Green Party to run a vigorous campaign in 2004 and present a true choice to the American people. You’ve run a great campaign these last few months, and you should have no problem getting renominated in 4 years.

But for now, sit back and relax, you’ve earned it. Who knows? Maybe next election you’ll even win a state or two.

”Congratulations! You’ve won D.C.!”

What a campaign! You’ve managed to surpass expectations and net yourself some electoral votes! You should have no trouble gaining federal matching funds next election, and you can take solace in the fact that the people of D.C. chose the only capable man this election.

Democrats are sure to be miffed, especially so if they lost, but you couldn’t care less at this moment. Good luck in 2004!

”Holy Cow! You won a state!”

Everyone thought it impossible, but you’ve pulled it off! You’re the first third-party candidate in over 30 years to win a state, and both you and your supporters are ecstatic. Federal matching funds in 2004 are all but guaranteed, and you’ve established the green party as a force to be reckoned with.

Let’s hope you’re more than just a flash in the pan and can run a similar campaign in 2004. The Green party may even find itself in the White House someday - and it’s all thanks to you.

”The Senate will now vote on H.R. 5411, the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2001.”

Those were the words of the clerk in the US Senate. They went through each Senator by state, asking for a voice vote from each of them. After all, was said and done, the tally was 81-19 in favour of the motion. the clerk said 'The motion passes. The bill will now be presented to the president for signing.' He stood up and turned around, only to see president Ralph Nader standing 2 inches behind him, which causes the Clerk to stumble back. 'Oh, h-hello there President Nader. I was just going to pres-' He gets interrupted by the loudest yell he had ever heard, when president Nader bellowed at him:

VETOED!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

president Nader then had his 74th veto overridden that congress just 5 minutes later.

”Good lord! You’ve won the 2000 election!”

Everyone thought it impossible, that at best you would get 5%, but you’ve proved everybody wrong! This is the biggest political upset in American history, beating out Truman over 50 years ago. An impromptu party has been arranged at the Green Party headquarters in DC, your answering machine is clogged with congratulatory calls from your supporters, and every news station in the country has been clamouring to get to you for an interview

What you've achieved tonight is a stellar victory that will be studied for the rest of American history. From Nader’s Raiders to the White House in 30 years, let’s hope your surprise victory has also netted the Green Party some senate seats, or you’ll have to compromise big in the coming years, considering your stiff opposition from both parties. This definitely wasn’t supposed to happen - Good luck!

"It is Over"

The results are coming in, and the phone is ringing. You reach slowly into your drawer and pull out something you never thought you would use. The TV announcer drawls, "The biggest loser of tonight is Ralph Nader! Nader appears to have only received

votes nationwide." You pull the gun to your head, and slowly press on the trigger... and then there was nothing.

A noise suddenly grabs your attention, but your vision is still fuzzy.

"Ralph, cmon!"

The voice seems strained. Your vision suddenly clears. You are in a white room. As your eyes trail sluggishly around the room, you notice something strange. There are a series of glass pods lining the sides of the room. In each pod, there is a person inside each, with every person having some form of cap on their head.

"Get out of the simulator, Ralph! We have some shopping to do," and then finally, you remembered.

”As expected, you've lost the 2000 election.”

This was hardly a surprise, considering the stranglehold that the two-party system holds on American politics. To make matters worse, you didn’t even get 5% of the popular vote, so the Green Party will have to do without federal matching funds.

Still, you’ve run a decent campaign, and your campaign has tried the best it could. You have a chance to cross that 5% threshold in the next election at least, considering you’ve been a perennial candidate for 8 years now. Good luck in 2004!

description.source: Today you have announced the selection of Dick Cheney as running mate. Can you speak more about him?
What key points will you emphasize as you accept your party's nomination for President of the United States?
What is your overall strategy for the 2000 campaign?
Do you have any plans to change American tax policy?
Which of the following best describes your position on the $200 billion surplus that is projected for this year?
Do you believe that Elian Gonzalez should have been returned to Cuba?
Do you have any thoughts on the Bill Clinton scandal that you would like to share?
Which of the following best describes your position on education?
Which of the following best describes your position on Social Security?
Did you support Bill Clinton's actions leading to the bombing of Serbia?
What are your thoughts on the USS Cole bombing, which has killed 17 American sailors. How should we prevent such incidents of terrorism in the future?
What is your vision for the foreign policy of this country?
Do you have anything to say about your alleged drug use in the 1970s?
Another day, another rally on the campaign trail. What do you prefer to talk about today?
Do you support proposals to expand oil drilling in Alaska, and specifically in the Alaska National Wildlife Refuge?
What do you think of proposals to build a sophisticated missile defense system in Eastern Europe?
What is your position on abortion?
Do you have any plans to address or change immigration policy if elected President?
Another day, another rally on the campaign trail. What do you prefer to talk about today?
The Kyoto Protocol would commit the United States (along with many other countries) to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Would you support this plan as President?
Do you think that new regulations from Bill Clinton have unfairly hurt coal-producing states?
Some suggest you lack the experience and qualifications for to be President. What do you say?
In Texas, a man named James Byrd was brutally murdered in what many call a hate crime. What is your opinion of federal hate crime legislation?
It is November 2nd, only five days before the voting. News has just broken that you were arrested for drunken driving in 1976. What is your response?
Where will you make the final stop(s) of your campaign before the voting begins?
We need to expand benefits for Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid. We can use the surplus as well as defense cuts to balance these increases.
I can certainly see the need for some legislation, but it should be addressed at the state level.
We should enact tax cuts to return this money to the American people. My plan will reduce the burden for all Americans who currently pay income tax.
We should try to keep things as they are. The economy has been unusually good the past few years, and we already have a large federal debt to pay down.
I would prefer to see us allocate this money to new and existing government programs so that all Americans can share in our prosperity.
I believe that we need to return control of education to the states and to the people. I would end the Department of Education as President.
Many schools are squandering the resources of the federal government. I support providing school vouchers directly to parents, so that they can choose where their child goes.
We need more spending for America's struggling schools, and national standards and testing to identify and fix poor performers. Every child deserves a strong, functional school to attend.

We need to increase pay for teachers and increase funding for the Department of Education. I don't support nationwide standards or testing -- they will distort the learning process and lead to education by rote.
The Social Security system is a financial time bomb. We need to get rid of it, or at the very least cut its benefits significantly.

The average worker would do much better if their money was invested in the stock market. I support a plan to allow workers to contribute at least some of their Social Security contribution to an individual investment account.
I would establish an iron-clad lockbox for the Social Security fund. When we allow the federal government to borrow our Social Security money, we put every senior in this country at risk.
We need to increase benefits for Social Security. Many people can barely survive on the monthly payment, while we spend billions on the military and run a huge budget surplus.
The Cold War is over. We should cut defense spending and stop operating so many bases overseas. I would pull troops out of places like Germany and Okinawa, where we are no longer defending anything.
America should remain tough, but humble. I am concerned about some of our recent interventions in places like Somalia and Serbia.

We need to remain an engaged, committed defender of human rights in the world. We should do everything possible to secure the friendship of nations like Russia and China, and to prevent atrocities and genocide in the developing world.
I would focus on removing dictators like Saddam Hussein and Kim Jong Il from power. They threaten the stability of the world and perpetrate evil upon their people.
Bill Clinton was an embarrassment to the United States, and his impeachment was well-deserved. I believe that he should have been removed from office.
I don't think we need to belabor the point. I pledge to the American people that I will restore honor and dignity to the White House when I am President.
I am my own man. I respect Bill Clinton in many ways, but his personal conduct was lacking in this case.
This is a non-issue. Bill Clinton is one the best Presidents of the last fifty years, and we should be focusing on his policies and successes, not his personal affairs.
Returning Elian to Cuba was unconscionable. I did not support this decision by the Clinton Administration.
We should be talking less about Elian, and more about my plans to expand upon the great prosperity of this nation.
The law is the law. Elian belongs in Cuba with his father. These questions are never easy, but the Clinton Administration and Janet Reno did what they had to do.
This was an issue that had no bearing on the security of the United States. We also ruined any chance of mediation by insisting on the autonomy of Kosovo.
This certainly helped unseat Slobodan Milosevic, but as President I will make sure that America treads carefully before intervening in foreign nations' affairs.
I support our actions in this theatre. For minimal cost we were able to stop a potential genocide and put a dictator to justice.
The bombing of Serbia killed many innocent civilians and increased antagonism with Russia and China. I believe military intervention should be a last resort.
We need huge tax cuts across the board. Corporate, personal, and capital gains taxes should be slashed. This will further expand the economy through increases in investment.
My budget will cut taxes and return a portion of our budget surplus to the American people. Everybody who pays taxes will receive a reduction.
We have a plan for middle class tax cuts. But it would be irresponsible to make huge changes while we still have a large debt.
I have no plan to cut taxes. If anything, we might need some increases to strengthen Social Security.

I support a strong, overwhelming response against whoever perpetrated this attack. Any government that harbors such terrorists should be overthrown, even if it requires the commitment of American troops.

We need to do two things -- first of all we need better procedures to ensure that our forces in dangerous regions do better at protecting themselves. Secondly, we will investigate who is responsible for this attack, be it Al-Qaeda or some other group, and attack them accordingly.

This attack was a tragedy, but it underscores the need to the United States to have a more limited foreign policy. The Cold War is over, and it doesn't make sense to deploy troops in so many parts of the world.
A crime is a crime, no matter what the motive is. I do not support ideas that some victims should be held in higher regard than others.
I support increased federal hate crime legislation. No American should ever feel like a target of intimidation because of their identity.

We have no proof that global warming exists, and we should be expanding our production of coal and oil to obtain energy independence. I would not surrender the sovereignty of our nation for such trivial objectives.
I would not. The Protocol exempts 80% of the world, including major population centers such as China and India, from compliance, and would cause serious harm to the US economy.
It seems very unlikely that the Senate will ever come up with the votes to ratify this agreement. I don't know how my support or opposition would change that equation.
We have worked for years with many other countries to negotiate this agreement. I support the environment and believe the Protocol should be ratified.
We have almost 9 million illegal immigrants in this country. I support stronger enforcement of immigration laws to reduce this number.

All people contribute to a prosperous America. I support a combination of stronger immigration enforcement with a path to citizenship for people currently in the country. We can do better than we did with the 1986 law.
I prefer to focus on making responsible use of our budget surplus and securing prosperity for the next generation of Americans.

We need a path to citizenship for those in the country, and we need a system of work permits and strict enforcement on employers, so that immigrants do not depress American wages. We should increase aid to Latin America to reduce the rich-poor divide in our economies.
Over a million unborn children are killed every year in this country. We need judges who will overturn Roe v. Wade, or we need a Constitutional Amendment to end the practice of abortion.
I am a pro-life candidate for President, but I understand that we have certain legal protections in place. At the very least, we can end taxpayer funding for this practice.

My goal as President will be to reduce abortions in this country to the lowest level possible. We can increase education and funding for contraception, to reduce unwanted pregnancies. I might be open to ending late-term abortions.
I strongly support the right of a woman to choose. We need to defend this right, and we should increase funding for women's health services, unconditionally.

Absolutely. Anything we can do to work towards energy independence in this country is a positive step. Oil and coal are the foundation of any energy policy, and should be exploited as much as possible.
This is fine with me, but it is a small part of the overall solution. We need to drill wherever we can, while encouraging innovation in other sectors of the energy market.
I oppose these plans. The ANWR is an environmental treasure of the United States, and the oil gained from any exploitation will be relatively limited.
This is a giveaway to oil companies that will not resolve America's underlying energy issues. We need more government investment in renewable energy sources, and strict regulations on oil and coal.
Absolutely. This is just another example of meddling that harms the economy, hurts energy production, and puts hard-working Americans out of work.
Unfortunately, coal is one of the dirtiest forms of energy in existence. I don't see how we can continue to rely on it for the majority of America's energy needs.
This is a necessary step to protect our allies in Europe from current and future threats to their security. I will strongly support this as President.
As President, I will reach out to key military leaders for their advice on this issue.
To defend against whom? The Cold War is over and we should be working with Russia, not against them. This is just more unnecessary military spending.

After eight years of scandals and excesses from the Clinton Administration, I will return this country to its rightful principles -- small government, clean moral conduct, and the freedom of the people.

I will ask the American people if they really want to vote for a third term of Bill Clinton, and remind them that I am the true conservative alternative. I will remind them of Al Gore's campaign finance violations and frequent misrepresentations to the American people.

Conservatism doesn't mean anger and divisiveness. I will govern as a sensible, pragmatic conservative and pass reforms that are broadly acceptable to the American people. I will return a part of our historic surplus to all of our hard-working families who pay taxes.

As President, I will work with Republicans and Democrats to advocate for programs that all Americans can approve of. We need to move past the divisiveness of recent years and strengthen our economy, Social Security, education, and Medicare. I would prefer to return some of the budget surplus to the people, but I am willing to compromise to get things done.

We will emphasize that a vote for Al Gore is a vote for the scandals and liberal policies of the Clinton Administration. We offer a true, conservative alternative to the American people. I will discuss my evangelical Christianity and small-government beliefs.

It is important to nail down our conservative base by emphasizing tax cuts, my evangelical background, opposition to abortion, a strong defense, and limits to government spending. We will ignore Bill Clinton, but paint Al Gore as out of touch.

We need to run an attacking campaign against Al Gore. We will expose his misstatements and emphasize that his proposals will squander our budget surplus and greatly increase the size and scope of government.

I will campaign as a conciliatory, moderate conservative. I will emphasize my record as the Governor of Texas, and my support across different groups and parties. We will minimize any talk of budget cuts or overturning existing programs. We will resist the temptation to criticize Bill Clinton.
I plead guilty. I don't have experience with the broken political culture of Washington, unlike my opponent. I will clean this system up when I am President.
Let's give a good speech about how I am the mainstream, conservative candidate who will control spending and return our surplus to the American people.

Domestic issues. Let's talk about my plans to reform Social Security, education, and Medicare to ensure the future prosperity of America. Let's remind voters that these are common-sense proposals that appeal to almost everyone.
We need to attack Al Gore's views on the environment, on energy, on taxes, on spending, and on the right direction for our country. He is out of touch with the American people.

I will emphasize my record and experience as Governor of Texas. I will remind voters that I have worked across the aisle, won support from many different groups, and will be a uniter, not a divider, when I arrive in Washington.
Let's give a good speech about how I am the mainstream, conservative candidate who will control spending and return our surplus to the American people.

Domestic issues. Let's talk about my plans to reform Social Security, education, and Medicare to ensure the future prosperity of America. Let's remind voters that these are common-sense proposals that appeal to almost everyone.
We need to attack Al Gore's views on the environment, on energy, on taxes, on spending, and on the right direction for our country. He is out of touch with the American people.

I will emphasize my record and experience as Governor of Texas. I will remind voters that I have worked across the aisle, won support from many different groups, and will be a uniter, not a divider, when I arrive in Washington.
I will spend the end of my campaign with my brother Jeb in Florida. This state will be critical to our chances.
I will appear in Pennsylvania and spend the latter half of the day in Ohio. These are two huge states that we can bring into the fold.
The upper Midwest is key. I will start in Iowa, travel through Wisconsin, and end up in Michigan.
We need to focus on states like Missouri, Tennessee, and Arkansas. Clinton may have won them four years ago, but with one last push we can make them go Republican.
This could destroy my campaign in the final days. We must accuse the Gore campaign of leaking this to discredit my candidacy, and challenge their credibility and timing.
I will admit my guilt and apologize to the American people for hiding this story. I will say it was a mistake in judgment to believe that this would not come to light in our modern media environment.

I will emphasize that I made mistakes in the past that I'm not proud of, and that I've always been up front with the American people about that fact. I will also remind the voters that I have not drank alcohol since 1986, and question why this came out five days before the election.
I refuse to comment on this issue. My spokeswoman will remind the American people that the real issue is who will be a better President for the country.
These stories are absolutely false. I never used illegal drugs and those who say I did are completely mistaken.
I did some things when I was younger that I'm not proud of. But my record in office and my conduct over the past two decades is clear. I stopped drinking in 1986 and never looked back.
These types of stories should be irrelevant to a political campaign. We've all done things when we were young that we're not proud of.
This is nonsense. I have served as the Governor of Texas, the second largest state in the country, for nearly six years.
James Buchanan had a lot of experience in government. Abraham Lincoln didn't. So what if I'm a little unseasoned? I have the instincts for the job.
Dick Cheney is a principled conservative leader. The two of us will govern over a conservative, patriotic administration. Let's turn the page from the Clinton era.
Dick Cheney is the best person for the job. He has served in all kinds of roles and performed admirably in every case.

text.source: How the fuck did Florida tie are you fucking kidding me

“Too close to call!”

The state of Florida has a margin of victory under half a percent, and with the election hinging on its result, the recounts in the state are going to decide it. Every court option and legal procedure will be investigated by you and your opponent, so be ready for the long haul. Let’s hope this delay in fundamental democracy doesn't result in the unpreparedness of any critical governmental agencies. That would be truly terrible!

“GOD FUCKING DAMNIT GORE”

Those words rang out from the president's office, despite the door being shut. In the room, were President Bill Clinton and Vice President Al Gore.'I BROUGHT THE ECONOMY BACK FROM A TERRIBLE STATE RUN BY INCOMPETENT REPUBLICANS. I WON DURING THE MID-TERMS AND GAVE YOU A FREE TICKET TO THE PRESIDENCY. AND WHAT DO YOU DO? YOU LET THE SON OF THE GUY WHO I BEAT BECOME PRESIDENT! 538 VOTES TO 0!' Those were the words of a less than happy Bill Clinton. Gore responded 'I-I don't know what happened, I-I thought I ran a good campaign b-but...' Clinton interrupted, saying 'You know exactly what happened Gore. For some reason, you did a tank photo op like Dukakis, which is already bad enough. BUT THEN you accidentally fired the tank, I have no clue how, those things are hard to fire, and you hit a group of spectators. Killing 5. Your court date is in a month so you better start prepping a defence team.' 'co-' 'If you’re asking me for a pardon, you can shove it. Then in your speech to the nation about it, you claimed the ghost of William Mckinley had fired the tank by controlling your body. You then spent 50 thousand dollars of taxpayer money on hiring an exorcist to try and remove him. That’s why you lost, Al.
Sorry, you've lost the 2000 election

You still have many options for your political career as of now. You are still popular in your party and Texas, so there is no doubt you can still influence the next candidate. Perhaps it will be you, or your brother. Maybe the American public will get sick of the Bush family and choose someone else entirely. Whatever the case, let’s hope the Republicans can recover as the Democrats did 8 years ago.

Despite your best efforts, Al Gore will succeed Clinton in the presidency. Many Republicans are disappointed with your loss, seeing the Monica Lewinsky scandal, among others a real opening for them to return to the White House. The closeness of the election will likely inspire Gore to be a bit more moderate and bipartisan in his decision-making. With the close Senate, it will certainly be needed.

Despite your best efforts, Al Gore will succeed Clinton in the presidency. Many Republicans are disappointed with your loss, seeing the Monica Lewinsky scandal, among others a real opening for them to return to the White House. Gore flipping the House and Senate will give him some breathing room, but with the slim margins, he will have his work cut out for him.

Many are shocked at the margin you lost by, seeing the Lewinsky scandal as giving a lot of socially conservative states the impetus to vote for you. Many it really IS just the economy that matters.

Congratulations! You won the 2000 election

What will happen next is up to you, although most people have some expectations. Tax cuts will certainly be going into effect, and some bills related to gay marriage or homosexual people in the military will as well. Just keep an eye out for 2004, and don't make the same mistakes as your dad.

Well done! You've prevented another term of Democrats and succeeded your father as the next Republican president. Your impressive margin allows the Senate and House to stay in Republican hands, with a Republican president for the first time since Dwight Eisenhower!

Well done! You've prevented another term of Democrats and succeeded your father as the next Republican president. You've managed to flip a few seats in the house and Senate, but it's best you act quickly on your promises or the midterms could take that all away.

Well done! You've prevented another term of Democrats and succeeded your father as the next Republican president. You barely won, however, so let’s hope your bipartisanship and compassionate conservativism resonate with many Americans.
For the first time since 1888, the loser of the popular vote has won the election! This has many Democrats are very angry, especially at Ralph Nader for "spoiling" the election.
Sorry, you've lost the 2000 election

It's up to you what you want to do next. A run in 4 years isn't totally out of the question, but after your decades in politics, you might be burnt out. In any case, let’s hope Bush can continue the economic prosperity and tone down the foreign policy intervention, such as in Somalia. Anything more like that would be a disaster...

It just seems all the little things affecting your campaign were too much to handle. Maybe you should have emphasized your relation to Clinton more. Maybe you should have moved politically left to catch some votes from Nader. Maybe you should have moved politically RIGHT to appeal to the south. Whatever it is, George Bush will be the next president. At least with the close margin, Bush's bipartisanship will have to be on full display.
