Whatever it is, George Bush will be the next president. As it has since 94, the House and Senate will be Republican hands firmly, as they made some small gains.

It just seems all the little things affecting your campaign were too much to handle. Maybe you should have emphasized your relation to Clinton more. Maybe you should have moved politically left to catch some votes from Nader. Maybe you should have moved politically RIGHT to appeal to the south. Whatever it is, George Bush will be the next president. Bush won by a larger than expected amount, and as such, the Senate and House will favour him heavily. I guess his bipartisanship won't be needed for the next two years...
For the first time in over a century, the loser of the popular vote has won the election! Your fellow Democrats are already having flashbacks of 1888, and are blaming Ralph Nader for it.
Congratulations! You won the 2000 election

You'll no doubt be continuing the economic policies of Clinton, but with your own, Al Gore twist. The environment, healthcare for all, and technology will be your 3 goals of the next term, and if you are successful as Clinton in your achievements, 2004 will be a cakewalk.

Despite another challenge being thrown at you, you've cast aside George Bush and flipped the script on the Republicans, allowing Democrats to win their own 3 presidential elections in a row. Another commanding win for the Democrats as well, and with this, you have flipped both chambers back. Who cares about 1994, anyways?

Despite another challenge being thrown at you, you've cast aside George Bush and flipped the script on the Republicans, allowing Democrats to win their own 3 presidential elections in a row. The house and Senate have tightened up in your favour, but you will still have to appeal to moderate Democrats to pass legislation.

Despite another challenge being thrown at you, you've cast aside George Bush and flipped the script on the Republicans, allowing Democrats to win their own 3 presidential elections in a row. Unfortunately, your win was nowhere near as big as Clinton's, so the chambers are in the Republicans favour for now.

Interestingly enough, you've lost the popular vote despite winning overall, for the first time since 1888. Republicans aren't too happy about losing 3 elections in a row to someone who won less than 50% of the popular vote.

”As expected, you've lost the 2000 election.”

Congratulations! You received 5% of the popular vote! You will enable the Green Party to run a vigorous campaign in 2004 and present a true choice to the American people. You’ve run a great campaign these last few months, and you should have no problem getting renominated in 4 years.

But for now, sit back and relax, you’ve earned it. Who knows? Maybe next election you’ll even win a state or two.

”Congratulations! You’ve won D.C.!”

What a campaign! You’ve managed to surpass expectations and net yourself some electoral votes! You should have no trouble gaining federal matching funds next election, and you can take solace in the fact that the people of D.C. chose the only capable man this election.

Democrats are sure to be miffed, especially so if they lost, but you couldn’t care less at this moment. Good luck in 2004!

”Holy Cow! You won a state!”

Everyone thought it impossible, but you’ve pulled it off! You’re the first third-party candidate in over 30 years to win a state, and both you and your supporters are ecstatic. Federal matching funds in 2004 are all but guaranteed, and you’ve established the green party as a force to be reckoned with.

Let’s hope you’re more than just a flash in the pan and can run a similar campaign in 2004. The Green party may even find itself in the White House someday - and it’s all thanks to you.

”The Senate will now vote on H.R. 5411, the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2001.”

Those were the words of the clerk in the US Senate. They went through each Senator by state, asking for a voice vote from each of them. After all, was said and done, the tally was 81-19 in favour of the motion. the clerk said 'The motion passes. The bill will now be presented to the president for signing.' He stood up and turned around, only to see president Ralph Nader standing 2 inches behind him, which causes the Clerk to stumble back. 'Oh, h-hello there President Nader. I was just going to pres-' He gets interrupted by the loudest yell he had ever heard, when president Nader bellowed at him:

VETOED!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

president Nader then had his 74th veto overridden that congress just 5 minutes later.

”Good lord! You’ve won the 2000 election!”

Everyone thought it impossible, that at best you would get 5%, but you’ve proved everybody wrong! This is the biggest political upset in American history, beating out Truman over 50 years ago. An impromptu party has been arranged at the Green Party headquarters in DC, your answering machine is clogged with congratulatory calls from your supporters, and every news station in the country has been clamouring to get to you for an interview

What you've achieved tonight is a stellar victory that will be studied for the rest of American history. From Nader’s Raiders to the White House in 30 years, let’s hope your surprise victory has also netted the Green Party some senate seats, or you’ll have to compromise big in the coming years, considering your stiff opposition from both parties. This definitely wasn’t supposed to happen - Good luck!

"It is Over"

The results are coming in, and the phone is ringing. You reach slowly into your drawer and pull out something you never thought you would use. The TV announcer drawls, "The biggest loser of tonight is Ralph Nader! Nader appears to have only received

votes nationwide." You pull the gun to your head, and slowly press on the trigger... and then there was nothing.

A noise suddenly grabs your attention, but your vision is still fuzzy.

"Ralph, cmon!"

The voice seems strained. Your vision suddenly clears. You are in a white room. As your eyes trail sluggishly around the room, you notice something strange. There are a series of glass pods lining the sides of the room. In each pod, there is a person inside each, with every person having some form of cap on their head.

"Get out of the simulator, Ralph! We have some shopping to do," and then finally, you remembered.

”As expected, you've lost the 2000 election.”

This was hardly a surprise, considering the stranglehold that the two-party system holds on American politics. To make matters worse, you didn’t even get 5% of the popular vote, so the Green Party will have to do without federal matching funds.

Still, you’ve run a decent campaign, and your campaign has tried the best it could. You have a chance to cross that 5% threshold in the next election at least, considering you’ve been a perennial candidate for 8 years now. Good luck in 2004!

description.source: Today you have announced the selection of Evan Bayh as running mate. Can you speak more about him?
What key points will you emphasize as you accept your party's nomination for President of the United States?
What is your overall strategy for the 2000 campaign?
Do you have any thoughts on the Bill Clinton scandal that you would like to share?
Which of the following best describes your position on education?
Do you believe that Elian Gonzalez should have been returned to Cuba?
Which of the following best describes your position on the $200 billion surplus that is projected for this year?
Which of the following best describes your position on Social Security?
What is your vision for the foreign policy of this country?
What are your thoughts on the USS Cole bombing, which has killed 17 American sailors. How should we prevent such incidents of terrorism in the future?
Did you support Bill Clinton's actions leading to the bombing of Serbia?
Do you have any plans to change American tax policy?
Do you support the air strikes and sanctions that have been levied against Iraq, with the goal of weakening Saddam Hussein?
What is your opinion on the performance and conduct of our current President, Bill Clinton?
Do you support additional gun control measures in this country? Can you give some specifics of what you want?
Do you believe it is appropriate for Hillary Clinton to run for Senate in the state of New York -- a state where she has never lived?
Do you support proposals to expand oil drilling in Alaska, and specifically in the Alaska National Wildlife Refuge?
Do you think that new regulations from Bill Clinton have unfairly hurt coal-producing states?
The Kyoto Protocol would commit the United States (along with many other countries) to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Would you support this plan as President?
Is it true that you claimed to have invented the internet?
Another day, another rally on the campaign trail. What do you prefer to talk about today?
In Texas, a man named James Byrd was brutally murdered in what many call a hate crime. What is your opinion of federal hate crime legislation?
Should low-income parents be able to use federal vouchers to send their children to private schools?
It is November 2nd, only five days before the voting. News has just broken that George Bush was arrested for drunken driving in 1976. What is your response?
Where will you make the final stop(s) of your campaign before the voting begins?
We need to expand benefits for Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid. We can use the surplus as well as defense cuts to balance these increases.
I can certainly see the need for some legislation, but it should be addressed at the state level.
We should enact tax cuts to return this money to the American people. My plan will reduce the burden for all Americans who currently pay income tax.
We should try to keep things as they are. The economy has been unusually good the past few years, and we already have a large federal debt to pay down.
I would prefer to see us allocate this money to new and existing government programs so that all Americans can share in our prosperity.
I believe that we need to return control of education to the states and to the people. I would end the Department of Education as President.
Many schools are squandering the resources of the federal government. I support providing school vouchers directly to parents, so that they can choose where their child goes.
We need more spending for America's struggling schools, and national standards and testing to identify and fix poor performers. Every child deserves a strong, functional school to attend.

We need to increase pay for teachers and increase funding for the Department of Education. I don't support nationwide standards or testing -- they will distort the learning process and lead to education by rote.
The Social Security system is a financial time bomb. We need to get rid of it, or at the very least cut its benefits significantly.

The average worker would do much better if their money was invested in the stock market. I support a plan to allow workers to contribute at least some of their Social Security contribution to an individual investment account.
I would establish an iron-clad lockbox for the Social Security fund. When we allow the federal government to borrow our Social Security money, we put every senior in this country at risk.
We need to increase benefits for Social Security. Many people can barely survive on the monthly payment, while we spend billions on the military and run a huge budget surplus.
The Cold War is over. We should cut defense spending and stop operating so many bases overseas. I would pull troops out of places like Germany and Okinawa, where we are no longer defending anything.
America should remain tough, but humble. I am concerned about some of our recent interventions in places like Somalia and Serbia.

We need to remain an engaged, committed defender of human rights in the world. We should do everything possible to secure the friendship of nations like Russia and China, and to prevent atrocities and genocide in the developing world.
I would focus on removing dictators like Saddam Hussein and Kim Jong Il from power. They threaten the stability of the world and perpetrate evil upon their people.
Bill Clinton was an embarrassment to the United States, and his impeachment was well-deserved. I believe that he should have been removed from office.
I don't think we need to belabor the point. I pledge to the American people that I will restore honor and dignity to the White House when I am President.
I am my own man. I respect Bill Clinton in many ways, but his personal conduct was lacking in this case.
This is a non-issue. Bill Clinton is one the best Presidents of the last fifty years, and we should be focusing on his policies and successes, not his personal affairs.
Returning Elian to Cuba was unconscionable. I did not support this decision by the Clinton Administration.
We should be talking less about Elian, and more about my plans to expand upon the great prosperity of this nation.
The law is the law. Elian belongs in Cuba with his father. These questions are never easy, but the Clinton Administration and Janet Reno did what they had to do.
This was an issue that had no bearing on the security of the United States. We also ruined any chance of mediation by insisting on the autonomy of Kosovo.
This certainly helped unseat Slobodan Milosevic, but as President I will make sure that America treads carefully before intervening in foreign nations' affairs.
I support our actions in this theatre. For minimal cost we were able to stop a potential genocide and put a dictator to justice.
The bombing of Serbia killed many innocent civilians and increased antagonism with Russia and China. I believe military intervention should be a last resort.
We need huge tax cuts across the board. Corporate, personal, and capital gains taxes should be slashed. This will further expand the economy through increases in investment.
My budget will cut taxes and return a portion of our budget surplus to the American people. Everybody who pays taxes will receive a reduction.
We have a plan for middle class tax cuts. But it would be irresponsible to make huge changes while we still have a large debt.
I have no plan to cut taxes. If anything, we might need some increases to strengthen Social Security.

I support a strong, overwhelming response against whoever perpetrated this attack. Any government that harbors such terrorists should be overthrown, even if it requires the commitment of American troops.

We need to do two things -- first of all we need better procedures to ensure that our forces in dangerous regions do better at protecting themselves. Secondly, we will investigate who is responsible for this attack, be it Al-Qaeda or some other group, and attack them accordingly.

This attack was a tragedy, but it underscores the need to the United States to have a more limited foreign policy. The Cold War is over, and it doesn't make sense to deploy troops in so many parts of the world.
A crime is a crime, no matter what the motive is. I do not support ideas that some victims should be held in higher regard than others.
I support increased federal hate crime legislation. No American should ever feel like a target of intimidation because of their identity.
I do not support new gun control laws. We need better enforcement of the existing laws we have. The Assault Weapons Ban should be allowed to expire.
I support the right to bear arms, with a couple of common-sense restrictions. We need background checks at gun shows, and better prevention measures to keep guns away from the mentally ill.
We need to renew the Assault Weapons Ban and make it permanent. I support other measures such as trigger locks to reduce gun violence in this country.
The only way we will end gun violence in this country is through large-scale legislation and the confiscation of troublesome weapons. The Second Amendment was never meant to apply to individuals.

We have no proof that global warming exists, and we should be expanding our production of coal and oil to obtain energy independence. I would not surrender the sovereignty of our nation for such trivial objectives.
I would not. The Protocol exempts 80% of the world, including major population centers such as China and India, from compliance, and would cause serious harm to the US economy.
It seems very unlikely that the Senate will ever come up with the votes to ratify this agreement. I don't know how my support or opposition would change that equation.
We have worked for years with many other countries to negotiate this agreement. I support the environment and believe the Protocol should be ratified.
I believe we haven't gone far enough on this issue. Saddam Hussein is a destabilizing leader, and he must be removed for the Middle East to truly prosper.

We are following the right course in Iraq. We must enforce our agreement to prevent Saddam from acquiring weapons of mass destruction. Saddam is allowing the sanctions to harm his people for his own selfish purposes.

The United States is much too entangled in the Middle East. We should pull back from the region and end sanctions in Iraq. I might remind people that these sanctions have killed hundreds of thousands of Iraqi children.
This seems like another attempt by the Clintons to stretch the rules. Hillary Clinton is clearly from Arkansas and should seek office from that state if she so desires.
I don't have any comment. I trust the people of New York to make the right decision on this issue.
Off the record, I am uncomfortable with this, but I prefer not to make a public statement about it.
The Clintons have added a greatly to the political life of the United States. I support Hillary Clinton in her campaign.
I see how this is appealing to some conservatives, but it still represents the interference of the federal government in education.
I strongly support this idea and will work to implement it as President. All parents deserve to choose where their child will attend school.
This plan will take money out of the public schools and will not fix the underlying problem of poor education in the United States.

Absolutely. Anything we can do to work towards energy independence in this country is a positive step. Oil and coal are the foundation of any energy policy, and should be exploited as much as possible.
This is fine with me, but it is a small part of the overall solution. We need to drill wherever we can, while encouraging innovation in other sectors of the energy market.
I oppose these plans. The ANWR is an environmental treasure of the United States, and the oil gained from any exploitation will be relatively limited.
This is a giveaway to oil companies that will not resolve America's underlying energy issues. We need more government investment in renewable energy sources, and strict regulations on oil and coal.
Absolutely. This is just another example of meddling that harms the economy, hurts energy production, and puts hard-working Americans out of work.
Unfortunately, coal is one of the dirtiest forms of energy in existence. I don't see how we can continue to rely on it for the majority of America's energy needs.

The Clinton Administration has added 23 million jobs to the American economy and unleashed an unprecedented wave of prosperity and innovation. I will continue his policies as President so that all Americans can prosper in the coming years.

We must not undo eight years of progress under President Clinton by cutting key programs and squandering the surplus on tax cuts for the rich. My opponent not only lacks experience, but his conservative ideas are out of step with those of the American public.

I stand here tonight as my own man. We have much more work to do to ensure that America's prosperity flows to all of the people. We need more spending for education, infrastructure, and important research. We also need to protect Social Security, Medicare, and the environment.

I stand here tonight as my own man. I will work day and night to support the hard-working American people. I will make sure our debt is paid down, and that senior citizens and middle class families are protected into the future. I will protect our most important programs from attacks and budget cuts.

We will hammer Bush on his lack of experience and qualifications for the Presidency. We should point to the tactics his operatives used to defeat John McCain as evidence that he is not nearly as moderate and conciliatory as he claims to be. We will point out his connections to America's economic elites.

Why screw up a good thing? I will campaign on the positive record of Bill Clinton and the Democrats over the past eight years, and pledge to continue those policies. I will appear with Clinton at a few rallies during the campaign to make sure Americans get the message.

It is important to shore up our support from liberal Democrats, especially with Ralph Nader in the race. I will pledge to increase spending on our most valued social programs, continue to increase taxes on high-earners like Clinton did, and I will look for other areas where I can appeal to the left.

We need to establish our independence from the Clinton Administration and let the American people know that I am my own man. I will emphasize my own scandal-free conduct, while pledging to help those Americans who have been left behind during the recent years of prosperity.
Let's give a good speech about how I am the mainstream, liberal candidate who will help hard-working Americans and use our surplus to shore up important government programs.

Domestic issues. Let's talk about my plans to protect Social Security, public eduction, and Medicare to ensure the future prosperity of America. Let's remind voters that these are common-sense proposals that appeal to almost everyone.
We need to attack George Bush's views on the environment, on energy, on taxes, on spending, and on the right direction for our country. He is out of touch with the American people.

I will emphasize my record and experience as Vice President to Bill Clinton. Voters are satisfied with the economy and direction of the country, and it is my job to continue the policies that have led to our current prosperity.
I will spend the end of my campaign with my running mate in Florida. This state will be critical to our chances.
I will appear in Pennsylvania and spend the latter half of the day in Ohio. These are two huge states that we can secure.
The upper Midwest is key. I will start in Iowa, travel through Wisconsin, and end up in Michigan.

The state of Florida has a margin of victory under half a percent, and with the election hinging on its result, the recounts in the state are going to decide it. “GOD FUCKING DAMNIT GORE”

Those words rang out from the president's office, despite the door being shut. In the room, were President Bill Clinton and Vice President Al Gore.'I BROUGHT THE ECONOMY BACK FROM A TERRIBLE STATE RUN BY INCOMPETENT REPUBLICANS. I WON DURING THE MID-TERMS AND GAVE YOU A FREE TICKET TO THE PRESIDENCY. AND WHAT DO YOU DO? YOU LET THE SON OF THE GUY WHO I BEAT BECOME PRESIDENT! 538 VOTES TO 0!' Those were the words of a less than happy Bill Clinton. Gore responded 'I-I don't know what happened, I-I thought I ran a good campaign b-but...' Clinton interrupted, saying 'You know exactly what happened Gore. For some reason, you did a tank photo op like Dukakis, which is already bad enough. BUT THEN you accidentally fired the tank, I have no clue how, those things are hard to fire, and you hit a group of spectators. Killing 5. Your court date is in a month so you better start prepping a defence team.' 'co-' 'If you’re asking me for a pardon, you can shove it. Then in your speech to the nation about it, you claimed the ghost of William Mckinley had fired the tank by controlling your body. You then spent 50 thousand dollars of taxpayer money on hiring an exorcist to try and remove him. That’s why you lost, Al.

VETOED!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

president Nader then had his 74th veto overridden that congress just 5 minutes later.

”Good lord! You’ve won the 2000 election!”

Everyone thought it impossible, that at best you would get 5%, but you’ve proved everybody wrong! This is the biggest political upset in American history, beating out Truman over 50 years ago. An impromptu party has been arranged at the Green Party headquarters in DC, your answering machine is clogged with congratulatory calls from your supporters, and every news station in the country has been clamouring to get to you for an interview

What you've achieved tonight is a stellar victory that will be studied for the rest of American history. From Nader’s Raiders to the White House in 30 years, let’s hope your surprise victory has also netted the Green Party some senate seats, or you’ll have to compromise big in the coming years, considering your stiff opposition from both parties. This definitely wasn’t supposed to happen - Good luck!

"It is Over"

The results are coming in, and the phone is ringing. You reach slowly into your drawer and pull out something you never thought you would use. The TV announcer drawls, "The biggest loser of tonight is Ralph Nader! Nader appears to have only received

votes nationwide." You pull the gun to your head, and slowly press on the trigger... and then there was nothing.

A noise suddenly grabs your attention, but your vision is still fuzzy.

"Ralph, cmon!"

The voice seems strained. Your vision suddenly clears. You are in a white room. As your eyes trail sluggishly around the room, you notice something strange. There are a series of glass pods lining the sides of the room. In each pod, there is a person inside each, with every person having some form of cap on their head.

"Get out of the simulator, Ralph! We have some shopping to do," and then finally, you remembered.

”As expected, you've lost the 2000 election.”

This was hardly a surprise, considering the stranglehold that the two-party system holds on American politics. To make matters worse, you didn’t even get 5% of the popular vote, so the Green Party will have to do without federal matching funds.

Still, you’ve run a decent campaign, and your campaign has tried the best it could. You have a chance to cross that 5% threshold in the next election at least, considering you’ve been a perennial candidate for 8 years now. Good luck in 2004!

Do you have any plans to change American tax policy?
The Kyoto Protocol would commit the United States (along with many other countries) to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Would you support this plan as President?
Should low-income parents be able to use federal vouchers to send their children to private schools?
What is your position on American trade policy? How do you feel about the World Trade Organization or NAFTA?
What do you think of proposals to build a sophisticated missile defense system in Eastern Europe?
Do you have any plans to help America's seniors better pay for vital prescription drugs?
Another day, another rally on the campaign trail. What do you prefer to talk about today?

We need to expand benefits for Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid. We can use the surplus as well as defense cuts to balance these increases.
I can certainly see the need for some legislation, but it should be addressed at the state level.
We should enact tax cuts to return this money to the American people. My plan will reduce the burden for all Americans who currently pay income tax.
We should try to keep things as they are. The economy has been unusually good the past few years, and we already have a large federal debt to pay down.
I would prefer to see us allocate this money to new and existing government programs so that all Americans can share in our prosperity.
I believe that we need to return control of education to the states and to the people. I would end the Department of Education as President.
Many schools are squandering the resources of the federal government. I support providing school vouchers directly to parents, so that they can choose where their child goes.
We need more spending for America's struggling schools, and national standards and testing to identify and fix poor performers. Every child deserves a strong, functional school to attend.

We need to increase pay for teachers and increase funding for the Department of Education. I don't support nationwide standards or testing -- they will distort the learning process and lead to education by rote.
The Social Security system is a financial time bomb. We need to get rid of it, or at the very least cut its benefits significantly.

The average worker would do much better if their money was invested in the stock market. I support a plan to allow workers to contribute at least some of their Social Security contribution to an individual investment account.
I would establish an iron-clad lockbox for the Social Security fund. When we allow the federal government to borrow our Social Security money, we put every senior in this country at risk.
We need to increase benefits for Social Security. Many people can barely survive on the monthly payment, while we spend billions on the military and run a huge budget surplus.
The Cold War is over. We should cut defense spending and stop operating so many bases overseas. I would pull troops out of places like Germany and Okinawa, where we are no longer defending anything.
America should remain tough, but humble. I am concerned about some of our recent interventions in places like Somalia and Serbia.

We need to remain an engaged, committed defender of human rights in the world. We should do everything possible to secure the friendship of nations like Russia and China, and to prevent atrocities and genocide in the developing world.
I would focus on removing dictators like Saddam Hussein and Kim Jong Il from power. They threaten the stability of the world and perpetrate evil upon their people.
Bill Clinton was an embarrassment to the United States, and his impeachment was well-deserved. I believe that he should have been removed from office.
I don't think we need to belabor the point. I pledge to the American people that I will restore honor and dignity to the White House when I am President.
I am my own man. I respect Bill Clinton in many ways, but his personal conduct was lacking in this case.
This is a non-issue. Bill Clinton is one the best Presidents of the last fifty years, and we should be focusing on his policies and successes, not his personal affairs.
Returning Elian to Cuba was unconscionable. I did not support this decision by the Clinton Administration.
We should be talking less about Elian, and more about my plans to expand upon the great prosperity of this nation.
The law is the law. Elian belongs in Cuba with his father. These questions are never easy, but the Clinton Administration and Janet Reno did what they had to do.
This was an issue that had no bearing on the security of the United States. We also ruined any chance of mediation by insisting on the autonomy of Kosovo.
This certainly helped unseat Slobodan Milosevic, but as President I will make sure that America treads carefully before intervening in foreign nations' affairs.
I support our actions in this theatre. For minimal cost we were able to stop a potential genocide and put a dictator to justice.
The bombing of Serbia killed many innocent civilians and increased antagonism with Russia and China. I believe military intervention should be a last resort.
We need huge tax cuts across the board. Corporate, personal, and capital gains taxes should be slashed. This will further expand the economy through increases in investment.
My budget will cut taxes and return a portion of our budget surplus to the American people. Everybody who pays taxes will receive a reduction.
We have a plan for middle class tax cuts. But it would be irresponsible to make huge changes while we still have a large debt.
I have no plan to cut taxes. If anything, we might need some increases to strengthen Social Security.

I support a strong, overwhelming response against whoever perpetrated this attack. Any government that harbors such terrorists should be overthrown, even if it requires the commitment of American troops.

We need to do two things -- first of all we need better procedures to ensure that our forces in dangerous regions do better at protecting themselves. Secondly, we will investigate who is responsible for this attack, be it Al-Qaeda or some other group, and attack them accordingly.

This attack was a tragedy, but it underscores the need to the United States to have a more limited foreign policy. The Cold War is over, and it doesn't make sense to deploy troops in so many parts of the world.
A crime is a crime, no matter what the motive is. I do not support ideas that some victims should be held in higher regard than others.
I support increased federal hate crime legislation. No American should ever feel like a target of intimidation because of their identity.
I don't think we need to make huge changes to a system that works for the majority of the people it is supposed to help.
I believe we should address this problem directly -- by adding a prescription drug benefit to Medicare.
We need more funding for Medicare. We need to hold providers accountable when they fall short, by curbing excess profits for pharmaceuticals and targeting HMOs that drop seniors.
We should incorporate Medicare into a larger, universal single-payer health insurance program. Many proposals I hear about are overly cautious and lacking in ambition.

We have no proof that global warming exists, and we should be expanding our production of coal and oil to obtain energy independence. I would not surrender the sovereignty of our nation for such trivial objectives.
I would not. The Protocol exempts 80% of the world, including major population centers such as China and India, from compliance, and would cause serious harm to the US economy.
It seems very unlikely that the Senate will ever come up with the votes to ratify this agreement. I don't know how my support or opposition would change that equation.
We have worked for years with many other countries to negotiate this agreement. I support the environment and believe the Protocol should be ratified.

These agreements are bad because they favor the rights of countries like China and Mexico over those of the United States. I support foreign trade, but I do not support the surrender of America's rights and sovereignty.
Free trade is a bulwark of American prosperity. I support our efforts to protect and increase foreign trade.
Our prosperity depends on the expansion of trade, especially with neighboring countries like Mexico and Canada. We should also expand our programs to support and retrain workers who are displaced.
These organizations and agreements are a scheme to enrich corporations at the expense of the American worker. Employment and wages will plummet while corporate profits expand.
We have almost 9 million illegal immigrants in this country. I support stronger enforcement of immigration laws to reduce this number.

All people contribute to a prosperous America. I support a combination of stronger immigration enforcement with a path to citizenship for people currently in the country. We can do better than we did with the 1986 law.
I prefer to focus on making responsible use of our budget surplus and securing prosperity for the next generation of Americans.

We need a path to citizenship for those in the country, and we need a system of work permits and strict enforcement on employers, so that immigrants do not depress American wages. We should increase aid to Latin America to reduce the rich-poor divide in our economies.
This seems like another attempt by the Clintons to stretch the rules. Hillary Clinton is clearly from Arkansas and should seek office from that state if she so desires.
I don't have any comment. I trust the people of New York to make the right decision on this issue.
Off the record, I am uncomfortable with this, but I prefer not to make a public statement about it.
The Clintons have added a greatly to the political life of the United States. I support Hillary Clinton in her campaign.
I see how this is appealing to some conservatives, but it still represents the interference of the federal government in education.
I strongly support this idea and will work to implement it as President. All parents deserve to choose where their child will attend school.
This plan will take money out of the public schools and will not fix the underlying problem of poor education in the United States.

This is clear political gamesmanship which I cannot support in good conscience. The Reserve should be used in cases of national emergency only. Furthermore, why did Clinton announce this decision so close to the election?
I understand the impulse to help America's families, but the Reserve should be used in cases of national emergency only. This action is unwise.
Oil prices have spiked to nearly $40 a barrel. We need to help hard-working Americans in states like New Hampshire by making temporary allowances from our reserve.
Absolutely. This is just another example of meddling that harms the economy, hurts energy production, and puts hard-working Americans out of work.
Unfortunately, coal is one of the dirtiest forms of energy in existence. I don't see how we can continue to rely on it for the majority of America's energy needs.
This is a necessary step to protect our allies in Europe from current and future threats to their security. I will strongly support this as President.
As President, I will reach out to key military leaders for their advice on this issue.
To defend against whom? The Cold War is over and we should be working with Russia, not against them. This is just more unnecessary military spending.

The most important priority is to prevent the election of George W. Bush to President. I will not put my name on the ballot in any contested state. I expect that people in other places will see that a vote for me symbolizes a vote for a new kind of politics in the long term.

The two parties are almost the same on every major issue. Neither supports meaningful campaign finance reform, universal health care, free college education, a peaceful foreign policy, or the protection of American workers. I present a true alternative to the American people.

If victory for the left means eight years of Bill Clinton and a term for Al Gore, then it is a shallow victory indeed. Bill Clinton has pushed cherished Republican proposals like NAFTA and welfare reform to fruition. I will end this betrayal of the American worker.

I am the true choice for Americans concerned about the environment and Social Security. I will enact strict regulation of the oil and coal industry, fight against big agriculture and GMO's, and support research and subsidies for alternative energy. I will increase funding and benefits for Social Security.

We will run a national campaign and gather as many votes as possible towards our goal of becoming a viable third-party. I will tell liberal Americans to resist the urge to vote for Al Gore, by reminding them of the many ways in which he does not differ from Republicans.
The best way to gather votes is to run up our totals in liberal states like New York, Massachusetts, and California. We will focus on these areas heavily.

I will focus extensively on how Republicans and Democrats alike have betrayed the American worker through trade agreements like NAFTA and a lack of protection for American industry. My campaign will focus on opponents of globalization who have no one else to vote for.

I will focus extensively on how Republicans and Democrats alike have betrayed the American environment. I will hammer on the themes of carbon emissions, GMO crops, giveaways to corporations, and other areas where both parties have failed the American people.

Let's give a good speech about the need for big changes to American politics and society. I will remind voters that the Democrats and Republicans are two sides of the same corporate policies, and attack Al Gore's pretensions to stand for the American worker.

Let's talk about how we are allowing large corporations to ruin the American environment for their own profits, while everyday people suffer from pollution, unclean water, and a dangerous lack of regulation on food and prescription drugs.

Let's emphasize that both Democrats and Republicans have sold out the American worker to the interests of corporations. I will remind people of NAFTA, the WTO protests, and other decisions that have decimated American manufacturing.
I will attack George Bush relentlessly. I will expose Bush as a phony and an elitist, corporatist conservative and not as the moderate that he presents himself as.

Jimmy Carter has been president for 8 years. Inflation has subsided to a steady amount, with unemployment dropping to virtually 0%. Most importantly of all, the government is now trusted more than ever under the leadership of Jimmy Carter, who beat up Richard Nixon on live TV in 1981, garnering a 99% approval rating. If you stay true and honest to America and help fix those problems, poor Reagan won't know what's waiting for him in 80.

Congratulations! Even though you were the favourite from the start, you could have faltered in several ways. You've carried the will of the country and sent a clear message to those DC insiders. Perhaps all the campaigning and stress will inspire you to return to your peanut farm.

Perhaps he might extend an olive branch to you as you did to the conservatives this election, and consider you for his vice presidency?

The year is 1984

Jimmy Carter has been president for 8 years. Inflation has subsided to a steady amount, with unemployment dropping to virtually 0%. The budget had been balanced in 78, and poverty and hunger have been eradicated, as everyone unemployed became a farmer, and is eating peanut butter and peach jam sandwiches. the USSR on the 21st of January had seceded all their land to the USA and declared their government dissolved. Most importantly of all, the government is now trusted more than ever under the leadership of Jimmy Carter, who beat up Richard Nixon on live TV in 1981, garnering a 99% approval rating. Mondale has already won the most recent election 873 electoral votes to 0 against those sorry Republicans, who disbanded shortly after. All is good in the world, thanks to our wonderful leader, Jimmy Carter.
Congratulations! You won the 1976 election!

A number of campaign reforms, many to do with finance will likely be enacted in light of Watergate, as the scandal preceding the Checkers speech Nixon gave in 52 is fresh in the minds of many. Other than that, Inflation and the USSR are yours to deal with, although the former will likely be dealt with differently than the past Democratic, New Deal administrations. If you stay true and honest to America and help fix those problems, poor Reagan won't know what's waiting for him in 80.

Congratulations! Even though you were the favourite from the start, you could have faltered in several ways. You've carried the will of the country and sent a clear message to those DC insiders. While you might not run for president again in four years, a Senate seat in Georgia could suit you very well. Returning to the governor of the state also is possible. Perhaps all the campaigning and stress will inspire you to return to your peanut farm.

The public just didn't think you were up to the task. That's the tradeoff with running a DC outsider like yourself, and the scale tipped in Fords' favour. He will have 4 more years to slash inflation and defend his reputation. He will have to be cautious and show restraint, as you came close to beating him. If the Bayh-Celler amendment didn't pass previously, surely the support to pass it will be present now?

Your quick thrusting into the political limelight and downfall was certainly dramatic. It's up to you what you do next. Perhaps a return to the house, although maybe not in a leadership role. A run in fours years is unlikely with Reagan and his coalition ready to nominate him. Perhaps he might extend an olive branch to you as you did to the conservatives this election, and consider you for his vice presidency?

Despite your best efforts, Jimmy Carter has bested you, making you the only president never elected to office. The toll of Watergate and Vietnam was just too much for you to handle. You can hopefully expand upon the recovery from stagflation in your second term, and hopefully bring honour back to the white house. It won't be an easy feat with your pardon, but America wants to give you a chance. Do well and you might be remembered for more than Nixon's pardon.

What is your opinion on abortion, and specifically the recent Roe v. Wade decision?

In the next issue of Playboy, there's an interview where you used the words "screw" and "shack up" and confessed, "I've committed adultery in my heart..." Many of your religious supporters are furious. What can you say to explain yourself?

I think the fact that this regime collapsed so fast once American troops were gone shows how unsound it really was. We should have never fought the Vietnam War in the first place.

Jimmy Carter has been president for 8 years. Inflation has subsided to a steady amount, with unemployment dropping to virtually 0%. All is good in the world, thanks to our wonderful leader, Jimmy Carter.
Congratulations! You won the 1976 election!

If you stay true and honest to America and help fix those problems, poor Reagan won't know what's waiting for him in 80.

Congratulations! Even though you were the favourite from the start, you could have faltered in several ways. You've carried the will of the country and sent a clear message to those DC insiders. Perhaps all the campaigning and stress will inspire you to return to your peanut farm.

The year is 1984

Jimmy Carter has been president for 8 years. Inflation has subsided to a steady amount, with unemployment dropping to virtually 0%. The budget had been balanced in 78, and poverty and hunger have been eradicated, as everyone unemployed became a farmer, and is eating peanut butter and peach jam sandwiches. the USSR on the 21st of January had seceded all their land to the USA and declared their government dissolved. Most importantly of all, the government is now trusted more than ever under the leadership of Jimmy Carter, who beat up Richard Nixon on live TV in 1981, garnering a 99% approval rating. Mondale has already won the most recent election 873 electoral votes to 0 against those sorry Republicans, who disbanded shortly after. All is good in the world, thanks to our wonderful leader, Jimmy Carter.
Congratulations! You won the 1976 election!

A number of campaign reforms, many to do with finance will likely be enacted in light of Watergate, as the scandal preceding the Checkers speech Nixon gave in 52 is fresh in the minds of many. Other than that, Inflation and the USSR are yours to deal with, although the former will likely be dealt with differently than the past Democratic, New Deal administrations. If you stay true and honest to America and help fix those problems, poor Reagan won't know what's waiting for him in 80.

Congratulations! Even though you were the favourite from the start, you could have faltered in several ways. You've carried the will of the country and sent a clear message to those DC insiders. Interestingly enough, Ford ended up winning the popular vote. Republicans are more shocked than angry. Perhaps passing a new version of the Bayh-Celler amendment can be among your reforms?

You still have many options, despite your defeat, as your jolt to the Democrats nomination and the new focus on character in politics will allow you to expand your horizons. While you might not run for president again in four years, a Senate seat in Georgia could suit you very well. Returning to the governor of the state also is possible. Perhaps all the campaigning and stress will inspire you to return to your peanut farm.

The public just didn't think you were up to the task. That's the tradeoff with running a DC outsider like yourself, and the scale tipped in Fords' favour. He will have 4 more years to slash inflation and defend his reputation. He will have to be cautious and show restraint, as you came close to beating him. If the Bayh-Celler amendment didn't pass previously, surely the support to pass it will be present now?

Your quick thrusting into the political limelight and downfall was certainly dramatic. It's up to you what you do next. Perhaps a return to the house, although maybe not in a leadership role. A run in fours years is unlikely with Reagan and his coalition ready to nominate him. Perhaps he might extend an olive branch to you as you did to the conservatives this election, and consider you for his vice presidency?

Despite your best efforts, Jimmy Carter has bested you, making you the only president never elected to office. The toll of Watergate and Vietnam was just too much for you to handle. Wow! Defying the odds, you have beaten back the Democrats to secure yet another term for your party. After the Watergate pardon, most thought you were done for, but you proved them wrong. You can hopefully expand upon the recovery from stagflation in your second term, and hopefully bring honour back to the white house. It won't be an easy feat with your pardon, but America wants to give you a chance. Do well and you might be remembered for more than Nixon's pardon.

text.source: Sorry, you lost the 1976 election.
I can't fuckin think of anything funny for Ford, he is so bland, just pretend this gif is playing and he is falling down the stairs.
The year is 1984

Jimmy Carter has been president for 8 years. Inflation has subsided to a steady amount, with unemployment dropping to virtually 0%. The budget had been balanced in 78, and poverty and hunger have been eradicated, as everyone unemployed became a farmer, and is eating peanut butter and peach jam sandwiches. the USSR on the 21st of January had seceded all their land to the USA and declared their government dissolved. Most importantly of all, the government is now trusted more than ever under the leadership of Jimmy Carter, who beat up Richard Nixon on live TV in 1981, garnering a 99% approval rating. Mondale has already won the most recent election 873 electoral votes to 0 against those sorry Republicans, who disbanded shortly after. All is good in the world, thanks to our wonderful leader, Jimmy Carter.
Congratulations! You won the 1976 election!

A number of campaign reforms, many to do with finance will likely be enacted in light of Watergate, as the scandal preceding the Checkers speech Nixon gave in 52 is fresh in the minds of many. Other than that, Inflation and the USSR are yours to deal with, although the former will likely be dealt with differently than the past Democratic, New Deal administrations. If you stay true and honest to America and help fix those problems, poor Reagan won't know what's waiting for him in 80.

Congratulations! Even though you were the favourite from the start, you could have faltered in several ways. You've carried the will of the country and sent a clear message to those DC insiders. They'll need to tread carefully, as the impressive turnaround from 72, despite the playboy interview, shows what America thinks of Ol' Dick Nixon's cronies.

Congratulations! Even though you were the favourite from the start, you could have faltered in a number of ways. You've carried the will of the country and sent a clear message to those DC insiders. As expected, your Playboy interview prevented a glorious decimation of the Republicans, but you'll take it, seeing as it could have been worse with the economic recovery.

Congratulations! Even though you were the favourite from the start, you could have faltered in several ways. You've carried the will of the country and sent a clear message to those DC insiders. Many were shocked at the tightness of the election, seeing as the negativity around the GOP and DC in general. Maybe you were TOO honest, Jimmy...
Interestingly enough, Ford ended up winning the popular vote. Republicans are more shocked than angry. Perhaps passing a new version of the Bayh-Celler amendment can be among your reforms?

You still have many options, despite your defeat, as your jolt to the Democrats nomination and the new focus on character in politics will allow you to expand your horizons. While you might not run for president again in four years, a Senate seat in Georgia could suit you very well. Returning to the governor of the state also is possible. Perhaps all the campaigning and stress will inspire you to return to your peanut farm.

The public just didn't think you were up to the task. That's the tradeoff with running a DC outsider like yourself, and the scale tipped in Fords' favour. He will have 4 more years to slash inflation and defend his reputation. He will have to be cautious and show restraint, as you came close to beating him. He with have the public breathing down his neck and Watergate looming over him for his term.

The public just didn't think you were up to the task. That's the tradeoff with running a DC outsider like yourself, and the scale tipped in Fords' favour. Many Democrats are wondering if Watergate might have affected the Republicans more than DC as a  whole, and more standard Democrats could have won this. certainly, your Playboy scandal makes them question nominating someone few people knew.

The public just didn't think you were up to the task. That's the tradeoff with running a DC outsider like yourself, and the scale tipped in Fords' favour. Lots of Democrats are incredibly angered that you could lose by such a margin, and are accusing you of throwing away the presidency with a single interview.

If it wasn't already bad enough for you, the popular votes ended up going in your favour. The public and the Democrats are enraged and in despair, as the will of the people to remove the man who pardon Nixon failed. If the Bayh-Celler amendment didn't pass previously, surely the support to pass it will be present now?

Your quick thrusting into the political limelight and downfall was certainly dramatic. It's up to you what you do next. Perhaps a return to the house, although maybe not in a leadership role. A run in fours years is unlikely with Reagan and his coalition ready to nominate him. Perhaps he might extend an olive branch to you as you did to the conservatives this election, and consider you for his vice presidency?

Despite your best efforts, Jimmy Carter has bested you, making you the only president never elected to office. The toll of Watergate and Vietnam was just too much for you to handle. The recovering economy, however, made this election quite close, so you can take solace in the fact that you went down swinging.

Despite your best efforts, Jimmy Carter has bested you, making you the only president never elected to office. The toll of Watergate and Vietnam was just too much for you to handle. America showed they wanted an outsider, and Carter managed to take that title. Let's hope he can help restore faith in government, and help the inflation die down.

Despite your best efforts, Jimmy Carter has bested you, making you the only president never elected to office. The toll of Watergate and Vietnam was just too much for you to handle. Your Watergate pardon might go down as one of the most blunderous moves in political history, as otherwise, you might have been able to disassociate yourself with Nixon. You, accordingly, got beaten by a larger than expected margin.

Wow! Defying the odds, you have beaten back the Democrats to secure yet another term for your party. After the Watergate pardon, most thought you were done for, but you proved them wrong. You won by a quite shocking margin. It seems your rose garden strategy worked well.

Wow! Defying the odds, you have beaten back the Democrats to secure yet another term for your party. After the Watergate pardon, most thought you were done for, but you proved them wrong. Carter put up a strong fight, however, and without the Playboy scandal, you likely wouldn't have won. The Democrats are sure to make some electoral changes after two outsiders in a row preventing them from winning...

Wow! Defying the odds, you have beaten back the Democrats to secure yet another term for your party. After the Watergate pardon, most thought you were done for, but you proved them wrong. You barely squeaked by, however. Carter gave you a run for your money, and congress isn't too friendly towards you either, so you better tread carefully.

You can hopefully expand upon the recovery from stagflation in your second term, and hopefully bring honour back to the white house. It won't be an easy feat with your pardon, but America wants to give you a chance. Do well and you might be remembered for more than Nixon's pardon.

description.source: You have selected Bob Dole as your running mate. Can you speak a little more about that?
What will your overall campaign strategy be this year?
A lot of voters are concerned about honesty and integrity in our government. What can you say about yourself in this aspect, particularly in light of your pardon of Richard Nixon?
What is your opinion on the court-ordered busing of students within school districts, in a way designed to achieve racial balance in our schools?
What is your position on the federal government making loans to states or cities in need of financial help? An obvious recent example is the $2.3 billion bailout of New York city.
Do you support the ratification of the Equal Rights Amendment, which states "Equality of rights under the law shall not be denied or abridged by the United States or by any State on account of sex."?
Would you support a law for universal health care in this country?
What is your opinion on abortion, and specifically the recent Roe v. Wade decision?
Do you support the Humphrey-Hawkins Full Employment Act?
What is your position on a pardon of Vietnam War draft evaders?
Do you believe that the United States can afford a reduction in defense spending?

Your campaign has just received a big break in the form of a controversial interview that Carter did with Playboy, where he confessed to "committing adultery in his heart" and used some coarse language. Any thoughts?
There is talk of a Presidential Debate for the first time since 1960. Is this something that you're interested in doing?

Some of your operatives want to attack Carter for the way he has equivocated on abortion, gun control, busing, labor issues, and so on. Will you approve a series of ads labeling him as a "flip-flopper"?

Your Secretary of Agriculture, Earl Butz, will be quoted in next week's Rolling Stone as making some very crude and racist jokes. Some have suggested you fire him before the article is released. What are your thoughts?
You have vetoed a significant number of bills in your two years as President. What was your reasoning?
Do you think that the Panama Canal should be turned back over to Panama?
How can we best prevent another episode like the 1973 oil crisis, which paralyzed the country?
Could we have done more to save South Vietnam in 1975, such as air strikes or a limited engagement?
What is your position on right-to-work laws? Would you support a national bill to repeal Taft-Hartley and do away with right-to-work?
The United States started selling large amounts of grain to the Soviet Union, in 1973. What is your opinion on this policy?
General George Brown, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, has made some comments that Israel has become a "burden" to the national defense effort. Do you agree with this?
In 1972, George McGovern proposed replacing the income tax exemption with a $1,000 guaranteed minimum income, for every American citizen. Are you interested in this type of proposal?
Do you think that the tax cuts in early 1975 were the right economic policy for this country?
Where will you focus your efforts on the last day before the election?

I think the fact that this regime collapsed so fast once American troops were gone shows how unsound it really was. We should have never fought the Vietnam War in the first place.
We did our best in Vietnam, but unfortunately things didn't turn out the way we wanted.

The year is 1984

Jimmy Carter has been president for 8 years. Inflation has subsided to a steady amount, with unemployment dropping to virtually 0%. The budget had been balanced in 78, and poverty and hunger have been eradicated, as everyone unemployed became a farmer, and is eating peanut butter and peach jam sandwiches. the USSR on the 21st of January had seceded all their land to the USA and declared their government dissolved. Most importantly of all, the government is now trusted more than ever under the leadership of Jimmy Carter, who beat up Richard Nixon on live TV in 1981, garnering a 99% approval rating. Mondale has already won the most recent election 873 electoral votes to 0 against those sorry Republicans, who disbanded shortly after. All is good in the world, thanks to our wonderful leader, Jimmy Carter.
Congratulations! You won the 1976 election!

A number of campaign reforms, many to do with finance will likely be enacted in light of Watergate, as the scandal preceding the Checkers speech Nixon gave in 52 is fresh in the minds of many. Other than that, Inflation and the USSR are yours to deal with, although the former will likely be dealt with differently than the past Democratic, New Deal administrations. If you stay true and honest to America and help fix those problems, poor Reagan won't know what's waiting for him in 80.

Congratulations! Even though you were the favourite from the start, you could have faltered in several ways. You've carried the will of the country and sent a clear message to those DC insiders. They'll need to tread carefully, as the impressive turnaround from 72, despite the playboy interview, shows what America thinks of Ol' Dick Nixon's cronies.

Congratulations! Even though you were the favourite from the start, you could have faltered in a number of ways. You've carried the will of the country and sent a clear message to those DC insiders. As expected, your Playboy interview prevented a glorious decimation of the Republicans, but you'll take it, seeing as it could have been worse with the economic recovery.

Congratulations! Even though you were the favourite from the start, you could have faltered in several ways. You've carried the will of the country and sent a clear message to those DC insiders. Many were shocked at the tightness of the election, seeing as the negativity around the GOP and DC in general. Maybe you were TOO honest, Jimmy...
Interestingly enough, Ford ended up winning the popular vote. Republicans are more shocked than angry. Perhaps passing a new version of the Bayh-Celler amendment can be among your reforms?

You still have many options, despite your defeat, as your jolt to the Democrats nomination and the new focus on character in politics will allow you to expand your horizons. While you might not run for president again in four years, a Senate seat in Georgia could suit you very well. Returning to the governor of the state also is possible. Perhaps all the campaigning and stress will inspire you to return to your peanut farm.

The public just didn't think you were up to the task. That's the tradeoff with running a DC outsider like yourself, and the scale tipped in Fords' favour. He will have 4 more years to slash inflation and defend his reputation. He will have to be cautious and show restraint, as you came close to beating him. He with have the public breathing down his neck and Watergate looming over him for his term.

The public just didn't think you were up to the task. That's the tradeoff with running a DC outsider like yourself, and the scale tipped in Fords' favour. Many Democrats are wondering if Watergate might have affected the Republicans more than DC as a  whole, and more standard Democrats could have won this. certainly, your Playboy scandal makes them question nominating someone few people knew.

The public just didn't think you were up to the task. That's the tradeoff with running a DC outsider like yourself, and the scale tipped in Fords' favour. Lots of Democrats are incredibly angered that you could lose by such a margin, and are accusing you of throwing away the presidency with a single interview.

If it wasn't already bad enough for you, the popular votes ended up going in your favour. The public and the Democrats are enraged and in despair, as the will of the people to remove the man who pardon Nixon failed. If the Bayh-Celler amendment didn't pass previously, surely the support to pass it will be present now?

Your quick thrusting into the political limelight and downfall was certainly dramatic. It's up to you what you do next. Perhaps a return to the house, although maybe not in a leadership role. A run in fours years is unlikely with Reagan and his coalition ready to nominate him. Perhaps he might extend an olive branch to you as you did to the conservatives this election, and consider you for his vice presidency?

Despite your best efforts, Jimmy Carter has bested you, making you the only president never elected to office. The toll of Watergate and Vietnam was just too much for you to handle. The recovering economy, however, made this election quite close, so you can take solace in the fact that you went down swinging.

Despite your best efforts, Jimmy Carter has bested you, making you the only president never elected to office. The toll of Watergate and Vietnam was just too much for you to handle. America showed they wanted an outsider, and Carter managed to take that title. Let's hope he can help restore faith in government, and help the inflation die down.

Despite your best efforts, Jimmy Carter has bested you, making you the only president never elected to office. The toll of Watergate and Vietnam was just too much for you to handle. Your Watergate pardon might go down as one of the most blunderous moves in political history, as otherwise, you might have been able to disassociate yourself with Nixon. You, accordingly, got beaten by a larger than expected margin.

Wow! Defying the odds, you have beaten back the Democrats to secure yet another term for your party. After the Watergate pardon, most thought you were done for, but you proved them wrong. You won by a quite shocking margin. It seems your rose garden strategy worked well.

Wow! Defying the odds, you have beaten back the Democrats to secure yet another term for your party. After the Watergate pardon, most thought you were done for, but you proved them wrong. Carter put up a strong fight, however, and without the Playboy scandal, you likely wouldn't have won. The Democrats are sure to make some electoral changes after two outsiders in a row preventing them from winning...

Wow! Defying the odds, you have beaten back the Democrats to secure yet another term for your party. After the Watergate pardon, most thought you were done for, but you proved them wrong. You barely squeaked by, however. Carter gave you a run for your money, and congress isn't too friendly towards you either, so you better tread carefully.

You can hopefully expand upon the recovery from stagflation in your second term, and hopefully bring honour back to the white house. It won't be an easy feat with your pardon, but America wants to give you a chance. Do well and you might be remembered for more than Nixon's pardon.

What is your opinion on abortion, and specifically the recent Roe v. Wade decision?
What is your position on the federal government making loans to states or cities in need of financial help? An obvious recent example is the $2.3 billion bailout of New York city.

Do you believe that the United States can afford a reduction in defense spending?

Do you think that the Panama Canal should be turned back over to Panama?

I can see both sides of this issue, but if Congress passes this Act I won't veto it as President.

The year is 1984

Jimmy Carter has been president for 8 years. Inflation has subsided to a steady amount, with unemployment dropping to virtually 0%. The budget had been balanced in 78, and poverty and hunger have been eradicated, as everyone unemployed became a farmer, and is eating peanut butter and peach jam sandwiches. the USSR on the 21st of January had seceded all their land to the USA and declared their government dissolved. Most importantly of all, the government is now trusted more than ever under the leadership of Jimmy Carter, who beat up Richard Nixon on live TV in 1981, garnering a 99% approval rating. Mondale has already won the most recent election 873 electoral votes to 0 against those sorry Republicans, who disbanded shortly after. All is good in the world, thanks to our wonderful leader, Jimmy Carter.
Congratulations! You won the 1976 election!

A number of campaign reforms, many to do with finance will likely be enacted in light of Watergate, as the scandal preceding the Checkers speech Nixon gave in 52 is fresh in the minds of many. Other than that, Inflation and the USSR are yours to deal with, although the former will likely be dealt with differently than the past Democratic, New Deal administrations. If you stay true and honest to America and help fix those problems, poor Reagan won't know what's waiting for him in 80.

Congratulations! Even though you were the favourite from the start, you could have faltered in several ways. You've carried the will of the country and sent a clear message to those DC insiders. Congratulations! Even though you were the favourite from the start, you could have faltered in several ways. You've carried the will of the country and sent a clear message to those DC insiders. Interestingly enough, Ford ended up winning the popular vote. Republicans are more shocked than angry. Perhaps passing a new version of the Bayh-Celler amendment can be among your reforms?

You still have many options, despite your defeat, as your jolt to the Democrats nomination and the new focus on character in politics will allow you to expand your horizons. While you might not run for president again in four years, a Senate seat in Georgia could suit you very well. Returning to the governor of the state also is possible. Perhaps all the campaigning and stress will inspire you to return to your peanut farm.

The public just didn't think you were up to the task. That's the tradeoff with running a DC outsider like yourself, and the scale tipped in Fords' favour. He will have 4 more years to slash inflation and defend his reputation. He will have to be cautious and show restraint, as you came close to beating him. He with have the public breathing down his neck and Watergate looming over him for his term.

If the Bayh-Celler amendment didn't pass previously, surely the support to pass it will be present now?

Perhaps he might extend an olive branch to you as you did to the conservatives this election, and consider you for his vice presidency?

The year is 1984

Jimmy Carter has been president for 8 years. Inflation has subsided to a steady amount, with unemployment dropping to virtually 0%. The budget had been balanced in 78, and poverty and hunger have been eradicated, as everyone unemployed became a farmer, and is eating peanut butter and peach jam sandwiches. the USSR on the 21st of January had seceded all their land to the USA and declared their government dissolved. Most importantly of all, the government is now trusted more than ever under the leadership of Jimmy Carter, who beat up Richard Nixon on live TV in 1981, garnering a 99% approval rating. Mondale has already won the most recent election 873 electoral votes to 0 against those sorry Republicans, who disbanded shortly after. All is good in the world, thanks to our wonderful leader, Jimmy Carter.
Congratulations! You won the 1976 election!

A number of campaign reforms, many to do with finance will likely be enacted in light of Watergate, as the scandal preceding the Checkers speech Nixon gave in 52 is fresh in the minds of many. Other than that, Inflation and the USSR are yours to deal with, although the former will likely be dealt with differently than the past Democratic, New Deal administrations. If you stay true and honest to America and help fix those problems, poor Reagan won't know what's waiting for him in 80.

Congratulations! Even though you were the favourite from the start, you could have faltered in several ways. You've carried the will of the country and sent a clear message to those DC insiders. They'll need to tread carefully, as the impressive turnaround from 72, despite the playboy interview, shows what America thinks of Ol' Dick Nixon's cronies.

Congratulations! Even though you were the favourite from the start, you could have faltered in a number of ways. You've carried the will of the country and sent a clear message to those DC insiders. As expected, your Playboy interview prevented a glorious decimation of the Republicans, but you'll take it, seeing as it could have been worse with the economic recovery.

Congratulations! Even though you were the favourite from the start, you could have faltered in several ways. You've carried the will of the country and sent a clear message to those DC insiders. Many were shocked at the tightness of the election, seeing as the negativity around the GOP and DC in general. Maybe you were TOO honest, Jimmy...
Interestingly enough, Ford ended up winning the popular vote. Republicans are more shocked than angry. Perhaps passing a new version of the Bayh-Celler amendment can be among your reforms?

You still have many options, despite your defeat, as your jolt to the Democrats nomination and the new focus on character in politics will allow you to expand your horizons. While you might not run for president again in four years, a Senate seat in Georgia could suit you very well. Returning to the governor of the state also is possible. Perhaps all the campaigning and stress will inspire you to return to your peanut farm.

The public just didn't think you were up to the task. That's the tradeoff with running a DC outsider like yourself, and the scale tipped in Fords' favour. He will have 4 more years to slash inflation and defend his reputation. He will have to be cautious and show restraint, as you came close to beating him. He with have the public breathing down his neck and Watergate looming over him for his term.

The public just didn't think you were up to the task. That's the tradeoff with running a DC outsider like yourself, and the scale tipped in Fords' favour. The public just didn't think you were up to the task. That's the tradeoff with running a DC outsider like yourself, and the scale tipped in Fords' favour. Lots of Democrats are incredibly angered that you could lose by such a margin, and are accusing you of throwing away the presidency with a single interview.

If it wasn't already bad enough for you, the popular votes ended up going in your favour. The public and the Democrats are enraged and in despair, as the will of the people to remove the man who pardon Nixon failed. If the Bayh-Celler amendment didn't pass previously, surely the support to pass it will be present now?

Your quick thrusting into the political limelight and downfall was certainly dramatic. It's up to you what you do next. Perhaps a return to the house, although maybe not in a leadership role. A run in fours years is unlikely with Reagan and his coalition ready to nominate him. Perhaps he might extend an olive branch to you as you did to the conservatives this election, and consider you for his vice presidency?

Despite your best efforts, Jimmy Carter has bested you, making you the only president never elected to office. The toll of Watergate and Vietnam was just too much for you to handle. The recovering economy, however, made this election quite close, so you can take solace in the fact that you went down swinging.

Despite your best efforts, Jimmy Carter has bested you, making you the only president never elected to office. The toll of Watergate and Vietnam was just too much for you to handle. America showed they wanted an outsider, and Carter managed to take that title. Let's hope he can help restore faith in government, and help the inflation die down.

Despite your best efforts, Jimmy Carter has bested you, making you the only president never elected to office. The toll of Watergate and Vietnam was just too much for you to handle. Wow! Defying the odds, you have beaten back the Democrats to secure yet another term for your party. After the Watergate pardon, most thought you were done for, but you proved them wrong. You won by a quite shocking margin. It seems your rose garden strategy worked well.

Wow! Defying the odds, you have beaten back the Democrats to secure yet another term for your party. After the Watergate pardon, most thought you were done for, but you proved them wrong. You barely squeaked by, however. Carter gave you a run for your money, and congress isn't too friendly towards you either, so you better tread carefully.

You can hopefully expand upon the recovery from stagflation in your second term, and hopefully bring honour back to the white house. It won't be an easy feat with your pardon, but America wants to give you a chance. Do well and you might be remembered for more than Nixon's pardon.

What is your opinion on abortion, and specifically the recent Roe v. Wade decision?

Order!

Richard M Nixon, how do you plead on 1 count of treason against the United States of America, 1 count of misappropriation of campaign funds, 1 count of obstruction of justice, one count of abuse of power, one count of…

Richard Nixon, as he heard all this droning from the judge, closed his eyes, waiting for the sentence to end. He had been up all night, unable to sleep due to all the stress from the trial.
