description.source: Congratulations! You have won the 1964 Republican nomination for President! As you take the stage to cheers and applause from one side of the floor- and stony silence from the other- what will you touch on in your acceptance speech?
In your acceptance speech at the 1964 Republican National Convention, you said 'And may I remind you that extremism in the defense of liberty is no vice.' What did you mean by that?
An embarrassing gaffe has hit papers all over the country- Goldwater suggests the use of nuclear weapons in Vietnam!
Why did you pick Bill Miller as your running mate?
A new wave of attack ads have gone out across the nation, highlighting Johnson’s involvement with Bobby Baker and Bill Sol Estes.
Your nomination has scared off moderates in the Republican Party, with several Republicans such as George Romney and Nelson Rockefeller refusing to endorse you. How will you unite your party?
Your civil rights position is the most controversial part of your campaign. Would you like to clarify your position to help ease the fears of Southern Democrats or Northern moderates?

Lyndon Johnson has aired an ad depicting a little girl picking flowers, followed by the sound of a nuclear countdown. This ad, known as the ‘Daisy’ ad, is causing much trouble for the Goldwater campaign.

Dwight D. Eisenhower is a very popular figure in the Midwest and Plains, but not as popular in the South. You’ve recently filmed a television ad appearing with Eisenhower. Where and how frequently would you like to air this ad?

Lyndon Johnson has attacked our record on social security greatly, even running an ad where our own running mate Bill Miller says we wish to destroy the social security system! How should we fight back against these ads?
Hubert Humphrey is another weakspot of Lyndon Johnson's, we could try to attack his running mate to gain an edge in the poll to hopefully swing more conservative-aligned moderates to our side.
Another day, another speech. What will you say today on the campaign trail?
There's been a lot of talk from your camp about cutting spending to reduce the growing inflation, what programs would you have in mind?
Goldwater has received an endorsement from the leader of the Alabama Ku Klux Klan. LBJ has already capitalized with attack ads going out nationwide. What should we do?
Would you appoint federal judges who support the decision Engel v. Vitale outlawing mandatory school prayer?
If elected as President, what would you do to lower the inflation rate in this country, which currently stands at over 4%?
Goldwater has been seen as the candidate of the John Birch Society, a fervent group of anti-communist conspiracy theorists. What should we do about this?

Having recently received endorsements from the Ku Klux Klan and the John Birch Society, you need to find a way to distance yourself from extremists and put yourself into the American political mainstream.

Today, famous South Carolinian and 1948 Dixiecrat candidate Strom Thurmond has officially switched his party affiliation from Democratic to Republican, an expected move after his endorsement of Barry Goldwater for President.

Nikita Khrushchev, Premier of the Soviet Union, has been overthrown by Leonid Brezhnev! This has hurt the Goldwater campaign, which has been using belligerent quotes from Khrushchev to gather votes from foreign policy minded voters.
What is your opinion of the military draft that is currently in place?
Famous actor Ronald Reagan has given a long speech in support of Barry Goldwater in California. The speech, immediately popular nationwide, has been dubbed ‘A Time For Choosing.’
Vermont and Indiana are key states for any Republican to win. Would you like to put campaign efforts into winning these states?
The 1964 Campaign is drawing to a close, and chances don’t look good for Goldwater’s success. Are there any last minute statements you’d like to make to win voters over?
Where would you like to campaign on the last day before election day?
Let it be known that I side with the states on the civil rights issue. I will not change this.

I would like to clarify in regards to the Civil Rights Act of 1964. Despite my vote against the bill, I will uphold it as President. I would like to see it repealed- I still believe it is unconstitutional- but a President cannot ignore laws that he dislikes.

I would like to change my previous position. With the passage of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, I shall make no attempt to remove this law, but I will oppose further legislation, such as mass busing or forced integration.
Bill Miller is a devout Catholic, a good man, and he has served New York with honor and distinction.
Miller and I agree on just about everything. I chose him because I believe we represent the future of this country.
We need to emphasize that Humphrey and Johnson are nothing but socialists and puppets of big union bosses.
There may be differences between our wings of the party, but we must remember that we are all Republicans, and we stand united in our common goals.

We need to make sure that our military is adequately filled with personnel. That being said, I would prefer to see a volunteer system in place. I'm confident that there are enough patriotic young men in this country to make that system work.
The draft is evil and should be abolished. We would never need it in the first place if warmongers like Johnson hadn't gotten us into this mess over in Vietnam.
Ike is too popular not to have this playing in every household.
Limit this ad to the Plains and Midwest. Ike enjoys the most popularity there.
Damn those TV ads!
We need to double-down on the states rights issue. Our only hope of victory is through the South.
Social Security is a winning issue. In these final days, we must expose Johnson’s lies about our opinion on the subject, and turn the tables back on him.
I would like to remind civil rights conscious voters that I was fighting for civil rights long before they were popular, as well as helping found the Arizona Chapter of the NAACP.
We need whoever we can get.
Goddamn it.
Hubert Humphrey is an extremist and a socialist. We cannot let this man be one heartbeat away from the Presidency.
We should avoid talking about Humphrey. It’s in poor taste.
Want to know who's at fault for this Civil Rights Act? It's Hubert Horatio Humphrey.
Goldwater’s record on Social Security has always been in support of the program. This is dirty politics from Johnson.
We need to clarify- Goldwater only advocates reforming Social Security into a voluntary program.
Let’s counter-attack Johnson on the inflation issue. This hurts the Social Security program more than anything I’ve proposed.
This decision was atrocious. I don't think it's an exaggeration to say that our way of life is at stake here when we don't allow our schools to teach basic moral values to our children.
I was disappointed with this decision. I would certainly appoint judges who see the wisdom in teaching our kids a few lessons about morality.

We have Catholics, Jews, and others in this country who should not be forced to pray in a certain way because of what some principal believes in a public school. This is a First Amendment issue in my opinion.
I will appoint judges who support religious freedom in the United States. Absolutely.
We should talk about states rights' and the Democrats plan to destroy the 10th amendment.
Let us talk about fiscal conservatism and our plans to reduce inflation.
Johnson’s weak point is the Bobby Baker case. Let’s talk about Baker and Billy Sol Estes.
Our inflation is being caused by all of this Great Society nonsense that Johnson passed. I will slash these programs, slash our deficits, and end our inflation problem overnight.

The inflation rate we have in this country speaks to the heart of the Democrats' problems in running the economy. They claim to be the party of the working man, but they are fine with debasing wages and property values with their misguided social engineering.

Right now we have the strongest economy almost in the history of the United States. Unemployment is at 3% and our national output is growing at a furious pace. Compared to this, our 4% inflation rate is a pretty minor concern.

The Republicans are grasping at straws with this inflation argument. They know that Kennedy and Johnson have managed the economy far better than Eisenhower, so they are resorting to the only argument they have left.
I don’t believe we have a good chance at these two states, but I would like to put effort into winning New Hampshire. We had a great primary showing there.
These states have to be won to win the election.
I’d rather put effort into winning the South. Vermont and Indiana are hopeless.
Put out a magazine article denouncing all these crazy conspiracies, but don't mention the Birchers by name.
We reject Bircherism. Make that an official statement.
We need their votes. We cannot risk denouncing the group in any way.
First and foremost, cuts will be in foreign aid.
For too long, farmers have been stopped from participating properly in the free market. Cutting their subsidies will benefit both the budget and the farmers.
I’m not sure. Maybe everywhere, really.
I want to remain silent on this.
These groups have a right to free speech, but Goldwater is neither a Klan member nor a Bircher.
We need to reject this endorsement right away.
I hate to admit it, but we need whatever support we can get. Keep quiet on this.
What does it sound like I said? We need extreme solutions to extreme problems.
Does a person not love their country extremely? Do people not believe in their God extremely? I hold my convictions extremely and I hope all that vote for us in November do too.
By the word extremism, I simply meant patriotism. This is just one big misunderstanding.

We'll need to pivot left somewhat if we want to cut in on Johnson's majority. By promising to respect the Civil Rights Act and highlighting our own forwardness on the issue, we can assuage liberal fears.
If we want a chance to get back in this fight, we need the moderates on board. Our speech will be on unity and strength in the party as much as it is about my ideals.

I've been the candidate of the conservatives this entire campaign, and I won't change that here. We're going to hit home on fiscal responsibility, tax breaks, escalation in Vietnam- red meat for our base.
'Barry Goldwater thinks we can.'
Let’s campaign in the border states- Arkansas, Tennessee, and North Carolina.
Let’s campaign in the Plains. We have a real shot there.
One final round trip- Vermont, New Hampshire, and Indiana!
We can win California. Put all efforts into that state.

We need to find a way to shut me up!

I will bring new, dynamic leadership to this country as President. I don't see how this line of argument puts me at any disadvantage.
This program is a good starting point, but I would much prefer a program of national health insurance for all Americans -- not just the elderly.

This program would represent a massive new financial commitment for the federal government, when care of the elderly properly rests with the affected family.
We need to dispatch an armed garrison to these islands, to make sure there is no mistaking our commitment in our fight against Communism.

I'm not sure it's practical or desirable from a military standpoint to defend two tiny islands that are much closer to the Chinese mainland than they are to Formosa.
I am satisfied with our progress over the past few years. We have prevented further expansion while avoiding any major wars.
We can never be fully satisfied, but we have certainly held our own in the Cold War over the past eight years, compared to where we were during the Korean War.
Cuba has been lost to the Soviet Union, providing a potential base for Communist aggression on the very doorstep of our nation. I am very unsatisfied with the current situation.
I am as satisfied as I can be. With sound defense policies and strong economic growth, we should continue to maintain our advantage over the Soviet Union.
I don't know, to be perfectly frank. Things are going well for now, but we will have many challenges to meet in places like Cuba, Lebanon, Latin America, Indochina, and elsewhere.

We have a missile gap, and an overly tight monetary policy that is constraining our growth. I'm very concerned that these shortfalls will allow the Soviet Union to gain an advantage if they are not addressed.
Education is a key front in our battle with Communism, and that includes adequate pay and respect for our nation's teachers. I would support additional federal spending on this.
I'm not satisfied with how well teachers are paid in this country, and I'd encourage local jurisdictions to address this issue further. We need to strike a good balance in this regard.
We need to minimize the federal funding of education, even in block grants. It could easily open the door to federal control of our schools.
We need to do anything we can to move our nation forward on this issue, including a civil rights bill and measures to protect voting rights.
I am supportive of a civil rights bill and will work with Congress to get one written and passed.
This is something that is more appropriately addressed by individual states, though I will do anything I can to enforce the decisions of our Supreme Court.
I would not support a measure like this. This would be an unnecessary and unconstitutional interference into the rights of our states.
Let's make a call to Mrs. King to offer our condolences, and let's demand the release of Mr. King.

We are on the right track economically. We can't deny that there was a recession in 1958, but the recovery has been strong and 1960 will see a very high rate of growth in this country.

We should always be concerned about internal subversion, but the external Soviet threat should be our primary focus at this point.
It's unfortunate that we've become less vigilant on the internal Communist threat in recent years. Espionage and infiltration of our government is as serious a threat as external Soviet action.
We've seen some alarming things out of Cuba, but this isn't necessarily a lost cause. Cuba has not declared itself a Communist state and we should be making overtures to prevent that.
We will defend our base at Guantanamo and do anything else that is necessary if Cuba continues its hostility. However, it is too early to make a conclusive determination at this point.

What we've unfortunately seen in Cuba is the consequence of insufficient support for anti-Communist governments and movements. We need to be much more aggressive in our actions against the Castro government.
We lost a lot of ground diplomatically after this event, and much of that could have been avoided had we issued a formal apology.
A formal apology sounds a bit extreme, but we could certainly have expressed our regrets and perhaps saved the Paris Summit from collapse.
Absolutely not. We cannot show weakness in the face of the Soviet threat, and the Paris Summit collapsed from the intransigence of Nikita Khrushchev.
He absolutely did, and I would like to see further action to desegregate our schools and enforce our civil rights.
I believe that Eisenhower did what he had to do in this case, to make sure the decisions of our Supreme Court are enforced.
We should have found a better way to resolve this issue, rather than intrude into the sovereignty of an American state.
We need to make sure we don't overextend ourselves into new regions when the situation does not warrant it.
This is a situation that we need to watch carefully, and I am open to a variety of measures if necessary.
I believe we need to defend South Vietnam at all costs, whatever commitment of our forces that entails.
I would support the use of massive air strikes or tactical nuclear weapons to defend our ally, South Vietnam.

We should be vigilant against labor union excesses, and the Taft-Hartley Act was a good start. I believe that we should keep that law in place.
We need to do anything we can to reduce the power of labor unions in this country, including a national right-to-work law.
I believe that we need more vigilance in the area of defense, for both military equipment and for missile development. We currently have a missile gap with the Soviet Union.

In the final analysis, every dollar spent on defense is taken from more productive uses within our economy. I will look for ways to find common ground with the Soviet Union so that we can cut defense spending.

description.source: What kind of tone will you attempt to set in your campaign this fall?
What do you have to say about the selection of Stuart Symington as your running mate?
Are you satisfied with the economy and the economic policies of this country over the past eight years?
There was a recent effort in Congress to pass a program to provide medical care to elderly Americans, but it was narrowly defeated. Will you make a further push for this type of program as President?
Do you believe that current levels of defense spending are adequate?
Is the United States adequately prepared to defend against the Soviet threat today?
Do you believe the United States is adequately prepared to defend against the Soviet threat over the next ten years?
Richard Nixon has made "experience" the centerpiece of his campaign. What do you have to say on this point?
Anti-Catholicism has been a huge issue thus far in the campaign, with hundreds of pamphlets and leaflets being distributed across the South and Midwest. Do you have any comment?
Did Dwight Eisenhower do the right thing when he sent federal troops to Little Rock to ensure the integration of the high school there?
Should the United States apologize to the Soviet Union for the controversy surrounding the downed U-2 spy plane and surrounding espionage?

There have been a large number of sit-ins recently, where black students and activists are sitting at whites-only lunch counters and department stores to advocate for desegregation. Do you support this movement?

Anti-Catholicism continues to be an issue. Major newspapers have published a statement by 150 Protestant clergy, including Norman Vincent Peale, opposing any Catholic as President. Do you have any comment?
There has been a proposal for a series of television debates between you and Kennedy. Is this something you are interested in?
Do you support a minimum wage of $1.25 per hour, with some exceptions for small business? Such a measure was recently defeated in Congress.

During the Great Depression, the federal government began a policy of farm subsidies to stabilize farm incomes and to target a specific output of each crop. Are these policies still necessary in 1960?
Has the United States adequately defended against the Communist threat in Indochina? Would you support further action there if necessary?
Do you believe that the islands of Quemoy and Matsu should fall within the United States defense perimeter in Asia?
How serious, at the current time, do you believe the internal Communist threat is?
Would you support the passage of a federal civil rights bill as President to address the worst excesses of segregation in the South?
What would you do as President to combat increasing unemployment in America's industrial cities?
What is your opinion on the current level of education funding in the United States? Would you increase federal education funding, even if it meant higher taxes or a larger budget deficit?
Do you believe that Cuba has been lost to the Communists as of this time? If so, do you think it is partially the fault of the United States?

Recently, Martin Luther King Jr. was arrested at a sit-in in Atlanta, and has now been sentenced to four months in prison for failing to get a Georgia driver's license after moving to that state. Do you have any comment or action you would like to take?
Where will you spend your final day before the election?
I will campaign as a mainstream liberal Democrat, emphasizing key parts of our platform and pressing the case for more vigilance in our national defense.
I have always been on the more moderate wing of the party. We need to emphasize my anti-Communism and my record as a Senator if we hope to win back the Eisenhower Democrats.
It is important to keep the Democratic Party moving into the future. We need to act on civil rights, education, and health care over the coming term.

I will deemphasize the political aspect of this campaign, as much as practicable, and emphasize my own personality and leadership ability. Of course I will still make strong statements on the Cold War.
Stuart Symington is a close friend of mine and a tireless advocate for liberalism in the United States. I look forward to working with him for the next four years.
Stuart Symington has served his home state of Missouri well for many years, as Harry Truman himself has noted, and is a staunch Democrat.
Let's be cautious with this idea. Nixon is a skilled debater, and the last thing we need right now is a campaign setback on national television.
I would love to go against Nixon in a televised debate. We could use the exposure and I'm confident that I would win.

Let's gather some of these leaflets and show them to the media and to major newspapers. I think they demonstrate the lengths that some people will go to discredit my candidacy.
I will attack the idea that any good Protestant would vote against my candidacy because I happen to be a Catholic.
We can't be out there responding to every little two-bit leaflet that some crank puts out. Let's wait and see how this issue develops.
Let's take this opportunity to make a major speech on the topic. I will address this issue exclusively in a televised speech, and put it to rest for good.
Let's put a couple of statements into my next campaign speech to address this issue, and reassure the public that I take no orders from the Pope.
I am Catholic and proud of it. I will not respond to bigoted attacks or innuendo, and I trust that these attacks will only help me by driving higher Catholic turnout.
This movement has my full support, as do the other civil rights measures of our day. I will push for a Civil Rights Act as President.
I support the civil rights movement, but I'm a little concerned about the disregard for the law that some of these activists have shown.

Richard Nixon and I entered Congress in the same year, 1947, and have both served in the highest levels of government for some time.
I question this premise, to be frank. It's still not clear to me exactly what role Nixon had in the Eisenhower Administration, or what policies of his have been implemented.
I will bring new, dynamic leadership to this country as President. I don't see how this line of argument puts me at any disadvantage.
This program is a good starting point, but I would much prefer a program of national health insurance for all Americans -- not just the elderly.
I would redouble our efforts on this front. Too many of our nation's elderly are unable to afford decent medical care in their advanced years.

I prefer a slightly different program, offering health insurance to the elderly that they can choose to purchase. The proposed program was mandatory, and also covered only those covered by the Social Security Act.
This program would represent a massive new financial commitment for the federal government, when care of the elderly properly rests with the affected family.
We need to dispatch an armed garrison to these islands, to make sure there is no mistaking our commitment in our fight against Communism.
I do believe we should defend these islands. We are committed to the defense of Taiwan, and that commitment must include all of Taiwan to be credible.
It wouldn't be responsible of me to comment at this point. As President I will consult with our military leaders to determine what is appropriate.
I'm not sure it's practical or desirable from a military standpoint to defend two tiny islands that are much closer to the Chinese mainland than they are to Formosa.
I am satisfied with our progress over the past few years. We have prevented further expansion while avoiding any major wars.
We can never be fully satisfied, but we have certainly held our own in the Cold War over the past eight years, compared to where we were during the Korean War.
Cuba has been lost to the Soviet Union, providing a potential base for Communist aggression on the very doorstep of our nation. I am very unsatisfied with the current situation.
I am as satisfied as I can be. With sound defense policies and strong economic growth, we should continue to maintain our advantage over the Soviet Union.
I don't know, to be perfectly frank. Things are going well for now, but we will have many challenges to meet in places like Cuba, Lebanon, Latin America, Indochina, and elsewhere.

We have a missile gap, and an overly tight monetary policy that is constraining our growth. I'm very concerned that these shortfalls will allow the Soviet Union to gain an advantage if they are not addressed.
We have too much of a farm surplus right now, and we need to reduce subsidies for production so that prices can fall into balance and benefit the consumer.
I think these programs need to be phased out over time, but in such a way that we don't bring sudden instability to our nation's farm policy.
They are absolutely necessary. Farmers are not in a good position to bargain for their crops, and any economic weakness in that sector can easily cause a recession in the broader economy.
Education is a key front in our battle with Communism, and that includes adequate pay and respect for our nation's teachers. I would support additional federal spending on this.
I'm not satisfied with how well teachers are paid in this country, and I'd encourage local jurisdictions to address this issue further. We need to strike a good balance in this regard.
We need to minimize the federal funding of education, even in block grants. It could easily open the door to federal control of our schools.
We need to do anything we can to move our nation forward on this issue, including a civil rights bill and measures to protect voting rights.
I am supportive of a civil rights bill and will work with Congress to get one written and passed.
This is something that is more appropriately addressed by individual states, though I will do anything I can to enforce the decisions of our Supreme Court.
I would not support a measure like this. This would be an unnecessary and unconstitutional interference into the rights of our states.
Let's make a call to Mrs. King to offer our condolences, and let's demand the release of Mr. King.
Let's make a public comment criticizing this arrest, and expressing our hopes that this situation doesn't escalate any further.
I will give a statement encouraging the State of Georgia to protect the safety of Mr. King, while criticizing him for participating in these inflammatory and illegal protests.
We need more spending and lower interest rates, and we need to repeal the Taft-Hartley Act and put more money into the hands of the American people.
We must do better. Our present Administration has advocated a hard money policy which caused the recession of 1958 and left idle industrial capacity in our country.
We are on the right track economically. We can't deny that there was a recession in 1958, but the recovery has been strong and 1960 will see a very high rate of growth in this country.
The Eisenhower Administration has unfortunately failed to take any real action in undoing the excesses of the New Deal. I would like to see a more conservative Administration in power.
I support this measure, and believe it would be greatly beneficial to millions of American workers.
Our current minimum wage is sufficient in my opinion. The minimum wage is a necessary expedient but we shouldn't be increasing it so much that we cause unemployment.
I believe a minimum wage is at the very least a bad economic idea, and possibly unconstitutional. I do not support this increase.
The last thing we need is a return to excesses and witch-hunts of the early 1950s. We need to keep ourselves focused on the external Communist threat.
We should always be concerned about internal subversion, but the external Soviet threat should be our primary focus at this point.
It's unfortunate that we've become less vigilant on the internal Communist threat in recent years. Espionage and infiltration of our government is as serious a threat as external Soviet action.
We've seen some alarming things out of Cuba, but this isn't necessarily a lost cause. Cuba has not declared itself a Communist state and we should be making overtures to prevent that.
We will defend our base at Guantanamo and do anything else that is necessary if Cuba continues its hostility. However, it is too early to make a conclusive determination at this point.

What we've unfortunately seen in Cuba is the consequence of insufficient support for anti-Communist governments and movements. We need to be much more aggressive in our actions against the Castro government.
We lost a lot of ground diplomatically after this event, and much of that could have been avoided had we issued a formal apology.
A formal apology sounds a bit extreme, but we could certainly have expressed our regrets and perhaps saved the Paris Summit from collapse.
Absolutely not. We cannot show weakness in the face of the Soviet threat, and the Paris Summit collapsed from the intransigence of Nikita Khrushchev.
He absolutely did, and I would like to see further action to desegregate our schools and enforce our civil rights.
I believe that Eisenhower did what he had to do in this case, to make sure the decisions of our Supreme Court are enforced.
We should have found a better way to resolve this issue, rather than intrude into the sovereignty of an American state.
We need more spending and should consider lower taxes to stimulate American economy and industry.
We need to strengthen our labor unions and protections for the nation's industry, including trade protections if necessary.
If we continue our current economic policies, the economy should continue to recover into the 1960s and we will see a rebound in our employment rate.
We need lower taxes, fewer regulations, and a smaller federal government. This will encourage private enterprise and spur a recovery to our industrial capacity.
We need to make sure we don't overextend ourselves into new regions when the situation does not warrant it.
This is a situation that we need to watch carefully, and I am open to a variety of measures if necessary.
I believe we need to defend South Vietnam at all costs, whatever commitment of our forces that entails.
I would support the use of massive air strikes or tactical nuclear weapons to defend our ally, South Vietnam.
I believe that we need more vigilance in the area of defense, for both military equipment and for missile development. We currently have a missile gap with the Soviet Union.
We can always find areas for improvement, but we have successfully defended the United States and our allies from numerous Communist threats over the past eight years.

In the final analysis, every dollar spent on defense is taken from more productive uses within our economy. I will look for ways to find common ground with the Soviet Union so that we can cut defense spending.
We will campaign up and down New York and the Eastern Seaboard.
We will focus on the Midwest.
We will travel to California and the West Coast.
We will focus on Texas and the South.

description.source: What kind of tone will you attempt to set in your campaign this fall?
What do you have to say about the selection of Everett Dirksen as your running mate?
Are you satisfied with the economy and the economic policies of this country over the past eight years?
There was a recent effort in Congress to pass a program to provide medical care to elderly Americans, but it was narrowly defeated. Will you make a further push for this type of program as President?
Do you believe that current levels of defense spending are adequate?
Is the United States adequately prepared to defend against the Soviet threat today?
Do you believe the United States is adequately prepared to defend against the Soviet threat over the next ten years?
To what extent will you make your experience as Vice President a theme of your campaign against the youthful Kennedy?
Southern Republicans are insisting that you visit their region extensively during this campaign, claiming that Kennedy will be vulnerable in some states. What are your thoughts?
Anti-Catholicism has been a huge issue thus far in the campaign, with hundreds of pamphlets and leaflets being distributed across the South and Midwest. Do you have any comment?

There have been a large number of sit-ins recently, where black students and activists are sitting at whites-only lunch counters and department stores to advocate for desegregation. Do you support this movement?
Did Dwight Eisenhower do the right thing when he sent federal troops to Little Rock to ensure the integration of the high school there?
Should the United States apologize to the Soviet Union for the controversy surrounding the downed U-2 spy plane and surrounding espionage?

Anti-Catholicism continues to be an issue. Major newspapers have published a statement by 150 Protestant clergy, including Norman Vincent Peale, opposing any Catholic as President. Do you have any comment?
There has been a proposal for a series of television debates between you and Kennedy. Is this something you are interested in?
Would you support the passage of a federal civil rights bill as President to address the worst excesses of segregation in the South?
What would you do as President to combat increasing unemployment in America's industrial cities?
Currently the highest income tax bracket pays a rate of 91%. Will you work harder to cut tax rates as President?

During the Great Depression, the federal government began a policy of farm subsidies to stabilize farm incomes and to target a specific output of each crop. Are these policies still necessary in 1960?
What is your opinion on the current level of education funding in the United States? Would you increase federal education funding, even if it meant higher taxes or a larger budget deficit?
What is your position on the power of labor unions in the United States?
Do you believe that the islands of Quemoy and Matsu should fall within the United States defense perimeter in Asia?

Recently, Martin Luther King Jr. was arrested at a sit-in in Atlanta, and has now been sentenced to four months in prison for failing to get a Georgia driver's license after moving to that state. Do you have any comment or action you would like to take?
Eisenhower has his own responsibilities as President, but he is able to hit the trail for the last week of the campaign. He will obviously provide a huge boost wherever he appears. What do you think?
Where will you spend your final day before the election?
I want Eisenhower to focus on the Midwest.
I want Eisenhower to travel to California and the West Coast.

I will pledge, as much as possible, to continue the policies of Dwight Eisenhower when I am President. I will also emphasize my experience in Eisenhower's Administration, particularly in world affairs.
I will praise the leadership of Eisenhower, but emphasize to concerned Republicans that I will be a more orthodox conservative when I am President.
It is important to keep the Republican Party moving into the future. We need to act on civil rights, education, and health care over the coming term.

I will deemphasize the political aspect of this campaign, as much as practicable, and emphasize my own personality and leadership ability. Of course I will still make strong statements on the Cold War.
Everett Dirksen has served the state of Illinois admirably during his time in the U.S. Senate, and I'm proud to have him on my ticket.
Everett Dirksen is a mainstream Republican who represents the direction that our party should take moving forward.
This movement has my full support, as do the other civil rights measures of our day. I will push for a Civil Rights Act as President.
I support the civil rights movement, but I'm a little concerned about the disregard for the law that some of these activists have shown.
These activists are trespassing on the property of lawful businesses. I think there are better methods of pushing for change in the South.
I think our best chance this year will come from winning the Midwest and Northeast. I can't make any promises about visiting the South.
I agree. We can definitely split the South if we make a strong play for it this year. I will visit extensively.
There are too many competitive states around the nation. To keep our entire party engaged, I pledge to visit all 50 states during this campaign.
I can't make promises in advance about where I will or won't visit.
I want Eisenhower to plant himself in New York, and to stay there until election day. That state is too important to take chances with.
I want Eisenhower to campaign up and down the Eastern Seaboard.
Let's be honest with ourselves. Kennedy is great on television and he did very well debating Hubert Humphrey in the primaries. We should probably avoid this.
I've been a champion debater for my entire life. I'd be happy to go against Kennedy on TV.
I've been a champion debater for my entire life. I'd be happy to go against Kennedy on TV.
I've been a champion debater for my entire life. I'd be happy to go against Kennedy on TV.
Honestly, I'd rather that people didn't bring this issue up. People know that Kennedy is Catholic, and this can only galvanize his support from that sector.
I wouldn't go to these extremes, but anyone should be concerned about a President who is forced to follow the dictates of the Pope.
Not particularly. Our campaign would prefer to move on to other issues to be perfectly honest.
Again, I'd have to say that this is a valid concern. This would set a dangerous precedent for the independence of our nation's executive.
This needs to be a key centerpiece of our campaign. Our current President is widely popular, and I can easily make the case that I was a central part of his Administration.
I think there are better themes to touch on. Let's focus on our plans for national defense and economic growth, and also focus more on Kennedy's inexperience.
This program is a good starting point, but I would much prefer a program of national health insurance for all Americans -- not just the elderly.
I would redouble our efforts on this front. Too many of our nation's elderly are unable to afford decent medical care in their advanced years.

I prefer a slightly different program, offering health insurance to the elderly that they can choose to purchase. The proposed program was mandatory, and also covered only those covered by the Social Security Act.
This program would represent a massive new financial commitment for the federal government, when care of the elderly properly rests with the affected family.
We need to dispatch an armed garrison to these islands, to make sure there is no mistaking our commitment in our fight against Communism.
I do believe we should defend these islands. We are committed to the defense of Taiwan, and that commitment must include all of Taiwan to be credible.
It wouldn't be responsible of me to comment at this point. As President I will consult with our military leaders to determine what is appropriate.
I'm not sure it's practical or desirable from a military standpoint to defend two tiny islands that are much closer to the Chinese mainland than they are to Formosa.
This is not a high priority for me as President. We need to create an old age insurance program and increase our funding for education.
I would be open to this, depending on how the economy goes in the next year or two.
We need to cut this rate substantially. It is way too high.
I am satisfied with our progress over the past few years. We have prevented further expansion while avoiding any major wars.
We can never be fully satisfied, but we have certainly held our own in the Cold War over the past eight years, compared to where we were during the Korean War.
Cuba has been lost to the Soviet Union, providing a potential base for Communist aggression on the very doorstep of our nation. I am very unsatisfied with the current situation.
I am as satisfied as I can be. With sound defense policies and strong economic growth, we should continue to maintain our advantage over the Soviet Union.
I don't know, to be perfectly frank. Things are going well for now, but we will have many challenges to meet in places like Cuba, Lebanon, Latin America, Indochina, and elsewhere.

We have a missile gap, and an overly tight monetary policy that is constraining our growth. I'm very concerned that these shortfalls will allow the Soviet Union to gain an advantage if they are not addressed.
We have too much of a farm surplus right now, and we need to reduce subsidies for production so that prices can fall into balance and benefit the consumer.
I think these programs need to be phased out over time, but in such a way that we don't bring sudden instability to our nation's farm policy.
They are absolutely necessary. Farmers are not in a good position to bargain for their crops, and any economic weakness in that sector can easily cause a recession in the broader economy.
Education is a key front in our battle with Communism, and that includes adequate pay and respect for our nation's teachers. I would support additional federal spending on this.
I'm not satisfied with how well teachers are paid in this country, and I'd encourage local jurisdictions to address this issue further. We need to strike a good balance in this regard.
We need to minimize the federal funding of education, even in block grants. It could easily open the door to federal control of our schools.
We need to do anything we can to move our nation forward on this issue, including a civil rights bill and measures to protect voting rights.
I am supportive of a civil rights bill and will work with Congress to get one written and passed.
This is something that is more appropriately addressed by individual states, though I will do anything I can to enforce the decisions of our Supreme Court.
I would not support a measure like this. This would be an unnecessary and unconstitutional interference into the rights of our states.
Let's make a call to Mrs. King to offer our condolences, and let's demand the release of Mr. King.
Let's make a public comment criticizing this arrest, and expressing our hopes that this situation doesn't escalate any further.
I will give a statement encouraging the State of Georgia to protect the safety of Mr. King, while criticizing him for participating in these inflammatory and illegal protests.
We need more spending and lower interest rates, and we need to repeal the Taft-Hartley Act and put more money into the hands of the American people.
We must do better. Our present Administration has advocated a hard money policy which caused the recession of 1958 and left idle industrial capacity in our country.
We are on the right track economically. We can't deny that there was a recession in 1958, but the recovery has been strong and 1960 will see a very high rate of growth in this country.
The Eisenhower Administration has unfortunately failed to take any real action in undoing the excesses of the New Deal. I would like to see a more conservative Administration in power.
We lost a lot of ground diplomatically after this event, and much of that could have been avoided had we issued a formal apology.
A formal apology sounds a bit extreme, but we could certainly have expressed our regrets and perhaps saved the Paris Summit from collapse.
Absolutely not. We cannot show weakness in the face of the Soviet threat, and the Paris Summit collapsed from the intransigence of Nikita Khrushchev.
He absolutely did, and I would like to see further action to desegregate our schools and enforce our civil rights.
I believe that Eisenhower did what he had to do in this case, to make sure the decisions of our Supreme Court are enforced.
We should have found a better way to resolve this issue, rather than intrude into the sovereignty of an American state.
We need more spending and should consider lower taxes to stimulate American economy and industry.
We need to strengthen our labor unions and protections for the nation's industry, including trade protections if necessary.
If we continue our current economic policies, the economy should continue to recover into the 1960s and we will see a rebound in our employment rate.
We need lower taxes, fewer regulations, and a smaller federal government. This will encourage private enterprise and spur a recovery to our industrial capacity.
Labor unions have been needlessly undermined by the Taft-Hartley Act, and by self-serving investigations from both parties. I will do anything I can as President to support our nation's laborers.
I support unions and I oppose the excesses of leaders such as Jimmy Hoffa. Unions, cleansed of their corrupt elements, should play a central role in the American economy.
We should be vigilant against labor union excesses, and the Taft-Hartley Act was a good start. I believe that we should keep that law in place.
We need to do anything we can to reduce the power of labor unions in this country, including a national right-to-work law.
I believe that we need more vigilance in the area of defense, for both military equipment and for missile development. We currently have a missile gap with the Soviet Union.
We can always find areas for improvement, but we have successfully defended the United States and our allies from numerous Communist threats over the past eight years.

In the final analysis, every dollar spent on defense is taken from more productive uses within our economy. I will look for ways to find common ground with the Soviet Union so that we can cut defense spending.
We will campaign up and down New York and the Eastern Seaboard.
We will focus on the Midwest.
We will travel to California and the West Coast.
We will focus on Texas and the South.

description.source: A wave of strikes and economic turmoil has led to bipartisan support for a new labor law. The Taft-Hartley Act, limiting the power of labor unions, has been placed on your desk. Will you sign this bill or veto it?
The Jewish state of Israel is set to declare its independence on May 15, 1948. Will your Administration recognize this new nation?
A young, liberal Senate candidate from Minnesota named Hubert Humphrey is pushing for a civil rights plank in the Democratic platform. You can either encourage this movement or nip it in the bud.
Do you stand by your decision to implement a loyalty program for employees of the federal government? Do you believe that Communist infiltration is a serious threat right now?
The Soviet Union has blocked West Berlin from receiving any supplies from Western Europe. What are your thoughts on this situation?
Is there anything you can say during your acceptance speech at the national convention to shake this race up?
You are making a whistle-stop tour of the country to promote your candidacy. What region will you visit over the next two weeks?
Would you support an act that would allocate federal funds for the construction of low-income housing?

I support this program, but I'm concerned with some of the actions I'm seeing from the FBI and the House Un-American Activities Committee. We need to balance this program with appropriate concern for due process and civil liberties.

We need to go after Thomas Dewey hard. I haven't heard him take a serious stand on any major issue of our time, and this country needs a true leader.
I will pledge to visit every state in the Union before election day. I stand for every working man in this country, and I'll let them know all about it before this is done.

The Republicans are putting out a nice platform, but their own Congress has sandbagged half of these proposals in the past two years alone. I will call Congress into session and make them put their money where their mouth is.

The Marshall Plan is provocative towards the Soviet Union, and is likely to lead to further aggression and escalation from them.

The HUAC is not something I plan to address very much as I campaign.
I'm not very comfortable with the activities of this committee, and I believe they should be scaled back to a minimum.

Corporations have been raising prices much faster than wages have increased, and they are pocketing exorbitant profits as a result. I will fight for the rights of labor, and for better regulation during my next term.

We have already passed the Taft-Hartley Act and a modernized system of price supports for food, and their effect can clearly be seen in the drop in inflation since 1947. I'm confident this trend will continue.

We need to control the spending and interference of the federal government, and reinforce our commitment to a sound American dollar. These policies will bring inflation under control in my Administration.
We need a federal housing bill that will produce low-income housing and provide cheaper mortgages for all Americans, so that we can get more housing built in this country.
We are clearly overcrowding our urban areas at the moment. At the very least, we can expand the federal highway system to make more areas accessible to families and developers.

It has taken a couple of years after the end of the war, but I can already see that many new houses are being built by private developers to resolve this shortage, and I can only predict that this trend will continue without any special action by the government.

Part of our current economic problem is the inability of Congress to pass programs which would help the American worker. I'd rather see us have more housing, more roads, and better health care than to see us with an unnecessary surplus.
I've always been an advocate of “pay-as-you-go liberalism”, as I've put it. I believe that we can pass the programs this country needs without destroying the fiscal health of the government.
We've run up quite a national debt over the past few years, and rightly so, but now that World War II is over, we should focus on paying down this debt.
In the world we live in now, we need to remain vigilant, lest we see the world overwhelmed by Communist expansion. I think this measure is, unfortunately, a necessary one.
You will never see me support the conscription of American boys into the military during peacetime, whether it be in 1940 or in the current time, or in a future time.

The economy would be even better without the obstructionism of Congress, or the excessive profiteering and price-gouging from many companies. But overall, we've seen great prosperity since the end of World War II.

We have 10% inflation, crippling labor issues, and a legacy of overreach dating to the New Deal. I'm not very satisfied at all with our economic situation.

description.source: What do you have to say about your announced running mate, John Bricker?
A wave of strikes and economic turmoil has led to bipartisan support for a new labor law. Do you support Truman's decision to veto the Taft-Hartley Act?
The Jewish state of Israel is set to declare its independence on May 15, 1948. Do you support Truman's decision to recognize this new nation?
To what extent are you prepared to make anti-Communism an issue in this campaign, or to attack Harry Truman on the issue?
To what extent will you emphasize your support for civil rights legislation in New York as you hit the campaign trail?
Do you have any comments to make on the Soviet blockade of Berlin, and the airlift in progress to resupply that city?
What will be the main focus of your acceptance speech at the Republican Convention?
You are making a whistle-stop tour of the country to promote your candidacy. What region will you visit over the next two weeks?
In general, what is your view on the providing of foreign aid to American allies?
Would you support an act that would allocate federal funds for the construction of low-income housing?
What are your views on a federal health insurance program?

Your party has passed a fairly ambitious and liberal platform which you have supported. However, if the Republican Congress won't pass these laws now, how do you expect to push them forward as President?
What are your views on the expansion of Social Security?
Do you support the federal funding of primary education, and if so, in what form?
You are making a whistle-stop tour of the country to promote your candidacy. What region will you visit over the next two weeks?
What are your views, in general, on the Marshall Plan?
Is the House Un-American Activities Committee going too far in its attempts to root out Communist influence, or should it be doing more?
What do you think about the proposed Constitutional Amendment to limit the President to two terms in office?
How will you reduce the inflation rate, currently around 10% annually, if you are elected President?
What will you do to help resolve the severe housing shortage in this country?
You are making a whistle-stop tour of the country to promote your candidacy. What region will you visit over the next two weeks?
What are your views on the current federal budget surplus? Would you attempt to maintain this surplus as President?
What do you have to say about the provision of large-scale military and economic aid to Turkey and Greece, to prevent a Communist takeover in those countries?
You are making a whistle-stop tour of the country to promote your candidacy. What region will you visit over the next two weeks?
Before you head to New York to spend the election day, is there one last place you want to hit on the campaign trail?
I support the HUAC, although I do wish it could be a little more aggressive in its rooting out of Communist influence.
Absolutely not. This is a perfectly reasonable measure, designed to prevent a strike in one industry from crippling the American economy.
I support Truman's veto. The National Labor Relations Act was put in place to protect the rights of labor, and it should be respected.
I've supported the Israeli state from the beginning. I'm glad that Truman came around, but he absolutely sent the wrong message by vacillating on this issue until the very last moment.
I support the Israeli state, and I'm pleased that Truman and I are in agreement on this issue.
I believe it was a hasty and impetuous move by the Truman Administration to support the creation of Israel. I have to come out against this measure.

Not only will I speak about this issue, but I will use it to attack Truman. I've supported civil rights all along, while Truman seems to have come around at the 11th hour, and for transparent political gain.
I think part of any good campaign involves speaking about my past, and as Governor of New York I successfully pushed for some of the first anti-discrimination laws in the country.
My record speaks for itself. For the time being, we just need to keep the party energized and avoid any statements which might be deemed as controversial.
Not only is this a serious issue, but Harry Truman is complicit in it. It is no secret that he is, along with most Democrats, complacent on the issue of Communist infiltration.
I think there are legitimate questions to be asked about how much the Communists have embedded themselves into departments of the government. I support the measures we have in place to combat this.
If you'll remember my debate with Harold Stassen, I got this nomination in the first place by remaining above such type of politics.
I would have us move into East Germany if this blockade continues. We're the ones with a nuclear bomb. Why should we be afraid of the Soviets?
I support our current airlift and hope that it leads to an agreeable conclusion.
We need to pull back from West Berlin and maintain a more realistic defense perimeter. We're more likely to be drawn into World War III than to gain anything useful from the defense of that exclave.
Harry Truman is an ineffectual, vacillating, highly unpopular President. We need to hammer on this theme and remind the American people why they need a new leader in the White House.

I will talk about what I have accomplished in New York -- public works, a balanced budget, anti-discrimination laws, business creation, and funding for teachers and universities. This is the future of our party.
I will put out the olive branch to our conservative friends and talk about the need for less spending, a limited foreign policy, and Communist influence in the government.

We're way ahead, so why screw up a good thing? I will talk in general about the future greatness of this country once I'm President, and avoid alienating any potential allies or partners in government.
We're going up the Eastern Seaboard, from Maryland all the way to Connecticut.
We're going to hit the Midwest, from Ohio to Wisconsin and Iowa.
I'm going through the Plains and Mountain states. I could personally talk to a third of the voters in that region, as sparsely populated as it is.
We're going to hit the West Coast, and especially California.

I believe that a Republican Congress, working with a Republican President, will be able to come to accord on the key issues of our time.

We'll barnstorm as much of the Midwest as we can, going from state to state.
I support the expansion of benefits, which were set at fairly low levels during the 1930s and have been eaten up by our recent inflation.
I support Social Security, but I think the program is most solvent in its current form.
I've never been comfortable with the Social Security program, and I would like to see it rolled back.
This is something that we badly need right now. We have a housing shortage in this country, and too many working-class Americans cannot afford a home.
I can't make a conclusive statement on this issue. I'm sure that between myself and Congress we can work out a good solution once I'm elected.
I'm not comfortable with committing the federal government to the area of home construction, especially with all of the other responsibilities it has taken on over the past two decades.
I support universal health care coverage in this country, financed by the federal government.
I think there are definitely programs that the federal government can get involved in to improve public health, but I also support our current system of private care and insurance.
With a country that is getting more and more prosperous by the day, I'm sure that we can find a good solution in the area of health care.
We should not have the federal government involving itself in the health care business. Private enterprise has built an outstanding health care system and will continue to do so in the future.
I absolutely believe that the federal government should be providing funds, to the states of course, for them to apply to education spending on our country's youth.
This is something that we will research and consider seriously over the next four years. I'd have to see the details of any proposal before I could give my opinion.
I'm opposed to the provision of federal funds for primary education. It will inevitably lead to other forms of interference in what should be a state and local matter.
We are the only thing standing between the world and global domination by the Soviets. I'm prepared to take any measure to prevent the advance of Communism.

I support this kind of thing in limited cases where there is a clear threat. But I'm worried about some of the ill-defined, open ended commitments we are getting ourselves into with other countries, and with the United Nations.
This is a drain on American finances for a cause that threatens to entangle us in future wars, not of our making. I oppose the actions we have taken.
I support this Amendment as a necessary step towards the political health of this nation. We need to, periodically,  have a fresh point of view in government. Ours is not an imperial nation.
I believe strongly in the two-term precedent, but I don't believe it should be enforced by Constitutional Amendment.
I don't have a strong stance on this Amendment. I support the popular will of the people on this issue.
There should not be a limit on how many terms a President can serve. This is why we have an election every four years -- to gauge the will of the American people.
I support the Marshall Plan and believe that it is a force for the future peace and prosperity of our world.
Obviously, Europe needs some kind of aid after the horrors of World War II. I will be careful to see that this plan is fairly administered and does not become excessive.
The Marshall Plan is a waste of resources, and will slow the development of Europe by forcing nations to rely on foreign subsidies, rather than rebuilding their own economies.
The Marshall Plan is provocative towards the Soviet Union, and is likely to lead to further aggression and escalation from them.
The HUAC is a necessary defender of American values, and I don't see anything to criticize in its current conduct.
The HUAC is not something I plan to address very much as I campaign.
I'm not very comfortable with the activities of this committee, and I believe they should be scaled back to a minimum.

Corporations have been raising prices much faster than wages have increased, and they are pocketing exorbitant profits as a result. I will fight for the rights of labor, and for better regulation during my next term.

We have already passed the Taft-Hartley Act and a modernized system of price supports for food, and their effect can clearly be seen in the drop in inflation since 1947. I'm confident this trend will continue.

We need to control the spending and interference of the federal government, and reinforce our commitment to a sound American dollar. These policies will bring inflation under control in my Administration.
We need a federal housing bill that will produce low-income housing and provide cheaper mortgages for all Americans, so that we can get more housing built in this country.
We are clearly overcrowding our urban areas at the moment. At the very least, we can expand the federal highway system to make more areas accessible to families and developers.

It has taken a couple of years after the end of the war, but I can already see that many new houses are being built by private developers to resolve this shortage, and I can only predict that this trend will continue without any special action by the government.
I support this aid and think it is a necessary step to combat the Soviet Union.
I support this aid, but I think we could have been more careful about the cost.
I do not support this action that we have taken.

Part of our current economic problem is the inability of Congress to pass programs which would help the American worker. I'd rather see us have more housing, more roads, and better health care than to see us with an unnecessary surplus.
I've always been an advocate of “pay-as-you-go liberalism”, as I've put it. I believe that we can pass the programs this country needs without destroying the fiscal health of the government.
We've run up quite a national debt over the past few years, and rightly so, but now that World War II is over, we should focus on paying down this debt.
John Bricker is a great man who represents my views for the future of this country. Now let's get going with this campaign.

description.source: What themes will you emphasize as you accept the Republican nomination and begin your campaign?
In making appointments to your campaign (and by implication, when you are President), will you favor traditional Republicans, Progressives, or try for an even balance?
What position will you take in regards to the war in Europe as you campaign?
What motivated you to support the candidacy of Elmer Haskett for Vice President, as strongly as you did?
Do you have any statements to make about the Federal Reserve Act, which established the Federal Reserve in 1913?
What will your position be on the women's suffrage question as your campaign this fall?
Woodrow Wilson has recently pushed through the Adamson Act to avert a railroad strike, which establishes an eight-hour day for railroad employees. Will you attack this action in your campaign?
Theodore Roosevelt is hitting the campaign trail hard this fall. However, he continues to make bellicose speeches about the war in Europe. Will you distance yourself from his rhetoric?
How much will you emphasize your own reform efforts as Governor of New York, as you campaign nationally?
California, an important state this fall, is in the midst of a divisive split between Progressives and traditional Republicans. What are your own plans for visiting that state?
Do you support the Clayton Antitrust Act which was recently passed? Do you believe that unions should be exempted from the antitrust regulations?
Do you have a position to take on the calls for the prohibition of alcohol as you campaign this fall?
What do you make of Woodrow Wilson's response to the raids and outrages of Pancho Villa?
Do you have any plans to attack the nomination of Louis Brandeis to the Supreme Court?
What are your opinions on child labor legislation, as exemplified by the recent Keating-Owens child labor bill?
Do you plan to attack Woodrow Wilson's stance on preparedness and war with Europe, and if so, how?
Do you support the level of preparedness established by the recent National Defense Act?
Do you have any statements to make on the tariff question, and/or the recently established Tariff Commission, as you campaign?
Do you plan to support the Jones Act -- granting greater autonomy to the Philippines along with a plan to grant independence.
Do you support the broader establishment of workers' compensation programs and laws, at the federal level?
Do you have any statements to make about the Easter Rebellion which transpired earlier this year in Ireland?
Do you support the temporary curtailment of American shipping in the Atlantic, in order to reduce the chances of German submarine attacks and the resulting consequences?
Are you willing to meet with German-American and Irish-American political leaders to discuss your beliefs, regardless of your feelings towards their organizations?
Do you support the recently ratified 17th Amendment, requiring the direct election of U.S. Senators?
Where will you travel to during your final days before the election?
I encourage every state to expand the suffrage to women as soon as possible.
I support the passage of a Constitutional amendment protecting the right of women to vote.
My record as Governor of New York shows that I am willing to enact progressive reforms, and to combat machine politics. I will bring this mentality to the national stage as President.
Mr. Wilson has veered between ineptness on the one hand, and sudden, radical solutions on the other. I am the safe, pragmatic alternative in this contest.
We can all agree on the need for reform, in this day in age. The question is, will we have sensible, moderate change or naked overreach?

We've seen alarming measures during Wilson's first term. I stand firmly opposed to the income tax, the new interference with business, and the reduction in tariffs which will undermine our prosperity.

Mr. Wilson's vacillations on the issue have emboldened potential adversaries and led to unfortunate events like the sinking of the Lusitania. A more resolute policy would actually increase the chances for peace.
As President, I have no desire for war. However, I will spare no effort to protect the legitimate rights of American shipping and commerce.
If Mr. Wilson continues to allow American ships to travel in dangerous areas, it is only a matter of time before we are drawn into war. His claims to be the peace candidate ring hollow.
Wilson has repeatedly taken half-measures, when we should be doing much more to prepare for the threat of war.
I refuse to politicize the security of the United States. Wilson and I are both in support of the current measures.
Preparedness is a bellicose policy which leads us closer to the very thing we are preparing against -- war, that is.
If we must make a decision, we should appeal to the progressive element of the party. These voters are the most likely ones to bolt for Wilson this fall.
I'm a moderate candidate, and my purpose is to tie the different strands of our party into a unified whole. My appointments will reflect this.
The great mass of voters in this country are Republicans. If we keep the mainstream elements of the party happy, they will deliver us a victory in November.
I believe the appointment of Louis Brandeis to the Court shows exceptionally poor, and dangerous, judgment on the part of Woodrow Wilson.
We would be better served to focus on other issues as we campaign.
I have a substantial record of reform and progressivism as Governor of New York, and as a Supreme Court Justice. I won't hesitate to say so as I campaign.
My history as Governor of New York shows that I can balance the need for reform with respect for established institutions.
Obviously it is helpful to remind the voters of my achievements, but our primary focus should be on Woodrow Wilson and the issues of 1916.
We will plan our own visit to that state, and call upon the Governor and his opponents equally, to avoid giving offense.
It's best not to wade into the middle of a controversy -- we should not make any large trip to California during this campaign.
The Governor of California can barely be called a Republican. We will coordinate our itinerary with the established party apparatus on our visit.
I would actually redouble the points that Roosevelt is making about our lack of military preparation.
I'm not going to comment on the speeches of Teddy Roosevelt -- there is too much to lose in antagonizing him.
I will emphasize that I am my own man, and that I believe the one-sided neutrality of Woodrow Wilson is at risk of pushing us into a war with Germany.
Wilson's impetuous actions in pushing this into law, with no chance for debate in Congress, are incorrect and dangerous.
We all have different opinions about the Adamson Act, and I don't propose to make it a big part of my campaign speech.
Wilson and I may have our differences on other issues, but I believe an eight-hour workday is broadly popular and worthy of praise.
Mexico has been in turmoil for years, and anyone with foresight could have anticipated the problems that have arisen from our undefended border. Wilson did not.
Every good American should support our current expedition into Mexico, to apprehend the villainous Pancho Villa.
Rather than directly imposing ourselves on Mexican territory, we should be seeking other ways to assist the rightful government in securing that country.
In defiance of the popular will, the Democrats immediately slashed tariffs and created an income tax upon their rise to power. We propose to undo these actions.
We would prefer for tariffs to be higher, but the creation of a Tariff Commission is certainly a sensible step in the right direction.
I don't believe the tariff issue would resonate in our current campaign. I will focus on other issues as I speak to the voters.
Republicans have stood behind such legislation all along. It would have become law years ago without the obstruction of Southern Democrats.
I oppose child labor and believe the states should pass laws against the practice, as New York did while I was Governor. But it is not a matter for the federal government to interfere in.
This recent act is not something that I plan to address very much as I campaign.
In this case, I desired to emphasize my commitment to reform, and to introduce new blood into the national office of Vice President.
I believe that Burkett appeals to the voters of the West, and will help us win those states back to the Republican fold.
I would prefer that the measure grant immediate independence, but I can support it in its current form.
This is a necessary step forward in the self-determination of the Philippines.
This measure is premature at the present time. We have added greatly to the welfare of the Philippines and should not leave before our work is done.
This Amendment is a necessary reform in the functioning of our government, and removes a significant avenue of corruption from our electoral process.
Regardless of personal feelings, this Amendment obviously went through a stringent ratification process and reflects the overwhelming majority of the people.
I believe that Senators should be elected by the legislature of each state, in line with the original Constitution.
What we've done so far is a good start, but we're still far from prepared to meet the type of emergency which might arise.
We've taken moderate, sensible steps thus far. I support the mobilization of additional troops, along with other policies designed to maintain peace and deter aggression.
If we're so bent on avoiding war, why are we expanding the Army and contracting for new weapons?
We should be calling on Great Britain to treat the perpetrators of this uprising with leniency, and to consider the relationship it has with Ireland.
This isn't an issue that our campaign plans to address. It would be unwise to antagonize Great Britain at this crucial juncture.
The Irish uprising is a domestic issue of Great Britain and should not be the concern of any patriotic American.
I don't plan to address women's suffrage in this campaign. There are more important issues at hand.
I stand opposed to the expansion of women's suffrage.
I believe that the prohibition of alcohol would be a positive benefit for our country.
It would not be wise, at this point, to make any statements supporting or opposing prohibition in our campaign. There are too many people on both sides of this issue.
We reject any call for the prohibition of alcohol, and I would not support such laws as President.
I support the Federal Reserve in general, but I believe that we should have established a more centralized, federal government bank.
Before this act, our country caromed from one financial panic to the next. The Federal Reserve is a tremendous step forward.
The Federal Reserve idea is worthy of support, but I would prefer that private banks were given a larger role in its operation.
I believe the Federal Reserve was an unnecessary and destabilizing change to the nation's banking system.
I support the Clayton Antitrust Act and would hope to see further measures enacted to protect the rights of labor in this country.
I don't plan to give this act more than cursory mention as I campaign. There are better issues to focus on.
I don't believe that we should have one set of laws for business, and another for unions. This act is another example of federal overreach.
I can think of no better way to reinforce my commitment to peace and neutrality than to meet with such groups.
During my career, I have met with any number of individuals whom I have disagreed with. I don't see a need to apply a different standard to this situation.
I refuse to meet with any hyphenated-American group which places another identity above that of American.
I support a federal workers' compensation program which all dangerous industries would be required to participate in.
I do support the effort this year to establish workers' compensation for federal employees.
This is not a measure that I support.
If we are serious about avoiding entanglement in a European war, then we should not allow merchants to put American lives at risk of attack in known war zones.
It makes perfect sense to warn Americans of the dangers involved in such commerce, but it is not the place of the government to actively interfere in it.
We have certain rights as a neutral power, and to retreat from those rights would only serve to invite further aggression.
Let's make a final swing to the West Coast, and California in particular, before the voting begins.
Let's focus on the Midwest.
Let's focus on New England.
I would make our final campaign stops in New York.
